News.title: ‘Savile of the nursery’ paedo childcare worker Vincent Chan abused my boy… he’s still haunted by sicko in his nightmares
News.content:
Next

SARAH and Graham’s five-year-old son has just started his first term at ‘big school’.

But what should be an exciting and fun time has been plagued by distressing night terrors, bouts of anxiety and a string of gruelling appointments with psychiatrists, occupational therapists and social workers.



Their traumatised little boy, who must remain anonymous, is among the victims preyed upon by one of Britain’s most prolific sex offenders.

And now it has emerged that twisted paedophile Vincent Chan, who hoarded tens of thousands of horrifying images of child abuse, was allowed to carry out his reign of terror in plain sight – like Jimmy Savile.

BBC bosses turned a blind eye to Savile’s predatory behaviour for years, and furious parents say Bright Horizons nurseries did the same.



Chan is now behind bars but astonishingly he had been cleared by another safeguarding investigation three years before he was arrested for his sickening crimes.

Bright Horizons nursery in north London simply dismissed allegations about Chan’s vile behaviour and allowed the monster to carry on working with babies and toddlers.

The chilling revelation that Camden Council and nursery bosses were aware of concerns about Chan long before his arrest has devastated parents who now know there were missed opportunities to stop him.

In February, after he admitted 56 charges of child sex offences, including sexual assault by penetration, possession of indecent images and voyeurism, Chan was sentenced to 18 years in jail.

He had been routinely filming himself sexually abusing tots in his care.



After his conviction, prosecutors described Chan as a “prolific sexual predator”.

The anguished parents of his young victims have joined forces and are demanding to know how on earth he was allowed to continue in his job for so long.

While Graham and Sarah* will never know for sure exactly what their son endured, they believe he was subjected to cruel physical and verbal abuse, and witnessed sexual assaults on other children too.

Graham said: “We’re upset. It’s crazy to learn that there were missed opportunities to stop this predator who has affected hundreds of families, like the Savile of nurseries.

“Our son has just started school and he’s still very up and down, he has nightmares, doesn’t like raised voices, is anxious and wary of strangers. He won’t go near men he doesn’t know.



“He has distressing moments which we know are related to the time he spent with Chan because of things he has said in the past.

“He’s been left traumatised having been in an abusive environment for an extended period of time. We know he was made to hit other children by Chan.

“We don’t know how much he would have witnessed of the sexual abuse Chan inflicted on the girls.



“He should be enjoying life, it’s incredibly unfair.”

Parents have contacted the police, but cops are unable to investigate health and safety offences unless somebody dies and it becomes corporate manslaughter – until then it is a matter for the local council.

Graham added: “The fact that Chan was taken off duty in 2021 then someone made the decision to put him back in the room has raised serious concerns.

“The police say it would have had to get to the stage where he actually killed one of the kids before they could do anything.

“Otherwise it falls under the local authority and they are avoiding giving us answers.”



The couple have joined a group of families who have hired a barrister to demand answers from Camden Council – which has repeatedly delayed revealing the findings of their review into this case.

Nor will they reveal details of the earlier investigation, carried out by Chan’s bosses at Bright Horizons and overseen by Camden Council, which followed ‘significant concerns’ raised with the nursery back in 2021 about Chan’s conduct and behaviour by the parent of a young girl.

Chan was temporarily put on duties that involved no contact with children while the investigation took place.



But after it was completed, Chan was cleared to return to his role caring for young children.

Just a year later, in 2022, Chan was filming himself sexually abusing three-year-old girls at the nursery, which is now permanently closed.

It has since emerged that Chan had also committed sexual offences in his previous job as a teaching assistant at St Mary’s Church of England primary school in north London, including upskirting female pupils.

Graham added: “We are friends with the parents of little girls who were actually molested by Chan, they cry everyday, and I don’t think you can ever recover from that, it’s a life sentence.

“We all just want basic questions answered – what happened and who knew?



“If there is nothing to hide, why not just give us the outcome of their report?

“It’s incredibly simple stuff we’re asking for.”

London’s newest MP Sagal Abdi-Wali, who won Sir Keir Starmer’s former seat last week, was leader of Camden Council when Chan was filming himself sexually abusing children.



Before her the leader was Georgia Gould, who is now a Government Schools Minister.

Graham added: “Both of these women have been promoted to a position of trust, but they did nothing while this scandal took place and while families were waiting for answers – that’s a pretty horrifying thought.

“We’re about to get our third council leader since Chan was convicted. Surely our children are the most important people to protect.”

In 2022 Bright Horizons in Edinburgh was fined £800,000 after admitting health and safety failings when a ten-month-old baby, Fox Goulding, choked to death on a piece of mango.

After that trial, Bright Horizons took the extraordinary decision to remove the CCTV in all its nurseries across the UK.



In June Ofsted served a Welfare Requirements Notice on the chain, meaning they had to investigate all safeguarding and welfare failures by 1 August.

But during that time the Bright Horizons managing director Philip Smith took a lengthy holiday and was then promoted to oversee hundreds more nurseries across Europe.

Afterwards the Ofsted report stated: “Inspectors identified breaches of requirements at 39 settings, including significant weaknesses in safeguarding, leadership and governance.”

Graham added: “It’s shocking that there has not been a leadership change. They are protecting themselves.”



Chan worked at Bright Horizons from 2017 to 2024. He was suspended after seven years in his role after a colleague raised concerns when he filmed a child falling asleep and shared it to “entertain” them.

Police found Chan had more than 25,000 indecent images of children on his computer, including videos of himself sexually assaulting children at the nursery while they were sleeping at nap time.

The youngest child he indecently filmed was only six months old.

After Chan’s sexual offending came to light, Camden Council ordered a review of the decision to clear him to return to work.

And while the review concluded in November 2025, the findings are not expected to be published until early 2027, and have been pushed back repeatedly.



Sarah added: “We’re very, very angry. We want Bright Horizons to be held accountable.

“How can a paedophile be allowed to run around a nursery for seven years without consequence?

“We want Ofsted to have a strong digital device policy, so nurseries ensure you can’t take photos and share with other devices, and they’re checked, and we’d like an independent body for parents and caregivers to report and escalate issues, who then have the power to investigate and monitor nurseries.

“Also, no lone working in larger settings, and mandatory CCTV.

“I feel deeply committed to making sure something changes.”



A Camden Council spokesperson said: “We know the parents of the children who attended the nursery, and the wider public, will be concerned that a complaint was made about Vincent Chan to Bright Horizons in 2021 – and will want to know how this was responded to.

“In 2021, Camden Council’s Local Authority Designated Officer (LADO) provided advice to Bright Horizons, after Bright Horizons informed them (the LADO) of a complaint.

“We have shared all relevant documents and information with the independent review team. We want families to get the answers they deserve, in full, through the outcome of the independent review.

“We are ready to receive the review’s recommendations once it is published and take action.

“In the meantime, we are committed to making continual improvements to safeguarding. We are determined to make a real and tangible impact on national safeguarding arrangements for the future.”



Brighton Horizons have been contacted for comment.

News.title: ‘Magical’ UK pumpkin festival that attracts over 20,000 a year is suddenly AXED after a decade
News.content:
Next

A HUGE pumpkin festival has been cancelled for 2026 – because it became too popular.

The event welcomed thousands of visitors each year and was a hit with families and locals.

The Dalston Pumpkin Lantern Festival in east London has been scrapped this year after over 70 per cent of England was affected by drought.



More than 20,000 visitors flocked to the festival, held at the Eastern Curve Garden, last year, causing long queues and complaints that local residents were unable to attend.



“Taking a year off from the festival has not been an easy decision,” the organisers said.

Each October for 15 years, the Hackney community flocks to the site to carve hundreds of pumpkins, which are then displayed in the garden to create a magical glowing spectacle in the nights leading up to Halloween.

But in 2025, the large crowds included groups of adults who hadn’t been involved in the pumpkin carving, leaving children and families unable to get in, the organisers said.

“At times it no longer felt like the magical experience that our team of staff and dedicated volunteers work so hard to create,” they added.

But there are plenty of other pumpkin patches that Halloween fans can check out in and around London this year.

The London Pumpkin Patch in Parsons Green features a Trick-or-Treat Lane, live performers and an enchanted woodland, while Hobbledown Heath in Hounslow boasts jaw-dropping fire performances, marshmallow roasting and dodgems in the dark.

And east London’s favourite festival isn’t gone for good.



“Rest assured, Dalston Pumpkin Lantern Festival will be back next year, and between now and then, we will be exploring ways to make sure that it’s full of the community atmosphere that we all value so much,” the organisers added.

News.title: Horrifying moment Russian suicide bomb explodes in apartment behind man as he films video in Ukraine
News.content:
Next

THIS is the horrifying moment a Russian suicide bomb blasts into a man’s apartment.

Shocking footage shows his flat lighting up bright orange as the drone smashes into the building in Kharkiv, Ukraine.



Before the strike, an air raid siren can be heard blaring out as the Brazilian man talks to the camera.

Lucas Candido, who volunteers in Ukraine, says in Portuguese: “Soon it will explode. I hope it’s not in my building.”





Just moments before the drone crashes into his apartment, he says: “The problem here is that you don’t know if you’re going to die.”

Then the room explodes into light and his camera is sent flying.

Suddenly the video goes dark.

More footage shows the aftermath of the terrifying drone attack.



A smoking mess can be seen outside his flat, and inside furniture is smashed, with broken glass littering the ground.

The Brazilian volunteer shared the video on Instagram, calling it “one of the hardest moments I’ve ever experienced in the war”.

He wrote: “The video shows only a few seconds, but those who have been there know the weight of this experience.”



After the attack, he said in the video: “They caught us by surprise. Thank God it didn’t have a very serious side effect.

“They caught some colleagues. Almost all of them are injured.

“My leg is injured. But I’m fine, thank God. My friends are fine too, thank God. Unfortunately, Russia is like this, Russia is a coward.

“They caught us by surprise.”

It comes after heart-stopping footage emerged showing a man miraculously escaping death as a Russian drone strike decimates a playground.



Shocking footage showed the civilian as he ran away from the UAV, just moments before it erupted into a huge fireball.

In the jaw-dropping clip, a man could be seen turning and sprinting away as he sees a drone racing towards him.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Just seconds later, the suicide device obliterates a section of the playground in Sviatopetrivske, near Kyiv, sparking a towering inferno.

Recorded last week, the footage comes amid an intensified period of Russian strikes on Ukrainian cities.

News.title: His killer is jailed – but is Tupac ALIVE? All the ‘proof’ that has many fans convinced…& why number 7 is key to mystery
News.content:
Next

For almost 30 years, the murder of rap superstar Tupac Shakur went unsolved.

This week, former gang boss Duane “Keefe D” Davis was jailed for 40 years for orchestrating the 1996 killing, apparently answering one of music’s greatest mysteries. Or does it?



A hardcore group of fans continues to question whether Tupac is dead. Instead, ‘Tupac truthers’ insist he faked his death.

Theories place him everywhere from Cuba to Somalia, while clues to his fate supposedly pepper his music.



Numerical codes associated with the rapper are also said to hold the key.

Even those who accept that he died believe there is more to his death than the official account.

Read more features CRUEL WAIT Tragic twist in Ten Pound Pom 'murder' case over abduction of missing girl, 3

A Knight’s tale

Death Row Records boss Suge Knight was driving the BMW Tupac was travelling in when the rapper was gunned down in a Las Vegas drive-by shooting. Tupac was hit four times and died in hospital six days later, aged 25. Knight was also wounded.

In an April 2012 radio interview, Knight suggested that Tupac had faked his death.

“Maybe the question is … Pac’s not really dead … Pac’s somewhere else,” he said.

He claimed nobody had seen Tupac’s body after his death and that he had paid a mysterious crematorium worker $3million to dispose of it, after which the man vanished.



Knight later offered a different explanation, claiming Tupac’s mother had demanded an immediate cremation and that he had paid a fortune to persuade a reluctant worker to carry it out.



In a 2017 interview from prison, Knight, convicted of voluntary manslaughter after running over and killing a businessman in January 2015, doubled down on his theory.

Asked whether Tupac might still be alive, Knight replied: “With Pac, you never know.”

In October 2018, Suge’s son, Suge Jacob Knight Jr, posted claims on Instagram that “Tupac is alive” and “He never really left us”, and that the rapper was living in Malaysia.

Suge Jr shared digitally manipulated photographs placing Tupac with Beyoncé and 50 Cent. He suggested the Illuminati were pursuing him for revealing too much. He later backed down on the theories.

Clues and codes

Truthers believe Tupac lore is full of clues. He was shot on September 7 and died on the seventh calendar day, counting the day of the shooting.



His posthumous album, released under the name Makaveli, was titled The Don Killuminati: The 7 Day Theory.

The album cover portrayed him crucified like Jesus, while its artwork carried the mysterious message: “Exit 2Pac, Enter Makaveli.”

The name was inspired by Italian political thinker Niccolò Machiavelli, whose writings Tupac studied. One theory attributed to Machiavelli advocates faking death to confuse enemies.

Fans have also seized on the reported time of his death, 4.03pm, whose digits add up to seven. He was also 25 when he died. Two plus five? Seven again. Spooky!

On the track Blasphemy, a sampled religious broadcast speaks of Christ returning within seven days. On another track, Hold Ya Head, fans say Tupac can be heard declaring: “I’m alive.”



On an earlier track, Ain’t Hard 2 Find, Tupac rapped about rumours of his death, photographs of his body and his grieving mother, apparently predicting his fate.

And in the video for I Ain’t Mad at Cha, filmed before his death, Tupac is shot, goes to heaven and returns, while the video for Smile, released after his murder, depicts a Tupac lookalike being crucified and resurrected.

The sightings

Since his death, Tupac has been a busy boy, if you believe the sightings.



Five years after his murder, rumours started to surface that Tupac had been spotted in New York, where he was born.

Then, in 2004, a video emerged purporting to show Tupac in Cuba. Truthers pointed to the fact that Tupac’s godmother, Assata Shakur, a former Black Liberation Army activist, had fled to the island after being convicted of murdering a New Jersey state trooper.

In 2009, celebrity website TMZ published photographs of ‘Tupac’ in a New Orleans bar. “We were unable to get any sort of DNA evidence – but this photo is good enough for us. Thug life,” the website said.



That same year, a video was posted on YouTube which purportedly showed the dead rapper at a Lil Wayne concert. A year later, rapper Waka Flocka Flame met him at a New Jersey hip-hop festival.

He was back in New York in 2011, wearing a bright yellow poncho at an Occupy Wall Street protest.

Sightings in Sweden and Los Angeles followed in 2012. Even Kim Kardashian joined the Pac hunt that year, posting a photograph of a man resembling the rapper on Instagram, asking: “Hmmm Tupac is alive and working?!?”

On March 6, 2014, another Tupac sighting was reported at a Boston Celtics basketball game at TD Garden. The resemblance was so striking that fans started chanting Tupac’s name, and the moment was featured on the arena’s Jumbotron.



That same year, one of the most unlikely Tupac sightings occurred at the BET Awards at the Nokia Theatre in Los Angeles. The startling picture was posted on Instagram by Snoop Dogg, with the caption “Who PAC?”

Then, in 2018, a man in Somalia named Suldaan Mehdi went online claiming to have seen Tupac in a car with fellow rapper Yaki Kadafi, who was also killed in 1996.



The theory gained credence among believers because a year earlier, a figure resembling Tupac had appeared in a video by the rap group Outlawz, which Tupac founded in 1995.

Members of the group were said to have been with Tupac when he was in hospital before he died.

Public enemy?

Tupac had strong political ideals and was seen by some in the establishment as a dangerous provocateur.

His mother, Afeni Shakur, belonged to the revolutionary Black Panther Party, which challenged racism and police brutality in America. While pregnant with Tupac in 1971, she stood trial alongside other activists accused of plotting bomb attacks in New York. They were acquitted.

Tupac grew up surrounded by radical politics and became an outspoken critic of the authorities.



Some Tupac truthers suggested the US government feared he could become a powerful political leader and wanted him silenced.

Former LAPD detective Greg Kading, who investigated the killing, told The Sun that theories about Tupac’s death included claims that the CIA wanted the rapper dead because he might lead a new Black Power movement.

The protection racket

Documents examined by The Sun reveal that Tupac was named in an FBI investigation into allegations involving a militant group. The case was opened on October 17, 1996, just over a month after Tupac’s death.

At the time, the FBI began probing allegations that people associated with the militant Jewish Defence League were involved in an extortion racket targeting music stars.

According to an informant, the group ran a protection racket in which victims received death threats before being offered expensive security, with payments reportedly running to $50,000.



The documents alleged that rapper Eazy-E had been targeted before his death from AIDS in 1995 and that Tupac had also been approached. The FBI sought to corroborate the allegations, but the available documents do not establish that the racket was responsible for Tupac’s murder.

Diddy or didn’t he?

One of the most enduring theories surrounding Tupac’s death focuses on the bitter rivalry between Tupac’s record label, Death Row Records, and Sean “Diddy” Combs’s Bad Boy Records.

Convicted killer Duane Davis made allegations involving Combs and New York underworld figure Eric “Zip” Martin during recorded police interviews in 2008, transcripts of which have been seen by The Sun.



In the interviews, Davis claimed Zip supplied the murder weapon and alleged that Combs reacted enthusiastically when told about the killing.

Combs, 56, denies any involvement and has never been charged in connection with Tupac’s death.

In July 2025, Combs was convicted of two counts of transporting people for prostitution but acquitted of the more serious sex-trafficking and racketeering charges. He was sentenced in October 2025 and is serving a 50-month federal prison sentence.

Ultimately, prosecutors convinced a Las Vegas jury that Davis had orchestrated the drive-by shooting in revenge for the beating of his nephew, Orlando Anderson, by Tupac’s entourage a few hours before the killing.

Meanwhile, former LAPD detective Russell Poole advanced a separate theory that Suge Knight had orchestrated Tupac’s killing because the rapper was preparing to leave Death Row.



Poole believed the subsequent murder of rapper Biggie Smalls could have been designed to make both deaths appear part of the East Coast-West Coast rap feud.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Some fans believed Tupac confirmed the Knight theory at the beginning of Bomb First (My Second Reply), from his posthumous album, in which he can be heard whispering a message interpreted by some as “Suge shot me” and by others as “Shoulda shot me”.

News.title: Abu Dhabi royal found passed out on busy London street with barefoot child, 3, after cocaine binge
News.content:
Next

A MEMBER of the Abu Dhabi royal family was found passed out on a London street with a barefoot three-year-old after a cocaine binge.

Mahrah Al Nahyan was slumped against railings next to an unconscious man as the child played next to the busy road.



Members of the public stepped in to look after the youngster until police arrived but Al Nahyan remained unresponsive for another 30 minutes.

When she finally came to, she shouted out: “This is not a slaughterhouse, why do you care so much? Why are you so worried?”



Al Nahyan, 32, pleaded guilty to one charge of child neglect at Southwark Crown Court.

The court was told she has been undergoing drug addiction treatment at the Priory centre since the incident in June.

Al Nahyan is a member of the ruling royal family in Abu Dhabi – one of the richest and most powerful in the world – through marriage.

The family is thought to be worth more than £250 billion.

Video released by the CPS shows her lying on the pavement next to children’s toys, including a scooter and plane.

Rio Pahlavanpour, prosecuting, said a passerby “noticed the child was unattended, without shoes on the street with a scooter and seemed to be in close proximity to moving traffic”.



The court heard police attended and found drug paraphernalia in Al Nahyan’s bags but no illicit substances.

Stephen Vullo KC, defending, said she has since shown “significant remorse and resolve to overcome her addiction”.

He added: “She made a grave mistake that day and she knows it.”

Al Nahyan, who receives an £8,000 monthly allowance, was sentenced to a two-year community order with a rehabilitation requirement.

She was also fined her £5,000 plus £1,000 prosecution costs.



Mr Justice Johnson KC said: “By leaving [the child] to play barefoot in the street while under the influence of drugs, you showed a recklessness and disregard for [the child’s] safety.

“On one occasion they ran towards the road while chasing a piece of paper until a member of the public contained [the child].

“But for the intervention of strangers there was a serious risk they would be seriously injured or worse. They could have run away, become lost. They could have been taken or harmed by a stranger and could have become distressed seeing you and your friend unconscious in the street.”

News.title: Man killed in M5 crash after traffic slowed during ‘rolling road block’ to clear debris strewn across motorway
News.content:
CRASH TRAGEDY Man killed in M5 crash after traffic slowed during ‘rolling road block’ to clear debris strewn across motorway







Next

A MAN has died after two vehicles collided at the back of a “rolling road block” that had been put in place to clear debris on a major motorway.

Traffic was slowed on the M5 between junction 25 (Taunton) and junction 24 (Bridgwater South) in Somerset, on Tuesday at around 1.10pm.

The “rolling road block” was put in place due to debris on the northbound carriageway.

Cops said that the fatal two-vehicle collision happened soon afterwards at the rear of the queue, leading to the death of the man.





His family have been notified and our thoughts remain with them during this incredibly difficult time, said Avon and Somerset Police.

Cops said they are being offered the support of a specialist family liaison officer.

The motorway was closed in both directions during the initial emergency response and the southbound was opened within a few hours.

The northbound carriageway remained closed and diversions in place until around midnight, when it was reopened.

Avon and Somerset Police said the man’s family had been informed of his death and officers want to hear from any witnesses or drivers with dashcam footage.

The force said the work of the serious collision investigation team is important to ensure forensic evidence is gathered.

Photos and videos of the scene are also being secured in order to allow an in-depth investigation to take place.

“We would like to thank motorists for their patience and understanding,” the statement reads.



“If you were in the area and witnessed the collision, or have any dashcam footage which could help our enquiries, please call us.”

News.title: Paul Ferris’ cause of death revealed – days after notorious gang enforcer’s shock passing
News.content:
Next

PAUL Ferris’ cause of death has been revealed in official records.

His official death certificate reveals he passed away aged 62 at University Hospital Ayr at 9:10pm on Tuesday, October 6.



His occupation is described as author on the document certified by a medical practitioner three days after he lost his health battle.

The cause of deaths was assessed as “Multiple Organ Failure (Cardiovascular, Liver and Respiratory)” as well as “Decompensated alcoholic liver disease”.



Prior to his passing his liver was at a critical stage of alcohol-related cirrhosis where the liver can no longer function and can lead to death within weeks of diagnosis.

The details emerge as loved-ones prepare to say their final farewells to Ferris at Daldowie Crematorium on Monday.

'NO REMORSE' A CRIME expert who interviewed Paul Ferris has cast doubt whether he ever truly turned his back on the gangland world – and believes it could all have been a carefully constructed act. Professor David Wilson described his encounter with a “quietly spoken and thoughtful” man when he quizzed him about his past for a true-crime TV show. And the renowned criminologist revealed Ferris showed “no remorse” over a criminal past, leaving behind many questions that may never be answered. Ferris became a national figure following his 1992 acquittal for the murder of Arthur Thompson Jr, following a marathon trial at the High Court. 

The notorious former gangland enforcer Ferris made his name as he rose through the ranks to become a feared heavy for Godfather Arthur Thompson in the 1980s.

Ferris, nicknamed ‘The Wee Man’, died in hospital after having been admitted two days earlier.

After his death, a close family friend said: “News of his death will come as a shock to many who knew him throughout the different chapters of his life.



“Paul went straight for 25 years and wrote several best selling books.

“Our sincere condolences go to Paul’s family, friends and loved ones at this extremely difficult time.”

Ferris was controversially cleared of the murder of Thompson’s son – Arthur Jnr – in 1992 in the longest-running gangland trial in Scottish criminal history.

Ferris and Arthur Jnr – also known as ‘Fat Boy’ – had worked together but fell out after Ferris accused him of setting him up.

He became the prime suspect and was 28 at the time when he was charged with shooting Thompson dead in the city’s Blackhill area.



'TOTAL SHOCK' A GRIEVING friend of Paul Ferris told how the notorious hood’s sudden death had stunned Scotland’s underworld. Brian Anderson, 58, also revealed the former Glasgow enforcer and convicted gun-runner had never told him he regretted his criminal past. At the time of his death Ferris was working on a sequel to hit 2013 film The Wee Man. It was based on the first of his successful books about his mob experiences, The Ferris Conspiracy, published in 2001. The controversial figure was also set to launch a podcast. Photographer Brian snapped pictures of the gangland boss turned writer over 25 years and built a trusted relationship with him. Paying tribute, he said: “Paul was very articulate. He was very funny, cracking jokes a lot of the time. “But I remember him saying to me one time, when he looked in the mirror he would be frightened if he saw the person people thought he was.” 

He was filmed smirking on the steps outside court after being sensationally acquitted of the murder following the 54-day trial which included 300 witnesses and cost £4million.

He was later jailed for seven years in 1998 after being convicted of gun-running.

Ferris claimed to have turned his back on his former crime links for the past three decades, going on to become a writer.

A movie about his life, The Wee Man, was released in 2013, where Ferris was played by Line of Duty star Martin Compston.



Ferris’ death comes just over a year after his notorious killer brother Billy also passed away.

News.title: Child among six dead after horror plane crash near US state park
News.content:
Next

A CHILD is among six people killed after a small plane plunged into dense woodland in a horror crash.

All five adults and the youngster aboard the doomed aircraft were found dead as emergency crews raced to the wreckage.



Emergency responders rushed to the heavily wooded crash site, where they discovered the wreckage and confirmed all six people had died.

The rescue teams located the wrecked aircraft with “multiple individuals involved.”



Several neighbours had already began searching the area after seeing a low-flying plane.

Cops said: “As a result of the search, all six occupants of the aircraft were located deceased on scene.”

Investigators are now probing whether severe weather played a role in the tragedy after the plane reportedly made contact with air traffic control shortly before crashing.

The six-seater Piper aircraft came down at around 9.30pm on Tuesday near Mirror Lake State Park in Wisconsin.

It had taken off from Kenosha and was heading to Menomonie when disaster struck.

Despite the devastating impact, no other people, nearby homes or other properties were damaged.



Sauk County Sheriff’s Captain Matt Burch said: “Prior to the crash the aircraft was reported to be in contact with a nearby air traffic control tower.

“Investigators are working to learn what the content of those transmissions were and if a weather event in the area may have played any role in the crash.”

Authorities have yet to identify the victims as investigators work to establish what caused the fatal plunge.

Investigations are ongoing.
