Sports.title: Arsenal to cut jobs days after Mikel Arteta signs lucrative new contract
Sports.content:
Arsenal to cut jobs days after Mikel Arteta signs lucrative new contract

Arsenal are reportedly planning to cut 60 jobs as part of cost-cutting measures at the Emirates Stadium.

It comes just days after manager Mikel Arteta signed a new £25million-a-year contract.

3 Arsenal have informed staff they are set to cut 60 jobs Credit: Getty

His improved terms equate to an income of around £68,500-a-day.

The Spaniard has committed his future to the Gunners, with his deal now running until the summer of 2030.

Arteta's previous contract had been due to expire at the end of this season, with his salary also rising from £10million annually.

He had already been the Premier League's highest paid manager before being rewarded for ending the club's 22-year wait for a title.

Arsenal job cuts

However, Arsenal are now set for a round of redundancies a week on from handing their boss a new contract.

According to multiple reports, the club have informed staff they plan to cut 60 jobs in a bid to cut costs.

Employees were informed of the news by chief executive Richard Garlick on a call on Wednesday morning.

It is understood there are areas of the club which will not be affected by the redundancies.

Those include performance staff within both the men's and women's first-teams as well as the academy.

Instead, off-field areas will be targeted by the upcoming job cuts.

3 The Gunners will target areas off the pitch in a bid to cut costs Credit: Getty

The Arsenal Foundation, community positions and security department will also remain unaffected, though.

It is a move which comes after Arsenal reported losses for the seventh successive financial year.

The club's most recent financial reports, covering the 2024/25 season, included a significant rise in operating costs.

Figures increased from £148million in the previous campaign to £201million.

Those come despite the Gunners' improvement on the pitch under Arteta in recent seasons.

As well as their title triumph last term, Arsenal also reached their first Champions League final since 2006.

3 Arteta was handed a new £25million-a-year contract last week Credit: Getty

However, they were ultimately beaten on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain in May.

This season also marks their fourth successive campaign in the competition having returned under Arteta in 2023.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez transfer mooted after Manchester United outburst: ‘That’s his agenda’
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez may well be looking for a way out of Manchester United.

That's the view of former Liverpool and England midfielder Danny Murphy as he addressed the Argentine's post-match outburst.



3 Martinez's frustrations are understandable, according to McCoist Credit: Getty

Martinez took aim at sporting director Jason Wilcox during an interview on Tuesday night after the Red Devils' 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

The defender called out the lack of squad strengthening amid their five-match winless run.

talkSPORT understands his stance is shared by his fellow senior players at Old Trafford.



Why did Martinez criticise the United board?

Murphy believes there may be another motivation behind Martinez's outburst.

It comes after Rio Ferdinand argued players have previously been forced out of United for criticising the club's hierarchy.



The former Red Devils centre-back named Roy Keane and Cristiano Ronaldo as examples of those who found themselves in similar situations.

Reacting to Ferdinand's comments on White & Jordan, Murphy explained: "Martinez decides to say it. He’s saying that the repercussions are you’ll be gone, but that’s Martinez’s agenda.



"So he’d be happy with that. Especially if he gets weighed in, he’s got something in the pipeline, I’m sure.

"The reality is, it doesn’t matter what your view is, how big you are at the club and who you are, you can’t go against the hierarchy, the people who employ you, the people who pay your wages. You can’t."

Martinez, who joined United in 2022, is into the final year of his current contract.

However, the club holds an option to extend his deal by a further 12 months through to the end of next season.



It's also reported that Martinez pushed for a transfer to Atletico Madrid in the summer.

What did Martinez say?

In an interview with Amazon Prime moments after the final whistle, Martinez exclaimed: "It was really poor, really poor.

"I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it's a reflection of our club at the moment. We did it last season and now we expect more from the top.

"To bring more players, to compete. Other teams bring in many more players. I expect more from everyone… 100 per cent I expected more from our technical director.



"I have to be honest and also the players have to do more but it's just important when you make a strong squad for this type of night."

3 Martinez secretly wants to force a move out of United, says Murphy Credit: Getty

He added: "Last season we created a base to build an amazing team. It's annoying and disappointing to come here and I'm not seeing my team get an amazing result here."

talkSPORT verdict

Meanwhile, fellow ex-pro and talkSPORT host Ally McCoist insisted he understood Martinez's viewpoint but will never support a player for criticising their own club.



Speaking on Wednesday's Breakfast show, he was asked if he can see where Martinez was coming from.

McCoist replied: "I probably do to a certain degree. I’m not sure it’s his position to say it.

"He should concentrate on his own job, actually. He should be concentrating on not dropping (Dominic) Solanke for the equaliser at the weekend.

"To be honest, I didn’t hear the board having a go at him about that, but listen, he’s entitled to his opinion. So you’ve got to say, he probably does have a point.



"It’s not a good look. Straight away we’re talking about it, it’s the first thing we see when we come in, there’s another player not happy, there’s a bit of dissent within the camp.

3 Carrick's side are without a win in their last five matches in all competitions Credit: Getty

"I don’t really like players coming out and criticising the club or their own team-mates. I’m probably a little bit old school in that respect.

"I know there will be people out there that’ll think it’ll be refreshing, and what I will do, I’ll support his right to say it, but I don’t think it’s a good look."

Sports.title: Tiger Woods, 50, fuels talk of a comeback as he's seen in action in rare public appearance after horror DUI car crash
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods teased how he may look playing at Pebble Beach for next summer's US Open while putting on a driving range clinic at the famous golf resort.

Woods was filmed hitting balls at Monterey Peninsula Country Club, hinting that he may be close to a return to playing competitively again.

The 15-time major champion was in the area for a series of events at multiple courses - including the TW Invitational and the TGR Jr Invitational.

In between, he got some swings in as his TGR Live social media account posted a video with the caption: 'Back on your feed, right where this swing belongs.'

Woods also boosted spirits by hosting the match play finals of the youth event - even delivering introductions of 60 young players.

The golf legend has been seen hitting balls more frequently as of late, including posting a practice session from Liberty National in New Jersey last month.

Tiger Woods was spotted on the driving range again fueling rumors of a possible comeback

Woods was putting on a clinic while at Monterey Peninsula Country Club in Pebble Beach

Woods hasn't played competitively since 2024 amid health issues and a DUI arrest

In September, Woods pled no contest to the charges stemming from the DUI back in late March and struck a deal with prosecutors which will see the golfer banned from driving for five years.

After his arrest, Woods got permission from the court to fly to Switzerland – where he spent months in a rehabilitation facility.

The 50-year-old has not played in a professional golf tournament since the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon, where he missed the cut.

Woods changed his plea in a courtroom in early September, which allowed him to avoid the case going to trial.

According to police, Woods was driving at a high speed along a beachside road when his Land Rover clipped a tractor-trailer truck and rolled onto its side, causing about $5,000 worth of damage to the other vehicle.

He was able to crawl out of the car without any injuries before later admitting to officers he was looking at his phone and changing the radio at the time of the collision.

A Breathalyzer test did not reveal any alcohol in Woods’s system, but he refused a urine test, according to police.

The Sheriff’s report obtained by the Daily Mail said deputies found opioids in his pocket and he showed signs of impairment.

Woods previously broke the clubs out at Liberty National in New Jersey in September

Woods recently pled no contest to DUI charges and had his license suspended for five years

A previous hearing was held on August 4, following a July ruling that allowed prosecutors to obtain Woods' hospital records that were connected to the crash.

Martin County circuit court judge Darren Steele approved an agreement between the State Attorney's Office and Woods' legal team that allowed prosecutors to request records from the hospital that treated the PGA legend following his crash.

Back in May, Steele approved a similar agreement granting prosecutors access to Woods' prescription medication records from his Palm Beach pharmacy between January 1 and his March crash.

Prosecutors and Woods's attorney have agreed to a protective order that limits the release of any hospital or prescription records to the State Attorney's Office, law enforcement, state experts and the defense.

Woods was closing in on a return to golf and was widely expected to compete at The Masters in the days before the crash.

The 15-time major champion's legal problems have since been put into perspective by Vanessa's cancer diagnosis. She revealed her bout with an unspecified form of breast cancer back in May.

Woods changed his plea to no contest during a court hearing on September 2

Woods appeared puffy-eyed as he left the court alongside doting girlfriend Vanessa Trump

Vanessa led him back to a car after he had pleaded no contest and had his license suspended

The March crash marked the fourth major driving-related incident of Woods's adult life.

Five years earlier, when Woods rolled another SUV down a steep embankment in California, he did not face any accusations of driving under the influence. Instead, the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department claimed Woods was driving at around 80mph, nearly twice the legal limit, at the time of the crash.

Witnesses told TMZ that Woods appeared agitated and impatient while leaving a golf tournament parking lot in the moments before the crash.

Woods was never charged in 2021, but he wasn't so lucky in 2017, when he was found by Jupiter police about 15 miles from his home. Officers said they found him unconscious in his Mercedes-Benz, which was parked awkwardly on the roadside at around 3am.

Upon closer inspection, they noticed damage to his vehicle.

Woods didn't have any alcohol in his system, but later tests found the active ingredient for marijuana, two painkillers, Vicodin and Dilaudid, the sleep drug Ambien and the anti-anxiety drug Xanax.

Woods appeared puffy-faced as he arrived for his change-of-plea hearing in Florida

Vanessa was front and center inside the court as Woods pleaded no contest to reckless driving

Woods after his arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence (DUI) in Jupiter, Florida, on May 29, 2017. He later pleaded guilty to reckless driving

Woods changed his original not guilty plea in the wake of his DUI arrest back in March

Vanessa with him and her 19-year-old daughter Kai back in March

He later claimed he had been self-medicating for pain caused by his fourth back surgery and insomnia.

Woods did not specifically address the marijuana issue and he wasn't found with the drug in his possession.

Woods pleaded guilty to reckless driving and received a year of probation, a $250 fine and was ordered to undergo 50 hours of community service.

He was also banned from drinking alcohol during the probation.

In July 2017, Woods completed a private program to address his dependency on painkillers.

'I will continue to tackle this going forward with my doctors, family and friends,' he tweeted at the time. 'I am so very thankful for all of the support I've received.'

Woods stands alongside his lawyer to face County Judge Darren Steele on Wednesday

In April the Daily Mail broke the news that the golfer would leaving the country 'imminently'

The golf great flipped his Land Rover clean onto its side during his accident in Jupiter

Woods' most notorious car crash took place in 2009, when he rammed his Cadillac Escalade into a fire hydrant, tree and several hedges near his home.

He was treated for minor injuries and received a ticket for careless driving, but while he thanked his then-wife Elin Nordegren for getting him out of the car, there were lingering doubts about the story.

After all, it was only days earlier that the National Enquirer claimed he'd had an affair with Rachel Uchitel, a 9/11 widow and New York nightclub manager.

The alleged details of the November 27, 2009 crash were ultimately included in the best-selling biography by Jeff Benedict and Armen Keteyian, titled Tiger Woods.

Sports.title: Team-mates accuse British cycling's axed golden boy Matthew Richardson of having a 'God complex' - as his girlfriend ignores drama to win silver medal at the World Championships in his absence
Sports.content:
British cycling's golden boy Matthew Richardson has been accused of having a 'God complex' after being axed from the team following allegations of using racist language.

Richardson, 27, was sent home from the Cycling World Championships on Monday with the 'misconduct' probe over his behaviour still ongoing, while his 23-year-old cyclist girlfriend Emma Finucane remains at the competition in Shanghai and raced to a silver medal in the Women's Team Sprint on Wednesday morning.

Finucane put on a brave face, smiling with her team-mates Sophie Capewell and Rhianna Parris-Smith on the podium after losing gold to China.

Richardson has been accused of using racist and discriminatory language towards others and using the n-word, according to The Times, who also report that riders in the World Class Programme described him as 'arrogant' and having a 'God complex'.

'At the velodrome he’s the golden boy,' they added. 'Matty is one of their best chances of a gold medal in LA and he knows it.'

British Cycling began investigating Richardson after a formal complaint was made, it is understood.

The Olympic medallist broke his silence on Tuesday, writing on Instagram that he was 'deeply disappointed' and would co-operate with Team GB, who he joined after leaving the Australian programme.

Matthew Richardson (right) is not competing at the World Championships amid the ongoing misconduct probe but his girlfriend Emma Finucane (left) remains

Sophie Capewell (left), Finucane (centre) and Rhianna Parris-Smith are pictured with their silver medals on Wednesday after coming second in the Women's Team Pursuit

He said: 'I understand the seriousness of what has been raised in recent reports about my withdrawal from the 2026 UCI Track Cycling World Championships.

'British Cycling has said it looks into matters like this through its established procedures. I will co-operate fully with its processes. I assure everyone that I will do so properly, and appropriately and with contrition for the feelings of anyone who might be affected.

'Out of fairness to everyone involved, and on advice, like British Cycling, I will not be commenting further until any process is complete. I am deeply disappointed to miss the World Championships, and I wish the Great Britain team and every rider competing the very best.'

Richardson's exit sent shockwaves through the sport, while his girlfriend Finucane welcomed her parents to Shanghai ahead of the competition on Monday.

Her brother, Sean, 21, told the Daily Mail of his family's 'shock and surprise' at the latest development.

He said: ‘We are all pretty shocked and surprised - he’s a lovely guy. He’s been here a lot and never shown any signs of that sort of behaviour. My parents flew out to Shanghai yesterday - none of us knew.'

Emma, who won four gold medals at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, competes in the Individual Sprint, Team Sprint and Keirin. Ultimately it was China who took gold in the Team Sprint, with Finucane and Co settling for silver and Germany taking bronze on Wednesday.

In a statement sent to Daily Mail Sport, a British Cycling spokesman said: 'British Cycling can confirm that Matt Richardson has been withdrawn from the Great Britain Cycling Team squad for the upcoming 2026 Tissot UCI Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai, China.'

Richardson has been described as having a 'God complex' and being 'arrogant'

When approached by Daily Mail Sport about the misconduct allegations which are believed to have prompted Richardson's withdrawal, the organisation added that they would not be commenting further at this stage.

Richardson and Finucane live together in Manchester and have been dating since February 2024 after 'knowing each other for a long time'.

Richardson had been due to be one of four members of the men's sprint squad at the World Championships.

He had been due to join Harry Ledingham-Horn, Ed Lowe and Joe Truman in the squad.

Richardson had claimed three medals at the European Championships in Konya, Turkey, earlier this year.

The 27-year-old won gold in both the men's sprint and keirin events, as well as claiming silver in the team sprint with Truman and Hamish Turnbull.

Richardson had been due to make his comeback after he was injured during the Keirin World Series in July.

Richardson's partner is fellow British cyclist Emma Finucane, who welcomed her parents out in China amid the storm engulfing her boyfriend

Last week, Richardson said he is 'lucky' to be walking after being wiped out by a rival in an incident, which ruled him out of the Commonwealth Games three months ago.

Richardson had been slammed off the track by Japanese cyclist Kento Suzuki while competing in the event in July, leaving the velodrome in an ambulance.

The sprinter said he has not received an apology from Suzuki over the incident.

He was favourite to win gold in Glasgow but never got to take part after the horrifying crash. He was unable to walk for four days after coming away with a broken scapula and a heavily bruised hip.

Richardson had been hoping to defend the title he won when competing for Australia in 2022, before he switched nationality to represent Britain, which he claimed was like 'Hogwarts' compared to 'High School'.

The defector, who was born in the English town of Maidstone but moved to Perth at nine and went on to carve out a brilliant track career for Australia, caused a sensation by switching allegiance straight after winning two silvers and a bronze at the 2024 Paris Olympics. He received a life ban from competing for Australia.

Sports.title: Arsenal's missing piece! Champions' photoshoot mishap has fans questioning why they couldn't have waited another day for injured star William Saliba
Sports.content:
Arsenal are taking flak from fans after leaving William Saliba out of their annual squad photo.

The Gunners lined up 24 of their stars alongside Mikel Arteta and their Premier League and Community Shield trophies on a proud day at their London Colney training ground.

It is a photo which will be remembered for years and one they hope will mark a waypoint on their journey to multi-season dominance.

But they were scrambling to excuse themselves after taking the snap without their star centre-back.

Saliba, they explained, had a medical appointment and therefore had to be excluded.

The Frenchman is yet to play this season after suffering a back injury during the World Cup.

Arsenal are taking criticism after leaving William Saliba out of their squad photo... because of his medical appointment

Saliba pictured holding the Premier League trophy with Declan Rice during Arsenal's parade

Arsenal did not explain the nature of his medical appointment but he is building towards a return to the first-team.

Saliba, 25, has resumed individual training and while he has a way to go before he can play, Arteta is positive about his progress.

'It's over a week I think [he's been on the grass], obviously we're managing that load,' Arteta said.

'He's building now his capacity to good standards, and let's see in the next few weeks if we can start to introduce him to the team to see where we are to actually make him available for the squad.

'We're still talking about weeks, and when that happens, it's very different whether he would play just before or just after [the November international break] because it's a very specific injury, that the healing process I cannot tell you exactly how he's going to react to.'

Saliba played in 31 of Arsenal's title-winning games last season and made 50 appearances in all competitions as they reached the final of the Champions League for the first time since 2006, losing to Paris Saint-Germain.

Arsenal's supporters were less than impressed with the club's decision to take the photo without him.

'You could have just waited for Saliba to be back before doing this,' said one fan on X.

Another said: 'Why would you do this without Saliba? Surely he could’ve got his medical appointment moved, come on now!'

One said: 'So why not wait for Saliba to be back. This is very silly. Played a huge role to winning the Premier League. There is no pressure to post the picture.'

Somebody added: 'Please, reschedule another photoshoot because Saliba deserves to be in this picture.'

Another said: 'I am sorry this is very disrespectful to Saliba regardless of his medical appointment.'

So, what do you think? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

Sports.title: Man City punishment verdict 'expected early next year' - as Andy Burnham faces questions over 'freebies from Abu Dhabi deleted from public record'
Sports.content:
Man City appeal verdict 'expected early next year' - as Andy Burnham faces questions over 'freebies from Abu Dhabi deleted from public record'

Manchester City's appeal into their Premier League guilty verdict is expected to be heard by mid-January, according to the head of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR).

City were found guilty of all their alleged serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018 by an independent commission.

They were found to have made 'sham' agreements to manipulate their financial accounts to the tune of £900million over a nine-season period which saw them win eight trophies in the biggest cheating scandal in British sporting history.

The IFR could force owner Sheikh Mansour to sell the club, or bar any personnel from being owners or directors, once the appeal process is complete.

IFR chief David Kogan told Times Radio: 'The Premier League have said that they want to get this resolved within the season and actually, of course, it's not the Premier League, it's an independent commission that's going to hear this, made of three retired either judges or lawyers.

'My understanding is there is a prescribed process, which is 12 weeks, and so people are assuming this will actually be heard by the middle or the end of January. But as I say, it's not our process, it's that of the Premier League's independent commission. What I don't think we can do is take any judgment until we're quite clear.

Manchester City's appeal into their Premier League guilty verdict is expected to be heard by mid-January

Andy Burnham, then Greater Manchester mayor, pictured with Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak in 2019

'Obviously, City claim that they have some form of silver bullet to put off these charges and win the appeal, and we're not there to judge whether that's right or wrong yet, but I think we'll know in the early part of next year.'

Kogan threatened to resign from his role if there is any political interference in the IFR dealing with the saga.

The IFR was created in September 2025 and was given the task of protecting and promoting the sustainability of English football.

But Andy Burnham has had to defend himself after being accused of 'covering up' links to Manchester City following a register of interests being 'deleted'.

Kogan added: 'The prime minister is capable of saying whatever he wants to say. You asked me whether we have had any interference politically in any of the judgments we're making, and I'm telling you, categorically, we have not.

'We will take a judgment based on evidence, once the appeal has been heard by the independent commission of the Premier League, we're going to look at that evidence closely, we're going to actually have powers of investigation ourselves, and that will be what governs what we do.'

City could face expulsion from the Premier League, a fine, a points deduction, and even having their trophies stripped.

But Prime Minister Burnham came out in support of the crisis-stricken club's Abu Dhabi owners... before backtracking and vowing to release all material from his dealings with them.

Independent Football Regulator chief David Kogan says he will resign if there is any political interference

Mr Burnham previously claimed to have had just one formal meeting with City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

But he now stands accused of misleading the public after a deleted register of interest showed he joined Al Mubarak twice in a luxury box at City's Etihad Stadium, while he also accepted tickets to an Ed Sheeran concert, according to the BBC .

Mr Burnham accepted City-funded freebies worth nearly £1,200 which appeared on a register of interests that he signed in December 2020 during his time as Manchester mayor and was later taken down from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA)'s website, they report.

On April 18, 2020, the register shows a value of £699 given to 'dinner with the Chairman at Man City/ Man United derby at the Etihad.'

And later that year on August 17, the entry reads: 'Dinner with Richard Leese and Chair of Man City for the Everton match at the Etihad.' The match ticket value is given as £38, while the hospitality is listed at £300.

At PMQs on Wednesday afternoon, Mr Burnham was asked: 'Did anyone associated with the running of Manchester City raise the charges they were facing and have now been found guilty of, either with him or any member of his team?'

The Prime Minister replied: 'They did not raise those issues with me. I'm very happy for everything to be set out in full, it is why I asked the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, in response to a call from the leader of the opposition and others to set out a full statement of my key dealings with the owners of Manchester City Football Club.

'That statement was published on Monday and it includes the issues in the news today and that is the position.'

GMCA has not yet responded to Daily Mail Sport's request for comment. According to the BBC, it is the GMCA's policy to only publish entries from the current mayoral term.

On reacting to the deleted register of interests re-published on X, Reform UK's Robert Jenrick wrote: 'This saga stinks. Burnham appears to have concealed his extensive links to Man City's owners. Fans deserve better.'

The details of Mr Burnham's contacts with City during his time as mayor were released by GMCA on Monday.

They revealed the Prime Minister had a formal meeting with Al Mubarak at an investment summit in October 2021 while he was Greater Manchester mayor. He also chatted to Al Mubarak in the stands during a testimonial game in 2019 and was accompanied by City staff on official overseas visits to China and Japan.

But the deleted register of interests shows he was in a hospitality suite at the Etihad with Al Mubarak for a game against Everton and also the Manchester derby.

Burnham had previously said on The Rest is Politics podcast: 'I will quite clearly put out there everything that I have done working with them in my previous role as Mayor of Greater Manchester.

'None of it is recent, in terms of meetings I had. I only had one significant meeting and that was in 2021. That is right and I will put that all out there.'

The new revelation will only intensify scrutiny over the Prime Minister's relationship with City's Abu Dhabi owners, who maintain their innocence and are appealing the independent commission's verdict.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney's transfer request regret, Roy Keane's bust-up with Fergie and the interview that spelt the end for Cristiano Ronaldo - the warning signs for Lisandro Martinez after his Madrid meltdown
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney's transfer request regret, Roy Keane's bust-up with Fergie and the interview that spelt the end for Cristiano Ronaldo - the warning signs for Lisandro Martinez after his Madrid meltdown

As if things weren't bad enough for Michael Carrick after Man United were beaten by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday night, Lisandro Martinez plunged his beleaguered manager into further trouble with an astonishing post-match rant.

In it, the Argentine defender hit out at United's performance in Spain, insisted Carrick was 'doing his best', and accused the club's hierarchy of not backing the team enough.

'I expect more (investment) 100 per cent,' Martinez said. 'I expect more from our technical director. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.

'We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top; more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well. We created the base to create an amazing team. It is annoying and disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result.'

It remains to be seen if there are any ramifications for Martinez, but it all adds to the sense of crisis surrounding Old Trafford right now.

So, in light of Martinez's comments, Daily Mail Sport has taken a look at previous examples of United stars calling out the club – and what happened to them.

Lisandro Martinez called out Man United's hierarchy after their defeat by Atletico Madrid

The defeat in Spain heaped the pressure on under-fire Red Devils boss Michael Carrick

Jaap Stam – 2001

Jaap Stam was a key part of United's famous Treble-winning team in 1998-99, making his abrupt departure to Lazio in 2001 all the more shocking.

That came after the Dutch defender released an autobiography in August of that year, with some of the claims in it reportedly upsetting Sir Alex Ferguson.

Stam made statements about his views on opposition players and team-mates, while he alleged that Ferguson's approach to buy him in 1998 had been done without the permission of his former team PSV.

Ferguson was incensed and dropped Stam from his squad shortly before his departure, which at the time was put down to a generous offer from Lazio and a dip in form after an Achilles issue.

Years later, Ferguson admitted it was a mistake but his views at the time were no doubt affected by the release of Stam's autobiography.

Jaap Stam (right) left United shortly after the release of his controversial autobiography

Roy Keane – 2005

Roy Keane's exit from United 21 years ago was hugely explosive and came after a period where tensions between him and Sir Alex Ferguson had been rising.

Things came to a head following a 4-1 defeat by Middlesbrough at the start of November 2005, after which Keane appeared on MUTV and savagely ripped into his team-mates.

This included his brutal description of Rio Ferdinand, then United's record signing, when he said: 'Just because you are paid £120,000-a-week and play well for 20 minutes against Tottenham, you think you are a superstar.'

His comments were so inflammatory that Ferguson and United CEO David Gill ensured the interview was never broadcast. Those present had described the interview as 'explosive even by Keane's standards'.

His departure was confirmed by mutual consent a few weeks later, yet despite the dramatic ending, Keane was given a testimonial by United and Ferguson spoke highly of him after his retirement was confirmed in June 2006.

Roy Keane left United shortly after an inflammatory interview about his team-mates on MUTV

Wayne Rooney – 2010

Wayne Rooney may be United's record goalscorer after 13 years of glorious service, yet things could have been so different following the saga around his future in 2010.

Frustrated by the high-profile sales of Cristiano Ronaldo and Carlos Tevez the previous summer, Rooney raised doubts over the club's ambition in a statement after Ferguson revealed the forward wanted to leave.

Rooney claimed that in meetings, Gill and the Red Devils boss 'did not give me any assurances' over the future of the squad and the 'continued ability of the club to attract the top players in the world', insisting this wasn't about money.

Amid links to Man City, some fans protested outside Rooney's Cheshire mansion, with one banner reading: 'If you join City you're dead'.

But, in a dramatic u-turn days later following intense talks, Rooney signed a new five-year contract after receiving the assurances he craved.

Rooney later admitted his actions were wrong, and he went on to spend seven more years at Old Trafford before joining Everton in 2017.

United legend Wayne Rooney almost left in 2010 after handing in a transfer request

Cristiano Ronaldo – 2022

Cristiano Ronaldo's triumphant return to United in the summer of 2021 quickly turned sour, with the legendary Portuguese star leaving the club just over a year later after his contract was terminated.

Having grown frustrated with what he witnessed on and off the pitch, Ronaldo fell out with Erik ten Hag early on in the 2022-23 season.

So furious was Ronaldo that he gave an unsanctioned interview to Piers Morgan in November 2022.

Across the two-part chat, Ronaldo claimed he had 'no respect' for Ten Hag, insisted he felt 'betrayed' by the club and said that the Glazers 'do not care' about United.

He also hit out at his critics, which included former team-mates Gary Neville and Wayne Rooney, and made several other damning allegations.

Within a week of the interview airing, Ronaldo left the club by 'mutual agreement' without a pay-off, and he went on to join Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

Cristiano Ronaldo left United in November 2022 after falling out with boss Erik ten Hag

Jadon Sancho – 2023

When Jadon Sancho joined United from Borussia Dortmund in 2021 for £73million, it was one of the most anticipated Premier League transfers in years.

But things never got going for Sancho, and despite him eventually leaving on a free transfer this summer, his last Premier League appearance for United came on August 26, 2023, with a key moment coming a week later when they faced Arsenal.

Sancho was left out of the matchday squad that day, and ten Hag said post-match this was due to poor performances in training.

The winger immediately hit back on social media, saying the claims were 'completely untrue' and insisted he was being made a 'scapegoat' by the club.

Jadon Sancho famously spoke out against Erik ten Hag but things didn't work out well for him

Sancho appeared to choose the wrong man to take on, as, after refusing to apologise, he was banished from the first-team by ten Hag.

Sancho went on to join Dortmund on loan the following January, before successive season-long stints at Chelsea and Aston Villa.

He did feature once more for United – in the 2024 Community Shield – but the fact he was also deemed surplus to requirements under ten Hag's successor Ruben Amorim suggested that speaking out didn't work well.

Sports.title: Mike Tyson admits he suffered near-fatal overdoses at lowest point of his crippling drug issues... and reveals unusual remedy that saved him
Sports.content:
Mike Tyson admits he suffered near-fatal overdoses at lowest point of his crippling drug issues... and reveals unusual remedy that saved him

Mike Tyson has claimed he was saved by a powerful psychedelic from the toxin of a toad after suffering near-fatal drug overdoses.

The legendary boxer, 60, opened up on the terrifying health scares in a new Netflix docuseries, TYSON.

The former heavyweight champion detailed how he nearly died after battling alcohol and drug addiction, claiming: 'When I think about a low point, I think about this — OD'ing. I'm bleeding out, my nose is bleeding and I'm hysterical. I'm sweating.

'I OD'd, I've done it plenty of times but this one was a little more extreme than others.'

But Tyson survived after a shaman gave him 5-MeO-DMT, a substance found in the secretion of the Bofu alvarius toad. Early studies suggest it could help treat anxiety and depression.

The boxer claimed he has used the psychedelic 'over 100 times' and it helped him come off cocaine and alcohol.

Mike Tyson has claimed he was saved by a powerful psychedelic from the toxin of a toad

The legendary boxer, 60, opened up on near-fatal drug overdoses in a new Netflix docuseries

A shaman gave him 5-MeO-DMT, a substance found in the secretion of the Bofu Alvarius toad

'At the time we had this friend, he knew a shaman who does this thing called 5-MeO-DMT, it comes from the Bufo alvarius toad,' his third wife, Lakiha 'Kiki' Spicer, explained.

'Whatever kind of addictions or things that you're going through, it helps level them in your mind.'

According to the UC Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics, 5-MeO-DMT - which is also known as 'Bufo' or 'God molecule' or 'The Toad' - is 'usually inhaled through vaporizing or snorting.'

The drug, which is illegal to use recreationally in the United States, 'induces feelings of awe, visual and auditory hallucinations, and other sensations' with effects 'starting just a few seconds after ingestion and lasting about twenty to thirty minutes.'

In the new series, the 60-year-old is filmed smoking the drug at a treatment center.

'It blew my mind. I’ve done it over 100 times,' Tyson claimed. 'Any time I have to make a big decision about anything, I take the toad. I haven’t used cocaine and drink since.'

Sports.title: Tennis star who denied shoving a ball girl is now caught abusing a ball boy in f-word row over a TOWEL - before getting a dressing down from umpire and claiming 'I said nothing wrong'
Sports.content:
Tennis star who denied shoving a ball girl is now caught abusing a ball boy in f-word row over a TOWEL - before getting a dressing down from umpire and claiming 'I said nothing wrong'

Rafael Jodar has been involved in another ugly incident, with the Spanish tennis star caught swearing at a ball boy.

The 20-year-old, who courted controversy in May after being accused of pushing a ball girl at Roland-Garros, was captured using offensive language while demanding a towel during a match in Shanghai on Wednesday.

Footage of the immediate aftermath of the incident went viral online and captured Jodar's angry exchange with Ecuadorian chair umpire, Jimmy Pinoargote.

After losing two break points in succession, Jodar angrily told the ball boy: 'Give me the f***ing towel, damn it!'

Having received a warning for unsportsmanlike conduct by the umpire, he looked astonished and said: 'You give me a warning, man?'

The umpire replied: 'I understand, but not like that. Ask me and I'll ask him.' Jodar then denied anything untoward, arguing: 'But I didn't say anything bad to him.'

During his third-round win at the French Open against US's Alex Michelsen, Jodar was seen throwing a bottle of water to someone in his box at Roland-Garros before a ball girl suddenly walked across his path as he went to head backstage for a bathroom break.

The No27 seed had drawn fierce criticism online over the initial video, which one user shared on X while writing: 'But Rafael Jodar, he's a total creep. How he pushes the ball girl - And it's not the first time I've heard that he's awful off the court.'

Another fumed: 'Pathetic attitude from Rafa Jodar… I mean he's talented but this attitude doesn't belong in the tennis court.'

Sports.title: Football coach goes viral for his 'fight' not to even glance at glamorous journalist during interview
Sports.content:
A Czech football coach has gone viral for his apparent 'fight' to not even glance at a glamorous journalist during a post-match interview.

Sports reporter Sabina Jákšová was interviewing David Oulehla, coach of the Czech second division team FK Viagem Ústí nad Labem, last Friday following their 3-2 defeat against SFC Opava.

During the interview, Mr Oulehla appeared to be avoiding looking at her at all costs – a move that many on social media noticed.

One person wrote: 'He's fighting for his life.'

Another said: 'His level of self-control is biblical.'

And a third wrote: 'His wife is watching... total respect for his eye control!'

Ms Jákšová joined the second division club as a presenter at the end of the last season.

She said following her appointment: 'The club's management contacted me directly and made me the offer. I admit that I was happy and surprised at the same time.

Sports reporter Sabina Jákšová was interviewing David Oulehla, coach of the Czech second division team FK Viagem Ústínad Labem

Many online commented on his efforts to avoid eye contact with the glamorous reporter

Sabina Jákšová has worked at the club since the end of the last season

She had admitted that her knowledge of football is 'rather basic'

'I thought about it for a while, but finally said: "Why not? I'll try". However, I had no experience, so I learned everything along the way.'

She said that though her knowledge of football was 'rather basic to minimal... I like to learn something new, try new things and develop. At the same time, it's all very authentic. I'm learning how the club works as I go along.'

Last month, TNT Sports presenter Laura Woods left her colleagues stifling their laughter on a live broadcast with a rogue slip of the tongue.

The presenter was leading the post-game dissection of Liverpool's late 3-2 win over Atletico Madrid when she said: 'Diego Simeone, obviously quite a fiery character, he got himself sent off after the winner from Virgin.... Virgil van Dijk.'

Woods immediately realised the unfortunate mistake and laughed before regaining her composure.

Her pundits on duty for the night, Steve McManaman and Michael Owen, could be heard sniggering in the background.

Fortunately the footage at the time was a replay of an Atletico Madrid goal so viewers were unable to see the full reaction to Woods's blunder.

When the camera does switch back to the pitch-side set-up with all three on screen, Mr Owen and Woods still appeared to be smirking.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Andy Burnham warning sent as Pep Guardiola set to return
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United star Paul Scholes has doubled down on being more than happy to pick up another Premier League medal after Manchester City were found guilty of breaking the division's financial rules. The former midfielder's stance is in stark contrast to that of his United team-mate Wayne Rooney, who doesn't believe they deserve it.

There is a possibility City lose their titles, though the chances of the runners-up being promoted to champions instead appears remote for the moment. But Scholes, who has 11 Premier League titles to his name, would happily add another medal to his collection.

Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football, sponsored by Midnite, Scholes emphatically responded to Paddy McGuinness' assertion that he wouldn't want the title.

“Why not?" said Scholes. F*****g yeah. I only played 14 times somewhere in the last six months of the season. But yeah, I would take it. "We lost on goal difference that year. Do you not think the rest of our team, our teammates, the manager and the staff are working their bollocks off all year to try and win the league? And just because a team did it wrongly, cheated, that we wouldn’t want it?”

Rooney previously admitted he wouldn't be comfortable accepting a winner's medal. "I have heard Rio has come out saying about getting another Premier League medal... I wouldn’t really feel comfortable accepting another Premier League medal, if I’m being honest," said Rooney on the Stick To United podcast.

Sports.title: Peter Crouch hails 'amazing' family duo who save men from suicide
Sports.content:
Peter Crouch hails 'amazing' family duo who save men from suicide

Elaine Roberts and Luke Ambler were told by an emotional Peter Crouch that they've won a Pride of Britain award for setting up Andy's Man Club, an initiative that has helped tens of thousands of men going through hard times

View 6 Images Andy’s Man Club founders Luke Ambler and Elaine Roberts were surprised by Peter Crouch with a Pride of Britain award (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

When Elaine Roberts and Luke Ambler popped into Peter Crouch’s podcast studio, they got far more than they bargained for. The duo thought they were with the footballer for an interview about their charity, Andy’s Man’s Club. But, through tears, Peter told them they’d won a Pride of Britain award for setting up the initiative that has helped tens of thousands of men going through hard times.

‌



‌



Luke said: “I’m never lost for words, but that’s stunned me. An emotional Elaine simply added: “Gobsmacked.” Elaine and Luke will receive their Special Recognition award on stage at the Daily Mirror’s Pride of Britain Awards in partnership with P&O Cruises, on October 19.

‌



In 2016, Andy Roberts, Elaine’s son and Luke’s brother-in-law, tragically took his own life at just 23 years old. Elaine, 71, says: “Andrew was mischievous. Always had been, as soon as he could walk. He was like a little tough nut, but he had a heart of gold.

‌



View 6 Images Andy and his mum Elaine

“I got a knock on the door to say they’d found Andrew. I told Luke, and I just broke down. ‘Our Andrew’s gone.’ Doesn’t get any tougher.” And Luke says: “He was just a really kind, very caring young man.”

Andy’s devastated family had no idea that he had been struggling so much. They soon discovered that male suicide is the biggest killer of UK men under 50.

‌



Three months after losing Andy, Luke and Elaine used their grief to make a difference and set up Andy’s Man Club, a male suicide prevention charity. It’s a place where men struggling with their mental health can come together for support.

Elaine says: “Even though you’re drowning in your own grief, you don’t want anyone else to go through it, and you just want to stop as many as you can - whatever it takes to stop the next family going through it.

View 6 Images Andy's Man Club member Omar said: “I’d been through a very dark time in my life. People comforted me, and people told me it was OK."

‌



“I lost my son to suicide and Luke came to me three months later and suggested a coffee club where guys could go to talk, because I’m sure if Andrew would have talked to us he wouldn’t have taken his life.

Oliver Vikse, was one of the first nine men to walk through the door. He says: “I had a really bad period in my life. My family unit had broken down. I experienced homelessness and I lost three friends to suicide. I still remember the electricity in the room after that first session. It was so refreshing to sit and be heard.”

A simple concept was having profound effects. Luke, 36, a former pro rugby player, says: “Nine men turned up that first night. Not only did they need to talk, but they needed that connection to know that whatever they were going through in that moment, they weren’t the only one. A week after, 15 men turned up, and then 20 men, and it’s just never slowed down.”

‌



Andy’s Man Club is a simple, barrier-free space for men to have “a brew and a chat”. It started as one initial group meeting with just nine men in Halifax, and has now - ten years later - expanded into more than 360 community groups across England, Scotland and Wales, alongside online sessions.

View 6 Images Andy's Man Club member Josh said: "I’d lost my car, my job, my house. Something as simple as a hot drink and a smile made the heavy stuff feel just a little bit lighter."

Member Omar said: “I’d been through a very dark time in my life. People comforted me, and people told me it was OK." Member Josh said: "I’d lost my car, my job, my house. Something as simple as a hot drink and a smile made the heavy stuff feel just a little bit lighter."

‌



Neil said: “You feel worthless. Andy’s Man Club came along at just the right time. I think it’s safe to say without Andy’s Man Club, there’d be dead, divorced, or both."

Anthony said: “I felt like I wasn’t worthy of a place on this Earth. And ended up taking an attempt at my own life. It felt like it removed the hood... completely changed my life. And then I wanted to help others as well. Without them, without the club, I wouldn’t be here.”

Every Monday night, roughly 7,000 men gather for free, confidential, walk-in peer support - no registration or referral needed. The sessions are completely volunteer-led, with all group leaders having first interacted with Andy’s Man Club when they used it themselves.

‌



View 6 Images Luke says: “There’s one common thread that runs through it all: How can we give more guys hope?" (Image: STEVE ALLEN)

Luke says: “There’s one common thread that runs through it all: How can we give more guys hope, and how can we get more guys to believe that tomorrow can be better than today? If he’d have had a chat with someone, maybe he’d still be here now.”

And Elaine adds: “I’ve grown through my grief doing nothing but talking about it, helping other people. Haven’t we? I’d like to think he’d be proud. The amount of guys that come up to me and say, “If it wasn’t for you, I wouldn’t be here.” We’d rather he were here for Andrew, but it’s the next best thing.”

‌



Determined to shatter stigmas, Luke also started a viral #ItsOkayToTalk campaign, which reached more than 100 million people worldwide, building an incredible legacy that has saved thousands of lives.

As part of their work to raise awareness, Elaine and Luke arrived at That Peter Crouch Podcast studio. Breaking the news of their Pride of Britain award, Peter was overcome with emotion. He said: “I get emotional when people have achieved something amazing, and I don’t think they’ve realised quite how many people they’ve touched.”

View 6 Images An emotional Peter Crouch gives Elaine a hug (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

‌



Elaine and Luke will be presented with their Pride of Britain Award on Monday 19 October, at the Mirror’s annual ceremony at Grosvenor House in London.

Elaine says her mission is just getting started: “We’re trying to break down the stigma and we’ve only just scratched the surface. It’s about helping as many men as possible, one person at a time. We’ve been told Andy’s Man Club should be on prescription, bottled and sold at Boots. It can be emotional, but it’s an uplifting experience and makes you feel connected.”

Luke says: “The goal has always been to stop other families going through what ours went through. Seeing men who needed support now giving it to others makes me so proud. We’d be nothing without our team, volunteers, supporters and everyone who’s contributed.

‌



“Ten years building Andy’s Man Club alongside a growing family and my own business has been tough. But when someone says they’re still here because of it, you know why you’ve kept going and doing it. Alongside your mother-in-law? That’s a whole other story!

“It doesn’t feel like 10 years, it feels like the first day every day. Constantly re-ignites the fire to stop other families going through what we’ve been through.

*The Pride of Britain Awards will take place on 19th October, before airing on ITV and ITVX from 22nd October. Find out more about the Pride of Britain Awards 2026 HERE

Sports.title: Abandoned Champions League stadium now overgrown mess with explosives warning signs
Sports.content:
Abandoned Champions League stadium now overgrown mess with explosives warning signs

The impressive ground, which has hosted European Championship and Champions League games, has stood empty for more than a decade

View Image The Donbas Arena is a sorry sight these days as the war in Ukraine continues (Image: PHILIPPE DESMAZES/AFP via Getty Images)

A stadium that once hosted huge games at club and international level now lies abandoned and overgrown in war-torn Ukraine. Prior to 2014, the Donbas Arena was home to Shakhtar Donetsk.

‌



‌



The 52,000-seater ground, which cost £318million, officially opened in August 2009, three years ahead of Euro 2012, which was jointly held by Ukraine and Poland. At the time, it was a symbol of ambition in the country that declared independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.

‌



Having taken over from Dynamo Kyiv as the country's dominant force, Shakhtar hosted big Champions League games against the likes of Manchester United and Arsenal. The ground also hosted five games at Euro 2012, including England's 1-1 draw with France and 1-0 win over the hosts in the group stage.

‌



However, just five years after opening, the stadium had to be abandoned. The UEFA Category 4 facility was shelled as the Ukrainian armed forces clashed with pro-Russian separatists for control of the city.

£318m Champions League stadium that hosted Man Utd and Arsenal was abandoned after 5 years READ MORE :

Shakhtar's last fixture there was in 2014, a 3-1 win over Illichivets Mariupol that secured a fifth straight league crown in front of a crowd of less than 18,000 as the city braced for conflict.

Later that year, the venue sustained extensive damage to its turnstiles and entrances from heavy artillery fire and explosions as the conflict escalated. A shell initially hit the arena, sparking a blaze. Meanwhile, a rocket landed close to the stadium grounds.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Images from the period show the stadium with portions of its roof and facade obliterated and various fragments of debris strewn across the ground outside.

‌



A stadium guide told the BBC in 2019: "It was pretty costly to repair the roof after the blast pulled it off. The job needs finishing, and that takes money the DPR (Donet People's Republic) don't have."

Recent pictures of the overgrown site paint an even bleaker picture, with signs warning: "DO NOT WALK ON THE LAWN! CAUTION! EXPLOSIVE OBJECTS MAY BE PRESENT."

Article continues below

Shakhtar remain exiled and will play their 'home' Champions League games at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge, starting against AEK Athens on Wednesday.

Given Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which started in 2022, it remains unclear whether the stadium will ever be operational again, having sustained further damage.

Since the start of the conflict, Shakhtar have played matches in Lviv and Kyiv, as well as in Germany and neighbouring Poland. Meanwhile, the Donbas Arena is now a stark reminder of what Ukraine had and has now lost.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez 'challenged' by team-mate on flight home as Man Utd plot next steps
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez 'challenged' by team-mate on flight home as Man Utd plot next steps

Lisandro Maritnez's comments have sparked debate inside and outside of the Manchester United dressing room, having criticised the club's hierarchy after their loss away to Atletico Madrid

View Image Lisandro Martinez is facing a punishment from Manchester United (Image: Getty)

One Manchester United player is understood to have challenged team-mate Lisandro Martinez on their flight home from Madrid following his explosive comments in a post-match interview.

‌



‌



United defender Martinez slammed the higher-ups at Old Trafford for not signing enough players in the summer transfer window, leaving the team ill prepared for the Champions League. The 28-year-old even took aim at director of football Jason Wilcox, saying that he 'expects more' from him.

‌



His comments came after Michael Carrick's team suffered a controversial 2-0 loss against Atletico Madrid. Although a large portion of United's fans are on Martinez's side, at least one team-mate didn't agree with the decision to voice his frustration.

‌



Sky Sports report that one player - who is unnamed - challenged the Argentine over his comments as the squad got on board the plane to fly back to Manchester.

The club's board also haven't taken kindly to his interview. Martinez is likely to be hit with a fine and it remains to be seen whether he'll be dropped from the squad ahead of Sunday's game away to Leeds.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Meanwhile, his long-term future at Old Trafford is uncertain. Martinez's contract is due to expire at the end of this season, and while United have the option to trigger a one-year extension, club chiefs are actively looking to sign a centre-back and find ways of reducing their eye-watering wage bill.

It's added that the ex-Ajax star has been keen to leave for some time, hoping for a move to, coincidentally, Atletico this summer. United paid £57million for Martinez in 2022 and he's won two trophies, both under former manager Erik ten Hag.

‌



Carrick said after the defeat in Spain that he hadn't seen the full interview, but he'll no doubt be questioned on it later this week ahead of United's trip to Elland Road. Martinez told Prime Video Sport: "Really poor. Really poor. I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.

"We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well. Today, Atletico have an amazing team and they deserve to win today.

Should Man Utd punish Lisandro Martinez for comments on owners? Have your say READ MORE :

"I expect more [investment]. 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director [Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

Article continues below

"In general. Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team. It is annoying, disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here. It's disappointing."

He added: "You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager. What about other areas? I can't say more. Tonight it is easy to say the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."

Sports.title: Mason Greenwood's journey since leaving Man Utd as he prepares for frosty England return
Sports.content:
When Mason Greenwood's number flashed up to be substituted in the 71st minute of Manchester United's 3-1 victory over Brentford on January 19, 2022, no one expected that it would be the last time we saw him play on English soil for the best part of five years.

But 1,730 days later, he's back. Greenwood is set to line up for Fenerbahce when they take on Aston Villa at Villa Park in the Champions League on Wednesday.

The 25-year-old continues to his rebuild his career abroad after he left United in acrimonious circumstances. Days after the win at Brentford, Greenwood would be arrested and later charged with attempted rape, engaging in controlling behaviour and assault.

Just over a year later on February 2, 2023, the charges against him were dropped. The Crown Prosecution Service said that key witnesses had withdrawn their involvement and 'new material had come to light'.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Following an internal investigation, United decided to loan Greenwood out to Spanish club Getafe for the following season, as the forward took the first steps in rebuilding his career. Now he finds himself plying his trade in Turkey with Fenerbahce.

Mirror Football breaks down his journey since leaving Old Trafford permanently in 2024.

‌



How we got here

After a productive campaign with Getafe, scoring 10 goals and providing six assists, there was plenty of interest in Greenwood. Spanish heavyweights Barcelona and Real Madrid were linked with a move, but it was French giants Marseille who signed him from United.

The Red Devils, who had him on their books since the age of seven, accepted a bid of €31.6million (£26.6m) which included a significant sell-on clause thought to be worth 40 per cent. Marseille's decision drew criticism, including from the city's mayor, who urged them not to sign the one-time England international.

Greenwood found his feet quickly, though, and netted 22 goals in his first season under Roberto De Zerbi. Marseille qualified for the Champions League, as they faced Newcastle and Liverpool (both at home) in the league phase.

In his second term, Greenwood improved his goalscoring tally and netted 26 times. But with De Zerbi having left the Stade Velodrome in February, Marseille only finished fifth and needed to raise funds.

‌



View 5 Images Mason Greenwood spent the 2023-24 season on loan with Getafe (Image: Cesar Cebolla / Pressinphoto / Icon Sport)

Why Marseille sold him

Despite being their top scorer two seasons in a row, Marseille opted to sell Greenwood this summer. The striker had been receiving backlash from supporters for what critics perceived was a bad attitude, and it was felt that a fresh start was best for all parties.

Fenerbahce came calling and agreed a €39m (£33.3m) deal. Marseille explained: "This decision is the result of a joint discussion between the player and the club, who mutually agreed to end their collaboration. Olympique de Marseille thanks Mason Greenwood for his two seasons with the club and wishes him every success in his future career."

Greenwood helped the Turkish side qualify for the Champions League via the play-offs and registered an assist in their first game of this season's league phase, a 1-1 draw at home to Roma. He currently has four goals and two assists in seven Turkish Super Lig appearances.

‌



View 5 Images Mason Greenwood's performances were criticised towards the end of his time at Marseille (Image: Christophe Simon/AFP via Getty Images)

Ugly scenes in last Villa meeting

Wednesday won't be the first time that Greenwood has come up against Villa since leaving United. In August 2025, Unai Emery's side travelled to Marseille for a pre-season friendly.

Greenwood caught Amadou Onana with a late tackle and began laughing in his face. Villa's Tyrone Mings went over to defend his team-mate, grabbing the ex-United star by the collar and thrashing him around.

Mings and Greenwood were briefly team-mates for England in September 2020 when the latter made his one and only appearance in a Nations League match away to Iceland. There was no love lost between them.

‌



Regardless of the reception that he'll no doubt receive from Villa's players and fans, Matty Cash is still wary of Greenwood's 'threat'. "A few years ago at Manchester United, he broke in and was one of the best players in his position as a young boy," Cash said at Villa's pre-match press conference.

"He's still an attacking threat. He will come to England wanting to prove himself again, so it will be a good test. We spoke about it on Monday - if you concede goals, two or more, you won’t win games at this level."

View 5 Images Mason Greenwood and Tyrone Mings got into an altercation last year (Image: Neal Simpson/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

What next for Greenwood?

In the years since his departure from Old Trafford, there've been tentative links of a return to the Premier League. But it remains highly unlikely that Greenwood will return to his home country on a permanent basis in the near future.

‌



His contract with Fenerbahce is set to keep him in Istanbul until 2030 and his record suggests that the club would demand a sizeable fee to let him go. What Greenwood hasn't committed to, however, is which country he'd like to represent at international level.

FIFA's rules allow him the possibility of switching to another eligible nation and he obtained a Jamaican passport last year. But Greenwood refused a call-up for Jamaica, leaving the door open to play for England again.

View 5 Images Mason Greenwood appears to be settling in well at Fenerbahce (Image: Beyza Comert/Anadolu via Getty Images)

However, as of September 2025, he isn't in Thomas Tuchel's plans. "I have not spoken to him until now. I have not spoken to him or his camp," Tuchel said.

‌



"My understanding was that he tries to play for Jamaica so we didn't give it another thought. He was not in the mix at the moment and he is not in our thoughts for our team."

Perhaps Greenwood - also now a father of two - is targeting a return for England in time for the European Championship in 2028, and if he keeps up this form, there'll be clamour for a call-up. But teams, coaches and fans will always be forced to ask themselves bigger questions than just his footballing ability when it comes to Greenwood.

Sports.title: Jockey Kieren Fox suspended for 10 days over 'questionable' Wolverhampton ride
Sports.content:
Jockey Kieren Fox suspended for 10 days over 'questionable' Wolverhampton ride

Jockey Kieren Fox has been handed a 10-day ban after stewards deemed his mount to be a non-trier in a race at Wolverhampton, with the inquiry finding he made insufficient effort in the closing stages.

View 2 Images Kieren Fox: banned for ten days (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

Jockey Kieren Fox has been slapped with a 10-day suspension after stewards ruled his horse failed to run on its merits during Tuesday evening's seven-furlong novice contest at Wolverhampton.

‌



‌



The 37-year-old guided the Charlie Pike-trained 40-1 shot Missmisfortune to fourth place out of nine runners in the Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Novice Stakes.

‌



But following an investigation into his performance, and after questioning both Fox and the trainer's representative, Wolverhampton stewards concluded the jockey had not made adequate effort from the two-furlong pole.

‌



Trailblazing female jump jockey hit with 20-day whip ban and horse disqualified READ MORE :

Value Scope Extra: Future Champions Festival actually lives up to its name READ MORE :

Stewards challenged Fox over his riding inside the final furlong, observing that he employed his whip only once during that phase and seemed to ride "with a questionable level of vigour" towards the line.

Fox argued he felt he was "at his strongest" during that stretch, while Pike's representative expressed satisfaction with the ride, noting that Missmisfortune was a challenging ride.

‌



View 2 Images (Image: Simon Galloway, Getty Images)

Nevertheless, the stewards' report stated: "Fox was suspended for 10 days for failing to take all reasonable and permissible measures to ensure his horse was run on its merits.

"Having initially failed to put his mount in a position from where it could best mount a challenge by not asking Missmisfortune to improve having taken her off the rail approaching the two-furlong marker, he then appeared to ride without sufficient vigour for periods in the home straight."

Article continues below

Fox will serve his 10-day ban from October 27-31 and November 2-6. The jockey, who made a comeback in February following a six-year absence from racing, has notched up 238 British career victories, with 15 of those coming this year.

Sports.title: Mikel Merino on Arsenal's new style, 'finishers' and why they can't have a small squad
Sports.content:
Mikel Merino on Arsenal's new style, 'finishers' and why they can't have a small squad

Arsenal star Mikel Merino is happy to play whatever role he can as the Gunners look to compete on all four fronts and finally end their long wait for the Champions League

View 2 Images Arsenal midfielder Mikel Merino during the win over Lille

Mikel Merino says Arsenal’s entire squad have bought into their new “new style.”

‌



‌



Gunners boss Mikel Arteta oversaw a shake-up of his fitness and medical staff in the summer and has also been at pains to stress the importance of “finishers” playing a key role from the bench.

‌



Merino has yet to start in the Premier League this season, but has come on in all six of their games and insists he is very happy to play his part.

‌



World Cup winner Merino started against Lille in the Champions League and it was other substitutes - including Bukayo Saka, Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard - who really came on to seal the win.

But Merino says they are all buying into Arteta’s grand plan for this season with the Spain midfielder admitting there is a new approach when it comes to substitutes being ready and winning games late on.

Mikel Arteta's massive gamble pays off but struggling Arsenal star fluffs his chance READ MORE :

Kate Scott ruins Micah Richards live on TV over Man City 114 charges verdict READ MORE :

Rugby first coined the “finishers” phrase with players coming on against tired opponents. Now Arteta is sending a clear message to his whole match day squad that they are all involved.

‌



Merino said: “There’s a new style absolutely. That’s very personal, some players might like something and some players might like other things.

“I do like a lot what we’re doing, you can see the squad is fresh and ready to play at the highest level with the highest rhythm to the last minute. That’s good news. I don’t want to speak too much about it, to reveal anything or compare two different staff members.

View 2 Images Bukayo Saka came off the bench to grab a goal and an assist as Arsenal beat Lille

‌



“We really loved the guys who were here before and really appreciated the work they were putting in for us. The team was ready last season, this season it’s a different concept that’s working, congratulations to everyone.”

Substitutes making an impact from the bench is not new and nor is players doing different, intense warm-ups. But Merino was talking about a different mindset, different messages and also more detailed instructions when players come on.

Merino is also the epitome of a model pro and a manager’s dream because he has won the biggest honours but is happy to be a good squad member and Arsenal do always have a wealth of international quality and experience on the bench.

‌



Merino said: “Mentality is key. Also a bit of intelligence to have the reference of how the game is going, not only the result but what are they doing on the pitch, the momentum of the game, if we’re attacking or defending, what the team needs from you in that moment and then adapt to it with the best attitude possible.

“Mentality is the main concept when you score late in the game. When you get tired physically you get tired mentally.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"This team is proving that [they don’t], not only the guys on the pitch are always focused but the guys who come on for the last couple of minutes. They come ready to make an impact. It also speaks highly about the quality of the squad.

“It’s the key of this squad. Everyone is ready when they have the chance. With the amount of games we have, you see the squads are getting bigger and bigger.

‌



"There is no chance we could have a small squad. You need the biggest squad possible with most quality possible. I’m a perfect example of this, the finishers are crucial. I’ve had the opportunity to show it with club and country. We’re all ready to play our part.

“I’m happy to play to be fair. Whenever I’m on the pitch I’m with the best mentality, the best character to make an impact and put everything I have on the pitch.

“It’s always pressure, there’s always consequences if you do or don’t play well. We’re used to that. We’re professionals, we can’t think like that, we just have to think positive on what things we can do to help our team.”
