Sports.title: Spotlight: Wolff claimed Red Bull power unit would be “completely s***” – Horner | Briefs
Sports.content:
Former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner has taken another swipe at his ex-rival Toto Wolff.

Speaking after Red Bull-Ford’s first victory as a power unit manufacturer, Horner claimed Wolff dismissed their chances of success Formula 1. “He said this [Red Bull] engine was going to be completely shit and a disaster,” Horner told The Guardian

Horner founded Red Bull’s power unit programme after its former supplier Honda announced its withdrawal as a manufacturer at the end of 2021 (it returned this year with Aston Martin). Mercedes consistently refused to supply engines to Red Bull. Horner claimed McLaren CEO Zak Brown, whose team won the last two constructors’ titles, is unable to apply pressure to Wolff.

“Toto’s got it quite easy at the moment,” he said. “Zak Brown is compromised because he’s using Toto’s engine so he can’t ruffle feathers.

“All sport needs rivalry, whether it’s Ferguson and Wenger, Mourinho and Guardiola. It percolates and polarises. I used that to galvanise good people to take on Mercedes.”

Horner has given several interviews recently as he is promoting a forthcoming book. He claimed recent comments he made regarding his desire to run Ferrari’s F1 team were misinterpreted.

“Fred Vasseur is an experienced guy,” said Horner. “He’s done a decent job. But I, more than anyone, know the pressures of running a competitive organisation. My comments got taken out of context.”

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Questions Derek Chisora’s Retirement Advice
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley has dismissed Derek Chisora’s prediction that the Daniel Dubois rematch could be his final fight, pointing to the veteran’s own refusal to retire. Chisora makes an easy target, although questioning his credibility won’t help Wardley avoid another punishing night against Dubois.

“This is specially funny coming from Derek who should have retired many a year ago and has still carried on,” Wardley told talkSPORT Boxing.

Wardley can dismiss Derek all day long. When the bell rings, he has to stop Dubois from handing him another brutal beating.

His punch power offers a real path to victory. Dubois gets hit plenty. Wardley doesn’t need to reinvent himself to land something concussive. Catching Dubois early could silence the retirement chatter immediately.

The real test arrives if Dubois weathers the early storm. Wardley can’t trade jabs with Dubois, who controls distance behind a heavier, straighter lead hand. Letting combinations fly creates openings, but staying in the pocket makes Fabio an easy target unless he exits instantly.

Wardley mentioned his camp didn’t add special safety measures, choosing to ramp up workout tempo instead. That comment says nothing about tactical adjustments, since he addressed injury prevention rather than fight strategy.

Training harder in the gym won’t erase the danger Dubois brings. Better stamina might keep Wardley active late, but it won’t stop a stiff jab cracking his nose. It won’t deflect a hard right hand when he steps inside, either.

Chisora lecturing anyone on when to hang up the gloves is rich considering his own track record. Since knocking out Carlos Takam eight years ago, his record has been a parade of beatings at the elite level, interrupted only by narrow decisions over fading names like Kubrat Pulev, Gerald Washington, and domestic gatekeepers.

When Tyson Fury was using him as target practice in their third meeting while the referee practically begged Chisora’s corner to stop it, nobody thought, ‘Now there goes a man with sound judgment on ring longevity.’

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Calls Frank Sanchez Defense a ‘Maybe’
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic sees himself competing in the heavyweight division for another five years. His recent comments regarding mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez, however, spark an immediate debate over his willingness to face the Cuban next.

Talking through potential matchups with reporters, Hrgovic pointed toward Agit Kabayel and the winner of Daniel Dubois versus Fabio Wardley 2 before tossing in, “or maybe my mandatory,” according to The Ring.

That kind of phrasing is as transparent as glass. When a newly crowned champion starts referring to his official number one contender as “maybe my mandatory,” that is not a slip of the tongue. That is pure preservation instinct kicking in. Unfiltered remarks often expose a fighter’s true intentions faster than any scripted press release.

Hrgovic has not officially declined the fight, but brushing off his primary obligation as “maybe my mandatory” sounds suspiciously evasive. He understands how sanctioning bodies operate. Treating a mandated defense as an open question makes it look like he hopes the requirement simply disappears.

Hrgovic knows exactly what he survived against Moses Itauma. He got battered pillar to post, lost virtually every single second of the first eight rounds, and only walked away with the belt because a 21-year-old blew his entire engine looking for an early highlight reel. You cannot build a five-year reign on the hope that every opponent will gas out after eight rounds of teeing off on your chin.

Frank Sanchez represents the worst possible stylistic matchup for Hrgovic right now. The Cuban is powerful, disciplined, skilled, and does not sell out for wild early knockouts. He will not punch himself into exhaustion. Sanchez would force Hrgovic to actually box, lead, cut off the ring, and win rounds on skill and volume, things Hrgovic has struggled with whenever he steps up in class.

“I think I have a lot of fights left,” Hrgovic explained. “And I want to unify. I don’t know the exact number of fights, but I think I can be here for five more years.”

Planning a half-decade run at the top is bold talk for someone whose grip on the belt remains so fragile.

Chasing unification against the Dubois-Wardley winner certainly promises a richer payday. Neither option represents a walk in the park, though. Dubois previously stopped the Croatian, and Wardley possesses the raw power to scramble anyone’s night.

The sport is supposed to run on the mandatory system, forcing champions to defend against the rightful top contenders. When a guy wins a belt by the skin of his teeth and immediately starts scheming ways to bypass the division’s trickiest puzzle, it tells you everything you need to know about how confident his team really is in his longevity. If he actually fights Sanchez next, it will only be because the sanctioning body backed him into a corner with no exit.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Could Await Tyson Fury After Joshua
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury could face Agit Kabayel in Germany after Anthony Joshua, according to his manager Spencer Brown. The suggestion depends on Fury winning on December 11, although a crushing defeat might still leave a fun fight for Kabayel’s home supporters.

Managing both fighters gives Brown an easy angle, and he claimed their friendship will not stand in the way of a bout. They will share the ring if required, according to Brown.

“If he beats Anthony Joshua, you know, there’s Agit Kabayel in Germany,” Brown said to the The Ariel Helwani Show. “They’d do the dance if they needed to.

Longtime Wladimir Klitschko supporters would remember Fury taking his titles in Düsseldorf in 2015. Watching Kabayel beat Fury on German soil could feel like settling an old score. If Joshua had already battered him, some might enjoy seeing their current heavyweight star finish the job. That would make for a lively atmosphere, even if Fury arrived with his best years behind him.

Both Fury and Joshua share the exact same problem right now. Their legs are nearly gone, their punch resistance has diminished, and they rely heavily on smoke, mirrors, and holding to stay upright against anyone capable of applying sustained pressure. Kabayel is wrong for both of them. He throws with bad intentions downstairs, refuses to give opponents room to breathe, and punishes excessive clinching by working free hands into the flanks.

The British public loves watching former belt holders test their luck one time too many, and German fans would gladly pay top dollar to see Kabayel dismantle whatever remains of Fury.

The question is, would Fury agree to the fight? A fighter whose entire public persona rests on invincibility does not sign up to become fodder for a younger, hungrier pressure puncher. Even if Turki dangled a massive paycheck in front of him, taking the bout means accepting a scenario where he cannot dictate terms, control the tempo, or hide behind basic veteran survival tactics against Kabayel.

The Makhmudov and Wach performances laid everything bare. The legs were heavy, the reflexes were delayed, and the movement that once bailed him out looked completely gone. Against stationary targets, he managed to scrape by on pure size and roughhouse clinching, but Kabayel represents a completely different proposition.

For Fury, taking a battering from Joshua only to travel into Kabayel’s backyard is a recipe for humiliation

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Faces Race Against Time Against Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley could be racing against time to stop Daniel Dubois in Saturday’s rematch, with his damaged nose threatening to undermine his attempt to reclaim the WBO heavyweight title.

Wardley dropped Dubois twice in the first three rounds of their May fight, proving he has the power to hurt him. He couldn’t finish the job, and Dubois’ sustained attack left him with a badly cut nose and a swollen right eye before the 11th-round stoppage.

That makes another prolonged fight a concern. Paul Smith raised the possibility of Wardley’s nose reopening after seeing him in talkSPORT’s studio this week. Simon Jordan also questioned how well it had healed, predicting an early cut. Neither view establishes what will happen on Saturday, but the first fight showed how damaging Dubois’ punches can be.

Trying to out-jab Dubois looks a difficult route for Wardley. He hasn’t shown the same powerful, ramrod jab, and following Oleksandr Usyk’s approach requires more than putting combinations together.

Usyk’s movement allowed him to step into range, land, and get away before Dubois could respond. Wardley hasn’t demonstrated that same footwork. Throwing combinations while remaining in front of Dubois would give the champion opportunities to answer.

Wardley is intelligent, though, and five months may have given him time to make meaningful changes. He doesn’t need to reproduce everything Usyk does. Moving after punching and changing angles could reduce the punishment and buy him more time to find an opening.

His clearest opportunity remains Dubois’ vulnerability when caught clean. Those two early knockdowns give Wardley a reason to believe he can end the fight before cuts or swelling restrict his vision. Chasing that finish recklessly would also expose him to the punches he needs to avoid.

Smith would accept Wardley walking away afterward.

“I’d have no problem with him if he didn’t want to fight again after this,” he told talkBOXING.

Wardley hasn’t announced retirement plans. His immediate challenge is finding a way to finish Dubois—or showing enough tactical improvement to keep that clock from running out.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Backs Canelo Alvarez Over ‘One-Dimensional’ Mbilli
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora backs Canelo Alvarez’s boxing to beat Christian Mbilli, dismissing the challenger as too one-dimensional. That prediction leaves a bigger question unanswered: whether Canelo can handle the pace without tiring against a younger fighter who keeps coming.

“Canelo has the edge in this one. Mbilli is a good fighter, a strong fighter, but for me, he’s too one-dimensional,” said Fundora to DAZN.

Fundora pointed to Mbilli’s fight with Lester Martinez to explain his doubts, saying he expected a knockout.

“We saw when he fought Lester Martinez; he kind of lost, and I expected him to knock out Lester. But he lost, and Canelo has way more boxing [skills] than that.”

Fundora is committing two classic errors here: analyzing a fighter based on past reputation rather than current reality, and constructing an entire technical case on a false premise.

First, getting the outcome of the Martinez fight wrong completely undercuts his credibility. Mbilli did not lose that fight; it was a grueling split draw where Martinez had to resort to repeated, blatant shoving just to survive the inside pressure and create punching room. Building an argument that Mbilli will fold against Canelo because he “kind of lost” collapses the moment you look at what actually happened in the ring.

Second, Fundora is talking about Canelo as if this were the 2018 or 2021 version who could slip, counter, and control the center of the ring for twelve uninterrupted rounds. That fighter is gone.

At 36, after extensive wear and tear, long stretches of inactivity, and noticeable stamina drops in the second half of fights, Canelo has become an economy puncher. He relies on explosive, low-volume bursts to bank rounds while resting on the ropes.

Mbilli is the absolute worst style for an aging champion trying to conserve energy. Mbilli does not care about taking two clean shots if it allows him to land five to the body and force a phone-booth brawl.

Against a tireless pressure fighter who refuses to let him breathe, Canelo cannot just rely on superior technique. Ring IQ only works if the legs and lungs can carry out the plan for three full minutes of every round. Fundora is picking the name and the highlight reel, completely ignoring the clock and the stylistic nightmare right in front of Canelo.

Sports.title: Team Schofield Attacks Shakur Stevenson’s Power And Reputation
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield Jr. and his father criticized Shakur Stevenson’s punching power, opposition, and reputation, with the elder Schofield arguing that his elite billing comes from his connections to famous fighters rather than the opponents he has beaten.

“He got no power. He’s only elite by association, not by who he fought, because he haven’t fought nobody elite,” said Floyd Schofield during their Fight Hub TV interview. “People put him on the scales. Why? Because Andre Ward managed him. Because Crawford is like his big brother. Because Floyd Mayweather wanted to manage him when he was coming out the Olympics.”

Schofield’s father also called Shakur “a clown,” questioning why the boxing community gives his opinions so much attention.

The criticism followed Stevenson’s comments on X after Schofield’s unanimous decision win over Lucas Bahdi for the vacant WBA lightweight title. Shakur dismissed Schofield as a C-level fighter, something the newly crowned champion clearly hadn’t forgotten during the interview.

“When he tweeted, I was like, he really a fan because he was watching me. I can’t remember the last time I watched a Shakur fight,” said Schofield Jr.

The younger Schofield questioned Shakur’s right to criticize him after sharing the ring with a puncher like Bahdi. His complaint focused on Stevenson’s use of movement when facing dangerous opponents.

“He uses the whole ring like a track field,” said Schofield Jr. “Somebody who fights like that can’t tell me how I fight or how I should fight or what type of fighter I am.”

Schofield acknowledged that he has things to improve, yet remained pleased with his performance and the crowd’s reaction. Later, he endorsed his father’s comments: “You said everything I could say, bro. I agree 100%.”

The father’s strongest argument concerns opposition. Having Ward and Crawford’s approval doesn’t replace beating top fighters. Shakur’s power is a separate question, because a fighter can succeed through timing, accuracy, and defense without producing knockouts.

For all their criticism, the Schofields aren’t pushing to face Stevenson next. His father said their plans have nothing to do with Shakur, while discussing William Zepeda as an easier fight to arrange.

The insults are getting louder, while a fight between them remains outside Team Schofield’s immediate plans.

Sports.title: Vito Mielnicki Targets Major Step Up Against Xander Zayas
Sports.content:
Vito Mielnicki Jr. is asking for a major step up in class against Xander Zayas, calling for the fight on social media and offering to meet the former unified light middleweight champion at Madison Square Garden or in Puerto Rico.

Mielnicki’s win over Austin Williams has put him in position to pursue a bigger fight. Zayas would test whether Vito’s fairly basic style can take him much further against opponents with championship experience.

“Nothing but respect for my guy @xander.zayas, but this is the fight that needs to happen!!” Mielnicki wrote. “The big room at MSG or in Puerto Rico.”

Vito deserves credit for seeking it, especially with Puerto Rico among his proposed locations. He has been matched well and kept mostly out of harm’s way. The Williams victory was a good result, although Austin had already been softened up by defeats against Carlos Adames and Hamzah Sheeraz.

Zayas would bring quicker combinations and a more polished offensive game. This could be as high as Mielnicki goes unless he shows more versatility than he has needed through much of his career.

It’s also a good fight for the Top Rank-promoted Zayas. He has the skills to beat Vito through boxing or trading, with enough firepower to make an offensive approach worth watching.

The concern is whether Xander chooses to use it. His movement and holding against Jorge Garcia Perez and Abass Baraou produced wins without consistently showing how entertaining his offense could be. Taking that same approach against Mielnicki would be a disappointing choice against an opponent he should be able to attack.

Zayas tried boxing Jaron Ennis, found little success, and eventually traded before being stopped. Vito doesn’t present the same threat. Xander should have more opportunities to plant his feet and throw combinations without facing the punishment Ennis delivered.

Eddie Hearn has proposed interim fights for both before a summer meeting. Nothing is signed, but Mielnicki has made his interest clear. If it happens, Vito gets a chance to prove his ceiling is higher than it looks, while Zayas gets an opportunity to win with some excitement.

Sports.title: Richardson Hitchins Accepts Keyshawn Davis Fight, Awaits Contract
Sports.content:
Richardson Hitchins says he agreed to face Keyshawn Davis more than a month ago, contradicting Davis’ claim that he only just agreed to their planned December bout. Hitchins states the paperwork has still not arrived.

Keyshawn has spent the week hyping up his plans for fight night. Hitchins insists nothing is real until promotional teams deliver actual contracts.

“I accepted this fight over a month ago still no contract or anything official I’m still waiting for a contract and time is fucking ticking Keyshawn,” Hitchins posted on X.

That timeline cuts directly into the narrative Davis presented online. Davis made it sound like Hitchins stalled before giving in. Hitchins argues the delay sits entirely with the business side.

“Buddy finally accepted the fight.. this fight in December, this sh*t personal. Africa, I’m on yo ass in December, and I’m gonna beat yo ass,” Davis said.

Trash talk builds interest, but the bout still needs signatures. Hitchins and Davis represent two of the elite talents around the welterweight limit. On pure ring ability, they sit above most rivals, which makes the pairing significant regardless of social media squabbling.

Hitchins controls range behind a stiff jab. He rarely surrenders clean targets. Opponents who charge him blindly spend full rounds eating counters from outside.

Davis brings fast hands, heavy body work, and sharp punch selection. He must apply disciplined pressure. Following Hitchins without cutting off the ring will cost him rounds on the scorecards.

The central tactical issue comes down to style. Keyshawn needs to impose his tempo. Hitchins aims to make opponents second-guess their timing and reset from distance. Both possess the technical sharpness to punish miscalculations.

Before strategy and tactics, promoters must produce the paperwork. Hitchins insists he signed off on the bout weeks ago. With December fast approaching, the matchup remains talk until the contracts land.

Both guys carry themselves like established pound-for-pound attractions, but neither draws genuine ticket sales or pay-per-view numbers on his own. Hitchins has an Olympic pedigree and slick defensive fundamentals, yet his style often alienates casual fans, and his biggest career win is a controversial nod over Gustavo Lemos. Keyshawn Davis has real offensive talent, but he is still largely living off Olympic silver medal hype.

Ghana News.title: Government working to address economic challenges driving youth into galamsey – Mahama
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama says the government is working to address the economic challenges driving young people into illegal mining, as part of efforts to provide alternative livelihoods and curb the menace.

He says the implementation of the New Economy Agenda by his government, which seeks to invest in job-rich sectors of the economy, is expected to create opportunities for young people who might otherwise turn to illegal mining,galamsey.

Speaking during a courtesy visit by the Western North Regional House of Chiefs at the Jubilee House, President Mahama said the government is aware of the economic circumstances pushing some young people into the activity and believes that creating alternative sources of income must complement law enforcement.

“Often, when enforcing the fight against galamsey, we find even Senior High School students in illegal mining pits,” he said.

“When you ask them why they are there, they say their fathers could not give them money to go to school, so they have come to work and earn some money. It is a major issue we need to confront.”

He said that the government’s enforcement efforts have resulted in the arrest of several young people, with hundreds awaiting trial and others on bail while their cases remained pending.

President Mahama stressed that the government must address the circumstances that lead young people into galamsey while ensuring that the law is enforced.

“The question we must ask is, what alternative do we have for them? Alongside enforcing the law against illegal mining, we must provide alternative livelihoods. That is why we are implementing the New Economy Policy,” he said.

He expressed confidence that investment in sectors capable of generating significant employment would help reduce the attraction of illegal mining.

“I believe that if we invest US$10 billion in job-rich sectors of the economy, including tourism, one of the nine pillars, it should provide alternative livelihoods for our young people and discourage them from going into galamsey,” he said.

The Government’s New Economy Policy is a planned US$10 billion investment programme aimed at moving Ghana from economic stabilisation to job creation, wealth generation and sustained economic growth.

The idea is to channel investment into productive sectors that can expand businesses, increase local production and create employment, particularly for young people.

The President also called on traditional authorities to support the fight against illegal mining, particularly in forest reserves and water bodies.

He said the National Inter-Ministerial Coordinating Committee on Illegal Mining (NAIMOS) has made efforts to tackle the menace, but some communities continued to resist the task force.

“The National Inter-Ministerial Coordinating Committee on Illegal Mining (NAIMOS) is doing a good job, but in some communities, sometimes the youth, traditional authorities and others fight back against the task force,” he said.

He further disclosed that the Minister of Finance has provided an additional GH¢400 million in the 2027 Budget to recruit more Blue Water Guards to patrol water bodies.

On efforts to protect forest reserves, he said the government has cleared all nine reserves previously classified as red zones because of extensive destruction and the danger posed by heavily armed illegal miners.

He said soldiers have been deployed to clear the affected areas and will remain stationed there to prevent illegal miners from returning.

The President also disclosed that the Goldbod has started working with the military to replant destroyed forests and reclaim degraded land.

Under the programme, bulldozers will be used to level the land for the planting of economic trees, while the Forestry Commission would support the reclamation exercise.

Ghana News.title: Domestic Capital Africa campaign targets US$600bn pension funds for SME growth
Ghana News.content:
Africa’s more than US$600 billion in pension assets could play a greater role in financing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), infrastructure, and climate solutions if investors, regulators, and policymakers address the structural barriers limiting domestic investment.

Stakeholders made the call at the official launch of the Domestic Capital Africa (DCA) campaign, organized by Impact Investing Ghana (IIGh), the Africa Impact Investing Group (AIIG), Ghana Venture Capital and Private Equity Association GVCA, the Growth Firms Alliance (GFA) and regional partners on October 8, 2026.

Held under the theme "Mobilizing African Capital for Africa’s Prosperity,” the webinar brought together pension trustees, asset managers, impact investment advisers and regulators to explore ways of directing more African savings towards productive investments on the continent.

The campaign seeks to address the disconnect between the growing pools of institutional capital available in Africa and the financing needs of businesses, particularly SMEs, which continue to face limited access to long-term, appropriately structured funding.

The Board Chair of Impact Investing Ghana, Kwabena Boamah, said the initiative offered an opportunity to bring together stakeholders to develop practical solutions for financing Africa’s development with its own resources.

“Across our continent, institutional investors manage growing pools of capital. The opportunity before us today is to harness more of these resources to finance African businesses, infrastructure, innovation, climate solutions and sustainable development,” he said.

Mr Boamah said the campaign was more than a launch, describing it as a call to action for asset owners, fund managers, entrepreneurs, policymakers, regulators, and development partners to work towards a common goal.

Closing Africa’s SME financing gap

The campaign comes against the backdrop of a significant financing gap facing African businesses despite the substantial resources held by the continent’s institutional investors.

Data presented at the launch indicate that SMEs account for 92 per cent of enterprises in Africa, employ 80 percent of the workforce and generate 70 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP).

Yet these businesses face an estimated US$331 billion financing gap, with many unable to access the patient capital needed to expand operations, invest in technology and create jobs.

At the same time, African pension funds hold more than US$600 billion in assets, while Ghana’spension assets are estimated at about US$7 billion. Less than one percent of Ghana’s pension assets is invested in alternative assets, according to the presentation.

Stakeholders believe that mobilizing even a greater share of these funds into carefully structured investments could help bridge the financing gap while supporting long-term economic growth.

Esther Ndeti, Vice Chair of the Africa Impact Investing Group, said the challenge was to create the market infrastructure, investment vehicles, policy alignment, and trust required to connect available capital with businesses and development priorities.

“Domestic capital mobilization cannot be solved by any single institution. It requires collaboration among different partners and learning from the experiences of different African markets,” she said.

Amma Lartey of Impact Investing Ghana also highlighted the importance of mobilizing domestic capital to support African businesses and development priorities.

Her contribution aligns with the campaign’s objective of connecting institutional investors with investment-ready enterprises, particularly SMEs, to expand access to long-term financing, create jobs and promote sustainable economic growth.

The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Venture Capital and Private Equity Association (GVCA), Amma Gyampo, said Africa needed to move beyond the aggregation of capital towards addressing the underlying risks that discouraged institutional investors from financing businesses.

She noted that the continent’s development challenges, including limited economic opportunities for young people, required a more deliberate approach to deploying domestic savings.

“We cannot solve some of these structural issues and crises within our borders by parking the vast majority of our retirement savings in sovereign paper. We need to evolve,” she said.

Ms Gyampo said recent developments, including the launch of the Ci Gaba Fund of Funds, had demonstrated that domestic institutional capital could be successfully aggregated to support businesses.

However, she said the next phase of the effort must focus on developing risk-sharing arrangements and investment structures that meet the requirements of pension trustees and other institutional investors.

“We are ready to invest. They keep telling us this, but they also tell us that they need to see the risk structures and the deals they can actually back,” she said.

Ci Gaba offers a model for replication

A key example highlighted at the launch was the Ci GabaFund of Funds, a US$75 million blended-finance initiative designed to mobilize Ghanaian pension capital into SMEs.

The initiative was presented as the first pension-backed fund of funds in West Africa and a potential model for other African markets seeking to channel domestic institutional savings into businesses.

Its target investment areas include agribusiness, healthcare, education, clean energy, financial technology, and enterprises led by women and young people.

The Chief Executive Officer of Ci Gaba Venture Capital Limited and founder and CEO of Savannah Impact Advisory, Hamdiya Ismaila, who manages the Ci Gaba Fund of Funds, said collaboration had been central to the initiative’s development.

She stressed that fund managers must begin by understanding the market’s needs rather than designing investment vehicles before identifying the problems they are intended to solve.

“Collaboration is very important, but you also have to start with validated market needs, not a predetermined fund vehicle,” she said.

Ms Ismaila explained that listening to pension funds and understanding their requirements had informed the design of the Ci Gaba model.

“When you understand the market and validate its needs, you can develop a structure that is fit for purpose,” she said.

She added that investor confidence would depend on demonstrating the ability to manage investments effectively and generate returns.

“Pension money is not charity. It has to be returned, and it has to be returned in style,” she said.

Stakeholders called for regulatory flexibility, technical support, catalytic funding and stronger investor coordination to mobilize domestic capital. They said lessons from the CiGaba Fund could guide similar initiatives across Africa, helping channel pension savings into businesses, job creation and sustainable economic growth while protecting investors’ returns.

The DCA campaign builds on the pioneering work of Impact Investing Ghana and the Ghana Venture Capital and Private Equity Association (GVCA), which showcased insights from Ghana’s private capital and impact investment ecosystems at the World Economic Forum in Davos earlier this year.

Ghana News.title: Women leaders’ wisdom and work deserve recognition – Mahama
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has called for greater recognition of women’s contributions to society, saying the wisdom and work of women leaders deserve to be valued.

Speaking at the World Assemblies of God Congress in Accra on Wednesday, 14 October 2026, he highlighted the critical role women of faith play in nation-building.

The President urged society to acknowledge their leadership and contributions, emphasising the importance of valuing their service.

"Let us recognise our women of faith. And let the labour that sustains so much of our congregational life, and the wisdom, gift, and leadership of our women, be heard and valued," he said.

"Because a fellowship preparing for the future must make room for all those whom God has equipped to serve," he added.

His call came during the opening of the three-day congress, which runs until 16 October under the theme, “Commissioned: One Mandate, Every Nation”. The programme includes plenary sessions, workshops and revival rallies.

The 10th Triennial World Assemblies of God Fellowship Congress marks the first time the gathering has been hosted in Africa. It brings together church leaders and ministers to discuss the Church’s mission and its role in communities worldwide.

Ahead of the event, the General Superintendent of Assemblies of God, Ghana, Rev. Stephen Yenusom Wengam, said organisers expected more than 10,000 participants from about 100 countries.

Ghana News.title: NRSA to refund surplus from auctioned vehicles of non-subscribers after deducting towing costs
Ghana News.content:
The National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) has assured motorists who have not subscribed to the mandatory towing service that any surplus from the auction of their vehicles will be refunded to them after the cost of towing has been deducted, provided they can be traced.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show, the Director General, Abraham Amaliba, said the authorities would first deduct the cost of towing the vehicle from the money raised through its sale and return any remaining amount to the owner, provided they could be traced.

“If the amount is more than what you owe us, we’ll give the rest to you. That is, if we can find you. If not, we’ll put it in a government account,” he said.

His comments followed a question from the programme’s host about whether a vehicle owner whose car had been auctioned for failing to pay towing charges would receive the balance after the authorities had recovered their costs.

In response, Mr Amaliba clarified that the auction arrangement was intended to deal with vehicles whose owners had not subscribed to the towing service and could not be reached or had failed to respond to attempts to contact them.

He said the authorities would use vehicle registration records to trace the owners and give them 21 days to come forward before proceeding with the auction.

“The reason is that there were a lot of accident cars parked at the police station. You know that. And the people never came for them,” he said.

Mr Amaliba said the proposed provision was also intended to address the growing number of accident-damaged vehicles left unclaimed at police stations across the country.

According to him, the vehicles occupy space at police stations because their owners fail to return for them, leaving the authorities with the burden of storing them.

He said the new arrangement would provide a process for recovering the cost of towing and clearing vehicles that had been abandoned for extended periods.

“I don’t know whether you are aware most of our police stations are inundated with accident cars that people have not come to claim them. This law is to help clear them,” he said.

When asked how an injured driver who had been admitted to hospital would comply with the requirement to have a vehicle removed immediately after an accident.

The NRSA director-general said the authority was considering a system that would allow road safety officials and the police to identify vehicles left on major roads and arrange for their removal, even when the owners were unable to act.

“If the vehicle is not towed, we are going to have a back room which will give us access to all the major roads in Ghana,” he said.

He explained that the proposed system would enable the authorities to identify stationary vehicles that posed a risk to other road users and intervene where necessary.

“So we can see the car parked there and we, as road safety and police, can come and remove it for you. Then later we can deal with you,” he added.

Ghana News.title: Ghana must integrate AI into mainstream education – DigiMarkt Project Board
Ghana News.content:
The management board of the DigiMarkt Project has made a strong case for the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Ghana's mainstream education curriculum, stressing that the future of work will be driven by AI and digital competencies.

According to the Board, the rapid evolution of Artificial Intelligence and digital technologies makes it imperative for Ghana to undertake deliberate and urgent reforms in its educational system to equip students with relevant skills for a fast-changing global economy.

The Ghana Coordinator for the project and Dean of the Faculty of Applied Sciences and Mathematics Education at the University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development (USTED), Prof. Yarhands Dissou Arthur, made the call at the final conference of the DigiMarkt Project.

The event, held on the theme "Transforming the Digital Future of TVET in Ghana: The Role of the DigiMarkt Project," was hosted at the USTED campus in Kumasi and marked the climax of the two-year transformative initiative.

The project, co-funded by the European Union (EU) with a total grant of €394,185, sought to strengthen digital marketing and emerging technology competencies within Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) in Ghana.

Addressing participants, Prof. Arthur warned that Artificial Intelligence is set to dominate every facet of life and industry in the next three decades, and Ghana risks being left behind if it delays its adoption.

He stressed that AI should no longer be perceived as an elective or the preserve of computer science specialists, but rather as a fundamental literacy that every student must possess, similar to reading and writing.

"In fact, AI is something that is taking over the world in the next thirty years, and we as a country cannot afford to wait until it has taken over before we begin to learn," he stated.

He therefore proposed that AI be made a common course across all public and private universities in Ghana, just like basic Information and Communication Technology (ICT).

"I will recommend that in this university and in all universities in Ghana, AI should become a common course, just like we have been learning basic ICT - learning PowerPoint, Access and all those things. Today, AI can create all those things for you, so why don't we learn how to use AI now?" Prof. Arthur stated.

Beyond the tertiary level, Prof. Arthur advocated for the early introduction of AI at the Senior High School level to build a strong foundation and digital confidence among learners before they enter tertiary institutions.

He believes such an early start will demystify AI, promote innovation, and position Ghanaian students to compete globally in an increasingly AI-driven economy.

"In fact, even in our secondary education, we need to include it in our curriculum because it is what is ruling the world. But the question we need to ask ourselves is, how must we teach AI?"

Prof. Arthur noted that the real debate should not be about whether AI should be adopted, but about ensuring its responsible application. He warned against creating panic and imposing outright bans on AI in schools, emphasizing that responsible usage comes only through education and training.

"We need to teach students how to make responsible use of AI. And to be able to teach them how to use it responsibly, teachers and instructors in the various schools must first learn how to use it themselves," he stressed.

He disclosed that the University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development (USTED), Cape Coast Technical University, and Bolgatanga Technical University (BTU), through the DigiMarkt Project and with support from the European Commission, have established a state-of-the-art AI and digital marketing laboratory to spearhead the initiative.

"This laboratory we have established is for that purpose. If you are a secondary school and you want your teachers to be well-trained in the use of AI, including its application in teaching, you can come here. We can agree on terms and conditions and, in the interest of sustaining the project, offer you something that will be of great value to your school," he explained.

The Dean added that lecturers at USTED are already benefiting from the programme, using AI to develop lecture notes, prepare PowerPoint presentations and compile research materials.

Drawing a direct link between AI education and Ghana's unemployment crisis, Prof. Arthur explained that the DigiMarkt Project was originally conceived to enhance the employability of TVET graduates within the digital economy.

"We are a TVET university, and it has always been said that TVET is the way to go when we talk about unemployment. Unemployment in this country is high, and one of the ways we can address it is to provide our students with the requisite technical education and training," he stated.

He argued that technical skills alone are no longer sufficient in a competitive market, and that graduates must also be equipped with the capacity to sell their skills and products.

According to him, the digital transformation agenda extends beyond TVET institutions, as every sector of the economy now requires digital competence to thrive.

Looking beyond the classroom, Prof. Arthur further underscored how AI and digital marketing could serve as a bridge connecting Ghanaian youth to opportunities in the global job market.

He disclosed ongoing engagements with German partners under the DigiMarkt Project to establish remote work pipelines for top-performing trainees, particularly in high-demand areas such as data analytics, digital marketing and cybersecurity.

He said the initiative, if successful, would allow skilled Ghanaian youth to work remotely for international companies without necessarily leaving the country, thereby curbing brain drain while earning foreign income.

He concluded with a strong appeal to policymakers, educators and parents to embrace the AI revolution rather than resist it.

"AI is taking over, and we need to be fast; otherwise, the world will leave us behind," he warned.

Build Networks, Leapfrog Mistakes

The Project Coordinator of the DigiMarkt Project, Dr. Jonathan Barth, has urged Ghanaians and Africans not to copy every step Europe took in its digital and Artificial Intelligence journey.

According to him, not everything that works for Europe is necessarily good for African countries.

Dr. Barth explained that while Europe offers valuable lessons in digital transformation, Africa must contextualise those lessons to suit its own realities, challenges and opportunities.

He urged stakeholders to build the next approach together, build strong networks and leapfrog past the mistakes made by developed economies.

He emphasised the need for collaboration, sharing of methods, challenging of ideas and retaining only what works for Ghana and the continent.

Dr. Barth said this collaborative approach is key to ensuring that the Digital Technical and Vocational Education and Training (DigiMarkt) initiative truly empowers training providers and learners with relevant skills in digital marketing, Artificial Intelligence and cybersecurity, as a sustainable strategy to bridge the skills gap and tackle youth unemployment in Ghana.

The final conference brought together academics, students, industry players and international partners to demonstrate how AI-powered digital marketing tools can transform skills training, enhance entrepreneurship, create sustainable jobs for Ghanaian youth and chart a sustainable path for its outcomes beyond the funding period.

The project, implemented by a consortium of partners from Ghana, Germany and Slovakia, is aimed at repositioning Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) for the digital age.

It seeks to equip TVET students and staff with relevant skills in digital marketing, Artificial Intelligence, and cybersecurity as a strategy to bridge the skills gap and tackle youth unemployment.

Ghana News.title: Armwrestling: Ghana unveils World Armwrestling Championship squad, appeals for travel support
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Armwrestling Federation has unveiled a formidable squad for the upcoming World Armwrestling Championship in New Delhi, India, while appealing to corporate Ghana, government institutions, philanthropists and sports enthusiasts to support the team's travel and participation.

The squad, comprising some of the country's most accomplished Armwrestlers, is expected to fly Ghana's flag at the global competition as the team targets medals and seeks to consolidate the country's growing reputation as a force in international armwrestling.

Leading the contingent are world-class performers Mabel Yeboah-60kg, Blessed Abeka Nunoo – 65kg and Grace Minta – 89kg, who have distinguished themselves through their performances at international competitions. They are joined by Florence Boakye – 110+kg, Afia Kumah – 110+kg and Comfort Dunyo – 60kg, who are masters in the women's category.

The men's contingent includes Edward Asamoah Yamoah, Haruna Tahiru, Godwin Sackey, Daniel Acquah, Charles Osei Asibey Jr., Henry Otoo and Asinu Dodzie, all expected to bring their strength, experience and competitive spirit to the championship.

Ghana's participation is particularly significant given the country's impressive progress in the sport over the years, with its athletes making their mark at continental and world competitions. The national team has consistently demonstrated its potential to challenge the world's best, earning recognition for Ghana on the international sporting stage.

However, despite the team's ambition and preparations, securing the necessary financial resources to facilitate the trip remains a major concern. The Federation is therefore appealing to corporate institutions, government agencies, sports-loving individuals and other stakeholders to support the squad's travel and participation.

The appeal comes at a crucial time, with the Federation seeking to ensure that financial constraints do not prevent the selected athletes from representing their country at the prestigious championship.

Support from the private sector and other well-meaning Ghanaians would provide an important boost to the team's campaign while offering sponsors an opportunity to associate their brands with a sport that continues to deliver results and enhance Ghana's international sporting profile.

The Ghana Armwrestling Federation has, over the years, built a reputation for developing athletes capable of competing at the highest level, while creating opportunities for talent development, employment and national pride.

The Federation is hopeful that the latest appeal will attract the necessary support to enable the team to travel to India and compete against the world's best armwrestlers.

The 2026 World Armwrestling Championship is scheduled for India from October 26 to November 7, 2026.

Ghana News.title: NPRA cites pensions college, data bank to justify 10-storey building project
Ghana News.content:
The National Pensions Regulatory Authority (NPRA) has defended plans to construct a 10-storey building under the second phase of its office project, citing plans to establish a pensions college and a data bank for the pensions industry.

A representative of the authority, appearing before a Parliament's Public Accounts Committee, said the proposed facilities would support training for industry professionals and other stakeholders, as well as provide a central repository for data across the pensions industry.

“Embedded in Phase Two is going to be a pensions college that will be training the industry and other stakeholders. And then there is also going to be a data bank that will house the data for the entire industry,” he said.

The explanation followed questions from the chairperson, Abena Osei-Asare, about the need for the additional 10-storey structure and the authority's plans to finance the project.

The committee member challenged the need for such a large building, arguing that data storage did not require extensive physical space, and questioned how the authority intended to repay the loan.

The NPRA representative disclosed that the authority had planned to raise GH¢500 million for the project but had accessed GH¢200 million in 2025.

Asked whether the GH¢200 million would be sufficient to complete Phase Two, the representative answered in the negative.

The committee chair also sought clarification on whether the repayment would come from the authority's internally generated revenue or whether the government would bear the cost.

In response, the representative said the NPRA would repay the loan using its own resources.

The authority further explained that the design of the building was influenced by requirements governing construction along the stretch where its offices are located.

According to the representative, "The authority initially planned a four-storey structure because it lacked the funds to construct a 10-storey building at the time. "The second phase would subsequently meet the height requirement for the area.

Ghana News.title: 16 arrested as security team recovers guns, ammunition at Gbane mining site
Ghana News.content:
The Upper East Regional Police Command has arrested 16 suspects and recovered firearms, ammunition, suspected narcotic substances, and other items during a security operation at the Gbane mining site in the Talensi District.

The operation, carried out on Tuesday, October 13, involved personnel from the National Police Intelligence Directorate, the Upper East Regional Police Intelligence Directorate, the Special Operations Team, known as Black Cobra, and the Tongo District Police Command.

According to a statement issued by the Upper East Regional Police Command on Wednesday, October 14, 10 suspects were arrested during the police operation, while a military team from the 11 Mechanised Battalion arrested six additional suspects in a related operation.

The arrests form part of efforts to maintain security and public order in the area.

The police recovered 104 live AA cartridges, 37 wraps of suspected Indian hemp, 12 mobile phones and seven security uniforms bearing the name Nalamtaaba.

Other items seized included seven body armours, two pepper sprays, four torch lights, a knife, a weapon bag and a set of walkie-talkies.

In a related development, the military team from the 11 Mechanised Battalion arrested six more suspects and recovered two pump-action guns and 105 live AA cartridges.

The six suspects, together with the items seized, were subsequently handed over to the police in Bolgatanga for further investigation.

The recoveries bring the total number of suspects arrested in the two operations to 16.

The Upper East Regional Police Command said patrols were continuing in communities around the mining site to maintain peace and order.

The 16 suspects remain in police custody and are assisting with investigations. They are expected to be brought before the court.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: What led Manchester United’s Martinez to meltdown in Madrid – all to know
World.content:
Amid Premier and Champions League woes, Man United players and fans ponder how preseason optimism has turned to despair.

Share What led Manchester United’s Martinez to meltdown in Madrid – all to know on social media

Manchester United’s season plunged to a new low on Tuesday.

A third-place finish last season after a late charge under manager Michael Carrick gave Manchester United fans reasons to dream of a bright 2026-27 campaign.

But just two months in, hopes of a title charge or a top-four finish seem out of reach, with United registering their worst start to a football season in 40 years.

Their latest defeat – a 2-0 reverse at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League – is the third in five winless matches, and promoted centre-back Lisandro Martinez to blast the club’s board for a lack of support for the squad.

So where did it all go wrong for Man United? Al Jazeera explains:

A shambolic start to the Premier League season

When United lost to newly-promoted Hull City on the opening day of the top-flight season, the humiliating result gave supporters a glimpse of the disaster that would follow.

Of their nine matches across all competitions to date, United have won just two: August’s come-from-behind victory at home over Ipswich Town in the league, and the Champions League thrashing of Azerbaijani club Sabah last month.

A controversial Manchester derby defeat to Man City left a bitter taste, but the team had no excuses when they suffered a third-round League Cup exit to fellow league side Brighton & Hove Albion.

Then came identical 1-1 draws with Fulham and Tottenham Hotspur, two teams that are in the relegation zone.

The issues in United’s squad spread across departments, with the team failing to show any real urgency.



Sitting in 12th place, United’s points tally of six is their lowest total after six games since 1986.

Under-fire Carrick has plenty to ponder in latest Man Utd mess

United avoided a crisis at Craven Cottage in their last league game before the extended international break with a draw, needing a late equaliser to avoid a third consecutive defeat.

That dispiriting performance drew harsh words from pundits and ex-players, including Gary Neville, who particularly criticised the team’s second-half effort, calling it “absolutely pathetic”.

United boss Carrick, though, struck a defiant tone, trying his best to silence the noise surrounding one of the biggest clubs in world football.

“It’s not been ideal. It was always going to come at some point, and it’s come at the start of the season,” Carrick said.

The doom and gloom continued when United blew a late lead against 10-man Tottenham to draw 1-1 at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Carrick’s men were booed off at half-time and at the end of the match after a Tottenham side that began the day bottom of the table dominated for large spells.

“Obviously, it hurts, you know, it hurts a lot,” said Carrick, addressing the boos.

“It’s not nice to go through, but sometimes you have to go through it. That’s how it is, you know. It’s coming from a good place, really, and so I understand it.”

The 45-year-old former United midfielder was expected to build on last season’s optimism during his spell as interim boss. But having hauled United from the wreckage of Ruben Amorim’s reign, Carrick is in danger of losing his way in his first season as permanent boss.

Did Man United’s board fall short in their summer signings?

In the summer transfer window, United brought in three talented midfielders: Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos, and Youri Tielemans, as well as a backup goalkeeper, Karl Darlow. That cost them 155 million British pounds ($204m) and raised the question: should United have spent more?

The club’s decision not to buy an established left-back and a reliable striker left unresolved gaps in the squad, forcing the team to rely on makeshift options.

This was seemingly at the heart of Martinez’s Tuesday tirade in the Spanish capital.

“I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox], I have to be honest, as players we have to do more. But it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for these kinds of nights,” the Argentina international defender said.

What woes surround JJ Gabriel at Man United?

Away from the first team, transfer mania made news in the youth setup, but for the wrong reasons.



JJ Gabriel, widely considered one of football’s most exciting youth prospects, said he wants to leave the club and handed in a letter of de-registration. However, British media reported the club has no intention of granting that request and is hopeful a resolution can be found.

Recipient of the Premier League under-18 player of the year award last term, the promising winger has since drawn the interest of Europe’s top clubs such as Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich.

Off the pitch, Man United’s financial losses mount

Last month, United reported that their annual net loss increased by almost one third to 43 million pounds ($57m) despite record-breaking revenues.

The Old Trafford club reported 677.6 million pounds ($890.7m) in revenue in the year to June 30, up 1.7 percent.

However, the club announced a seventh straight annual loss after taxes as co-owner Jim Ratcliffe’s cuts to operating costs offset contractual payments to sacked manager Amorim and a big increase in loan repayments.

The club’s debt remains over one billion pounds ($1.3bn) despite record revenues that are unable to prevent losses at the UK football side.

British billionaire Ratcliffe has overseen wide-ranging, and often unpopular, cost-cutting measures, including widespread job cuts and increased ticket prices, after completing a deal to buy a minority stake in the club in February 2024.

Ratcliffe’s fallout with Man United’s fans

Away from football, Ratcliffe has also sparked controversy with his latest comments about immigration, which prompted Manchester United’s Muslim Supporters’ Club (MUMSC) to call for his resignation.

In February, the 73-year-old Ratcliffe said the United Kingdom had been “colonised by immigrants” and later apologised if he offended anyone. He doubled down on those comments in a BBC interview, saying the country “is on the slide” because of it.

The MUMSC condemned Ratcliffe’s words earlier in the year and once again spoke out against his latest comments, describing them as “deeply disappointing”.

It wasn’t the first time the United faithful expressed their frustration – before losing to Man City, fans protested against the current ownership with a banner that read “the way you treat us is a disgrace”.

World.title: Judge extends White House access for US media outlets amid Trump standoff
World.content:
CNN, MS Now and Politico can continue to access White House as judge maintains Trump’s ban likely illegal.

A federal judge has extended access to several media organisations that United States President Donald Trump had sought to ban from the White House.

US District Judge Timothy Kelly said Trump likely broke the law in banning journalists from CNN, MS Now and Politico from attending White House briefings.

The decision, published late Tuesday, expands on an emergency order issued by Kelly on September 24 that temporarily reinstated access to organisations. It said Trump likely discriminated against the news organisations based on their viewpoints, in violation of the First Amendment of the US Constitution.

He wrote that Trump’s “announcement of the ban and later remarks explaining the reason for it make this a straightforward conclusion: President Trump likely banned Plaintiffs from the White House because he believes that their reporting is generally inaccurate and biased against him”.

In announcing the ban, Trump had said the organisations “shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States”.

The Department of Justice subsequently said the reporters’ White House passes were revoked on national security grounds.

In his ruling, Kelly rejected the claim.

“First, there is no evidence in the record that President Trump made the decision to revoke Plaintiffs’ hard passes on national security grounds from the get-go, nor at any time has he directly stated that national security was the reason for his decision,” he wrote.



The latest order stands until Kelly, who was appointed by Trump during the president’s first term, makes a final determination in the case, or until an appeals court steps in.

Trump has long been a critic of legacy US media and has previously sought to restrict access to certain organisations.

He has also lodged rhetorical attacks on individual reporters both in person and on social media, while launching an array of lawsuits against media companies.

Speaking during an October 8 hearing, Theodore Boutrous, a lawyer for the three banned organisations, said Trump was seeking to “coerce better coverage”.

The Freedom of the Press Foundation was among the groups cheering the latest court ruling.

“But this fight is far from over,” senior adviser for advocacy Caitlin Vogus said in a statement.

“We have every reason to expect the administration will appeal Kelly’s latest order and also continue to prevent CNN and Politico from participating in pool coverage of the president,” she said. “Trump must not be allowed to trample on fundamental First Amendment protections by handpicking his press corps or turning pool duties into a reward for favorable coverage.”

World.title: Pope Leo recovering well after cancer surgery, Vatican says
World.content:
