The story is set in Muwonleru, a village dominated by Isawuru, a powerful herbalist whose spiritual influence keeps the community in fear.

It centres on the confrontation between Christian faith and traditional spiritual power after evangelists attempt to take the gospel to the village.

Isawuru, portrayed by Mr Bamiloye in the original production, became one of the filmmaker’s most recognisable characters.

The film’s treatment of spiritual warfare, deliverance, faith and the triumph of divine power over evil also became a defining feature of subsequent Mount Zion productions.

READ ALSO: Gbenga Adeyinka to end Laffmattazz tour in Lagos

Return after 33 years

More than three decades later, the story has been reimagined for a new generation in Agbara Nla: The Return, with Mr Bamiloye reprising his role as Isawuru.

Damilola Mike-Bamiloye, Joshua “Jay Mikee” Mike-Bamiloye, and Chris Odeh produced it. Mohammed Sedik and Damilola Mike-Bamiloye are credited as co-producers.

Mount Zion Film Productions, Circuits, and Sozo Films produced it, while Nile Entertainment handles distribution.

The cast includes Philip Olubakin as Olaboye, Damilola Mike-Bamiloye as Kola, and Aanu Kolade Abiodun as Bose. Gloria Mike-Bamiloye, Remilekun Mosiko, and David Kola Okeowo also feature in the film.

World.title: FCT judicial committee flouted procurement law, financial regulations in N866.5m contract awards – Audit report
World.content:
The latest federal audit has revealed a series of infractions by the Judicial Service Committee of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT JSC), Abuja, in awarding contracts worth about N866.5 million in 2023.

The report revealed the FCT JSC’s rampant disregard for procurement law, financial regulations and federal government’s policy directives.

According to the just released 2024 report of the Office of the Auditor-General of the Federation (OAuGF), the infractions stemmed from weaknesses in the judicial committee’s internal control system.

In some instances, the auditor general found no evidence of work done for the payments the FCT JSC made to contractors. In other cases, there were no documents to show that the committee awarded contracts to qualified contractors.

According to the report, many of the flagged infractions possibly resulted in the loss or diversion of public funds channelled into the contracts.

The FCT JSC is an institution of the judiciary established by the Nigerian constitution, to oversee judicial appointments, promotion, and discipline, as well as safeguard both the independence of the judiciary and the administration of justice in FCT courts.

One of its key responsibilities is recommending qualified lawyers for appointment to the bench, after conducting, what it called, rigorous evaluation of professional qualifications and experience, background and integrity checks, and consultation with relevant stakeholders.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The body, which its equivalent exists across Nigeria’s 36 states and at the federal level as the Federal Judicial Service Commission, is also mandated to ensure “high standards of ethical conduct and professional integrity.”

Key violations

But the new 2024 audit report on the 2023 finances of federal ministries, departments and agencies revealed that the FCT JSC, statutorily chaired by the Chief Judge of the FCT High Court and run day-to-day by an executive secretary, hardly played by the rules in a series of contract awards. Justice Husseini Baba-Yusuf, the incumbent chief judge of the FCT High Court and chair of the FCT JSC, has served in those roles since 2021.

The audit report identified five contracts aggregately worth N866.5 million with their litany of issues and the risks they pose to public funds.

The issues include award of a contract worth N302.3 million to non-accredited local manufacturers or assemblers, irregularities in the award of contracts valued at N192.1 million, and infractions in the award of renovation contracts worth N174.2 million.

The two other issues are award of N144.2 million worth of contract and payment to inactive companies without due diligence and splitting of N57.3 million contracts to circumvent procurement/ approval threshold.

The queried contracts summed up to N866.5 million in monetary value. The auditor general’said their handlings by the JSC raised concerns of possible supply of substandard products, diversion of public funds, loss of public funds, award of contracts to unqualified contractors, possible insider dealing and payments for fictitious transactions.

Meanwhile, this amount does not include the N112.6 million in salary vouchers flagged by the audit report as the sixth issue uncovered in the JSC’s financial records for 2023.

All told, the N866.5 million in questionable contract disbursements, coupled with N112.6 million in queried payroll entries, brings the total unaccounted sum at the FCT JSC to roughly N979.1 million for 2023.

The report, titled Annual Report on Non-Compliance/Internal Control Weaknesses in Ministries, Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government of Nigeria for 2024, was submitted by Auditor-General of the Federation (AuGF) Shaakaa Chira to the National Assembly on 17 July.

Volume II of the report covers a section on judiciary institutions, presenting findings on the infractions by the JSC of the FCT for the period between 1 January and 31 December 2023. The Code of Conduct Tribunal is the only other body whose infractions for the year under reference were captured in the section.

The report revealed that the FCT JSC failed to respond to queries on the issues raised.

Award of contract to non-accredited/local assemblers

The audit report flagged a purchase of “motor vehicle” for N302.3 million by the JSC in 2023. The type or the make of the vehicle was not disclosed in the report.

However, it revealed that the committee procured and made payment for the supply of the motor vehicle to contractors “who were not among the list of accredited local manufacturers/assemblers in Nigeria for the procurement of federal government vehicles.”

This action, according to the report, flouted the provisions of the Financial Regulations 2009 and “does not encourage local manufacturer/industrialisation in Nigeria.”

Paragraph 2305 of the Financial Regulations (2009) referenced in the report states, “As much as it is practicable, goods must be purchased from reputable manufacturers or their accredited agents. When goods are obtained through an agent, the procuring officer will satisfy himself that the goods are authentic.”

The report added that JSC’s action infringed on paragraph 1 of the Executive Order No. 3 (2017) which states, “All Ministries Department and Agencies (MDAs) of the FGN shall grant preference to local manufacturers of goods and service providers in their procurement of goods and services.”

It similarly cited paragraph 1 of the Establishment Circular Ref. No. NADDC.NAIDP/S.137/1/36 dated 17 March 2023, which provided an updated list of accredited local manufacturers/assemblers in Nigeria, for the procurement of federal government vehicles.

The report regarded the flouting of the financial regulations and policy documents as “anomalies” that possibly arose from the “weaknesses in the internal control system” at the JSC of the FCT.

These, according to the report, exposed the government to the risks of “supply of sub-standard vehicles” and “diversion of public funds.”

Award of N192 million without documents

The report also revealed a payment of over N192 million to companies without supporting documents showing the contractors’ qualifications.

The report found that seven vouchers totalling over N192 million were raised and the money was paid in favour of different companies for the provision of services and supply of goods to the JSC.

But the JSC failed to present any documentary evidence such as tax clearance certificate, Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) certificate of registration, PenCom certificate, Industrial Training Fund certificate, Nigeria Social Industrial Trust Fund certificate, among others, to show that the contractors were qualified bidders.

This lack of compliance, according to the audit report, contravenes Section 16(7) of the Public Procurement Act 2007, which states that “The procuring entity may require a bidder to provide documentary evidence or other information it considers necessary as proof that the bidder is qualified in accordance with this Act and the solicitation documents and for this purpose any such requirements shall apply equally to all bidders.”

No , no bid documents submitted for N174.2 million contract

Similarly, the JSC awarded contracts worth over N174.2 million to four contractors for renovations and rehabilitation without any s, bid documents submitted, or a detailed bid evaluation report, said the account general of the federation’s report.

Also according to the report, the contractors’ files lacked information about the contractors, pictorial evidence of the work done, or proof that the contractors had been filing their annual tax returns with the Federal Inland Revenue Service (now the National Revenue Service) and that “the company was inactive on the CAC dashboard.”

There was also no evidence of procurement due process as the JSC could not produce relevant documents such as s carried out in two national dailies, bid documents submitted, and detailed bid evaluation report.

The committee, by its actions or omissions, the audit report said, violated section 24(1) of the Public Procurement Act 2007 and paragraph 2907 (i) of the Financial Regulations.

Section 24(1) of the Public Procurement Act provides that “Except as provided by this Act, all procurements of goods and works by all procuring entities shall be by way of open competitive bidding.”

Paragraph 2907(i) of the Financial Regulations (FR) (2009), which the audit report said the JSC also flouted, states, “To ensure transparency and accountability, achievement of value for money, economy and efficiency, and equity and fairness, all procurements falling within the Bureau’s thresholds shall be by way of Open Competitive Bidding.”

The report again attributed the anomalies to weaknesses in the internal control system at the JSC.

It added that these pose the risks possible of insider dealing – using internal information to unfairly win public contracts. It also said the funds meant for the contracts could be diverted.

Award of N144 million to companies with inactive CAC and FIRS status

The report also flagged the JSC’s contracts worth over N144 million awarded to eight companies with inactive status on both CAC and FIRS portals.

This violates Section 16(5) and (6) of the PPA, which stipulate that “A supplier, contractor or service provider may be a natural person, a legal person or a combination of the two….”

The audit report also referenced Section 16(6) of the PPA (2007) states, “All bidders in addition to requirements contained in any solicitation documents shall (b) possess the legal capacity to enter into the procurement contract: (c) not be in receivership, the subject of any form of insolvency or bankruptcy proceedings or the subject of any form of winding up petition proceedings; (d) not have fulfilled all its obligations to pay taxes, pensions and social security contributions.”

The auditor general said the infractions, attributable to weak internal control, posed the risk of loss of public funds and diversion of public funds.

Contract splitting

The audit also found that the JSC unduly split a N53.6 million worth contract for the supply of computers and laptops into six units.

It observed that the contract was for the supply of the same products and ought to have been awarded as a single contract, but was rather split into six at a price that fell within the approval threshold of the executive secretary.

It added that all six smaller contracts were awarded about the same period in 2023, pointing out that the splitting enabled the secretary to circumvent tenders’ procedures.

Also, the JSC failed to provide documents showing the distribution of the computers/laptops, records of officers to whom they were issued, and details of their respective locations or user departments.

Section 20(2) of the PPA cited as a legal provision the transactions breached, states, “The accounting officer of every procuring entity shall have overall responsibility for the planning of, organisation of tenders, evaluation of tenders and execution of all procurements and in particular shall be responsible for… (e) ensuring that no reduction of values or splitting of procurements is carried out such as to evade the use of the appropriate procurement method.”

The report said the “anomalies could be attributed to weaknesses in the internal control system.”

It added that these transactions posed the risks of payments for “fictitious transactions” and diversion of public funds.

Suspicious N112.6 million salary vouchers

The report also faulted the committee for failing to present 93 salary vouchers totalling over N112.6 million, creating the risk of payments to non-existent staff members and a contravention of paragraph 601 of the Financial Regulations.

This provision mandates that “All payment entries in the cash book/accounts shall be vouched for on one of the prescribed treasury forms. Vouchers shall be made out in favour of the person or persons to whom the money is actually due. Under no circumstances shall a cheque be raised or cash paid for services for which a voucher has not been raised.”

No response from FCT JSC, audits’ recommendations

According to the audit report, the committee failed to respond to queries on any of the six infractions.

Therefore, the auditor general recommended that the Secretary of the FCT JSC, Omolola Akindele, account for all the funds, recover and remit them to the treasury and forward the evidence to the Public Accounts Committees of the National Assembly.

Failure to comply attracts sanctions, the report stated.

World.title: 2027: ‘We’ll dance back to Aso Rock’ —  Adeleke vows to lead movement for Tinubu’s re-election
World.content:
Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has urged Nigerians to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, expressing confidence that the president will secure a second term in the 2027 general election.

Adeleke spoke on Wednesday at the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja, where he pledged to mobilise support for Tinubu’s return to Aso Rock.

The governor, who recently aligned with the APC, said he could already feel victory coming for the president, adding that he was ready to lead the campaign movement.

“I can feel the victory coming in 2027. Nobody can stop this movement. I’m ready to lead this movement,” Adeleke said.

Known for his dancing style at public events, the governor said the campaign would be marked by celebration as Tinubu’s supporters worked towards securing his re-election.

“We’re going to sing, we’re going to dance all the way back to Aso Rock,” he said.

Adeleke also urged Nigerians to give Tinubu more time to implement his reforms, acknowledging the difficulties associated with the president’s policies.

“Everybody that is thinking otherwise, we must give our father, the President of this nation, time to work for his reforms to work. It’s not easy,” he said.

The governor said his decision to join the campaign was driven by a desire for action rather than excessive political rhetoric.

“That is why I am here to throw my weight because we want action, not too much talking. We don’t have time; work has begun. I’ve already started mine,” he said.

Adeleke called on Tinubu’s supporters across the country to intensify their efforts to secure a second term for the president, saying it would allow him to complete his programmes.

“From every corner, let us rise and make sure our president comes back for a second term so he can come back and complete his good work,” the governor said.

World.title: NASU demands immediate payment of workers’ entitlements
World.content:
By Victor Ahiuma-Young

ABUJA — The Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU) has demanded the immediate payment of outstanding salaries, promotion arrears, wage awards, pensions, gratuities and other benefits owed to workers and retirees.

NASU President, Dr Makolo Hassan, made the demand during the union’s ongoing National Executive Council (NEC) meeting in Abuja, expressing concern over what he described as the denial and delay of workers’ legitimate entitlements.

Hassan said the continued withholding of workers’ benefits was incompatible with the principles of fairness, dignity and social justice.

He said the union would continue to press for the settlement of outstanding entitlements, insisting that workers deserved fair treatment and protection from exploitative employment practices.

“We cannot claim to uphold the principles of decent work while workers are denied their hard-earned salaries, promotions, wage awards, pensions, gratuities and other legitimate entitlements,” he said.

The NASU president also rejected the increasing casualisation of labour and the use of contract employment arrangements which, according to him, deprive workers of job security, fair remuneration, dignity and legitimate benefits.

He described such practices as unjust and contrary to the principles of social justice and decent work.

“We shall remain resolute and unrelenting in our demand for equal pay for work of equal value, the regularisation of eligible casual and contract workers, the protection of workers’ rights and the immediate payment of all outstanding entitlements,” Hassan said.

The union’s demands come amid rising living costs, which Hassan said had significantly eroded workers’ purchasing power and made it increasingly difficult for many households to meet their basic needs.

He cited rising petrol prices and the cost of food, transportation, housing, electricity, healthcare and other essential commodities as factors worsening the financial pressure on workers.

“With the increase in the pump prices of petroleum products, the astronomical rise in the cost of food, transportation, housing, electricity, healthcare and other essential commodities, the current Minimum Wage has effectively become a slave wage that can no longer sustain Nigerian workers and their families,” he said.

Hassan extended the union’s concerns to retirees, insisting that workers’ dignity and welfare should not end upon retirement after years of service to their institutions and the country.

He lamented the hardship caused by unpaid gratuities, delayed pensions and prolonged verification exercises, arguing that retirees deserved financial security after decades of service.

“The dignity of labour must not end on the day a worker retires. After decades of service to our industries, institutions and nation, no retiree should be condemned to endless verification exercises, unpaid gratuities, delayed pensions or poverty in old age,” he said.

The NASU president consequently called for the prompt payment of pensions and gratuities, the settlement of outstanding liabilities to retirees and stronger safeguards for pension funds.

“We therefore demand the prompt payment of pensions and gratuities, the transparent and secure management of pension funds, the settlement of all outstanding liabilities to retirees, and periodic pension increases that reflect inflation, the cost of living and general wage reviews,” Hassan added.

World.title: FIFA to offer members $6.35-billion development fund windfall
World.content:
(Photo by OZAN KOSE / AFP)

Football’s world governing body FIFA is planning to set up a $6.35-billion development fund for the next four years, AFP learned Wednesday from a source close to the matter.

The plan is due to be approved at its Council meeting on Thursday in Zurich, where FIFA president Gianni Infantino and the 36 other members of the federation’s executive will gather.

To finance this development fund for the 2026–2030 period, which would allow money to be distributed to FIFA’s 211 federations as well as to the regional confederations, it would draw in part on its financial reserves after a commercially triumphant 2026 World Cup.

The plan, first revealed by the Associated Press, would allow for the payment of $25 million to each of its 211 member federations.

This is far more than the $10 million called for by two of Infantino’s chief critics, Aleksander Ceferin, the boss of the European confederation UEFA, and Victor Montagliani, the head of CONCACAF, the confederation of North and Central America and the Caribbean.

Thursday’s gathering is the first such meeting since April 28, and comes amid a crisis in the governance of world football, following Infantino’s announcement this summer of his desire to open FIFA’s premium competitions such as the World to private investors.

That plan was ultimately abandoned in the face of widespread criticism from the football world, with a rebellion led by UEFA, CONCACAF, and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).

At the end of September, Infantino launched a consultation process with the federations to reform how the global body operates, announcing that the first proposals could be examined as early as Thursday’s Council meeting.

The 56-year-old, who has headed FIFA since 2016, is running for re-election in March 2027.

His opponents have so far failed to agree on a candidate.

Ceferin has chosen to stand for a new term at the helm of UEFA and, according to several media outlets, Montagliani is expected to do the same at CONCACAF.

The deadline for submitting candidacies is November 18.

World.title: Makinde-Daura campaign council inaugurates North-Central zone coordinators
World.content:
Gov Seyi Makinde

The Director-General of Makinde-Daura Campaign Organisation Mr Felix Hyat, on Wednesday inaugurated North-Central zone coordinators with a charge on them to take message of the party to the grassroots.

Hyat said politics is inherently local and its success depends on localised mobilisation of people in various polling units.

“The journey begins at the polling units and moves to the ward headquarters, local government headquarters, state headquarters and ultimately, the national level. Your work as coordinators must be localised,” Hyat stated.

He emphasised that their mandate required sharing the message of the Presidential Candidate, Gov. Seyi Makinde, with every citizens across the country.

​Hyat described the Makinde-Daura ticket as a fantastic and unprecedented political pairing, urging all coordinators to count themselves as fortunate to participate in the mission.

He reminded them that the candidate is contested on a structured party platform, noting that party chairmen, candidates and campaign managers formed the critical stakeholders for electoral victory.

He noted that collective integration was the only way to move mountains and ensure the candidate’s name became a household fixture in every nook and cranny of the North-Central zone and Nigeria at large.

The D-G of the campaign organisation acknowledged that the party was racing against time but urged members to remain fully committed and prepared to make the necessary personal sacrifices.

He highlighted the pivotal role of polling unit managers and agents and warned that a campaign’s fate ultimately rested in the hands of its frontline agents, which made careful selection vital.

Hyat encouraged party members to maintain high morale, avoid discouragement and leverage internal dialogue to resolve any grievances.

He expressed absolute confidence that through collective sacrifice and grassroots mobilisation, the movement would successfully rescue Nigeria when voters head to the polls on Jan. 16, 2027.

Dr Tony Aziegbemi, Deputy Director of Operations for the campaign organisation, redefined the state coordinators as ‘field commanders’ tasked with driving the campaign’s core message to every household across the nation.

Aziegbemi explained that the campaign platform rested on four intertwined pillars: the economy, education, security and the socio-political system.

He decried the incumbent administration’s economic policies, citing the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) figures indicating that 35 million Nigerians went to bed hungry every night due to poorly planned decisions like fuel subsidy removal and currency floating.

​”We need to reach at least 15 million of those hungry people who go to bed hungry every night.

“And it is not because they are lazy; it is because of the lack of logic and common sense in the economic policies of this administration,” Aziegbemi stated.

Aziegbemi advised field coordinators to use provided templates to compile house-to-house canvassers and polling unit agents, giving them a strict two-week deadline to complete both lists.

Hajiya Inna Ciroma, Deputy Director of Administration for the campaign organisation, emphasised the disproportionate suffering of Nigerian women under current economic and security crises.

She noted that maternal anxiety ran high due to pervasive insecurity and the struggles of accessing quality education and economic survival for their children.

​”Therefore, Nigerian women, I am pleading with each and every one of us to come together; we should forget about our political differences, our religious difference, our zonal differences and think about some budget that will move this country forward,” she urged.

She appealed for broader support to reset Nigeria, praising the leadership qualities of the Makinde-Daura ticket.

(NAN)

World.title: How to check if your phone is approved by NCC to avoid being blocked
World.content:
Nigerians can now check whether their phones are approved by the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) for use on local mobile networks by dialling *315# or visiting the Commission’s official Device Checker website.



The Commission said the initiative formed part of an enhanced Type Approval Compliance framework that took effect on October 7, 2026, aimed at protecting consumers, safeguarding telecommunications networks and ensuring that devices sold and used in Nigeria meet the required technical standards.

“Type Approval is not merely a regulatory requirement. It is a vital mechanism for protecting consumers, safeguarding network performance and preserving confidence in Nigeria’s digital economy,” the Director of Technical Standards and Network Integrity, Edoyemi Ogoh, said at a news conference on the Commission’s Technical Standards and Network Integrity initiatives in Abuja on Tuesday,

Meanwhile, if you are planning to buy a new or fairly used phone, here is how to check its status before paying for it:

How to check if your phone is approved by NCC

Follow these steps to verify your device:

*Step 1: Dial *315#

Open the phone’s dialler and enter *315# to access the NCC Device Checker service. Follow the instructions displayed on your screen.

Step 2: Visit the NCC Device Checker website

You can also visit the Commission’s official portal at www.ncc.gov.ng/devicechecker to access the verification service.

Step 3: Get the phone’s IMEI number if required

If you want to check a phone other than the one you are currently using, you may need its 15-digit International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number.

To find the number, dial *#06# on the phone. The IMEI should appear on the screen.

For a phone you intend to purchase, ask the seller to provide access to the device so you can obtain its IMEI and complete the check.

Step 4: Follow the verification prompts

Enter the required information and follow the instructions provided by the service to check the device’s status.

Step 5: Review the result before buying

Check the information returned by the service. If the device’s status is unclear or verification fails, seek clarification from the seller or the NCC before completing the purchase.

An unsuccessful verification does not automatically mean the phone is fake. It may require further checks to establish whether it meets the applicable requirements.

What should you do if your phone fails the NCC check?

If the service does not verify a device, do not immediately conclude that it is counterfeit.

Instead, take the following steps:

Ask the seller to explain the verification result.

Confirm that the IMEI entered is correct.

Request supporting information about the device’s compliance status.

Contact your mobile network provider or the NCC for assistance if the issue remains unresolved.

If you have not paid for the phone, consider delaying the purchase until the verification issue is clarified.

The NCC has warned that devices found to be non-compliant with applicable requirements could be denied access to Nigerian

Do you need to verify a phone you already use?

According to the NCC, devices that were already connected to Nigerian mobile networks before the framework took effect were automatically verified and generally require no action from their users.

However, consumers buying second-hand phones or devices that have never connected to a Nigerian network should check their status before completing a purchase.

The framework covers smartphones, feature phones, cellular tablets, eligible Internet of Things devices, SIM-enabled point-of-sale terminals, cellular laptops and other equipment designed to connect to Nigerian mobile networks.

Will the NCC use the Device Checker to monitor your phone?

The Commission has said the system is designed for device identification and regulatory verification, not surveillance.

According to the NCC, the framework does not give the Commission access to users’ calls, messages, photographs, contacts, financial information or other personal files. It also said the Device Checker does not track users’ physical locations or movements.

The Commission has urged Nigerians to use only its official verification channels and warned consumers against fraudsters who may attempt to exploit the process. It advised users never to disclose one-time verification codes to sellers, callers or other individuals.

Vanguard News

World.title: Senate urges emergency repairs on Anambra-Rivers highway
World.content:
Senate

….Tasks Umahi to prioritise abandoned projects, rejects move to halt new road construction

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Senate has urged the Federal Government, the Federal Roads Maintenance Agency (FERMA) and the South-East Development Commission (SEDC) to undertake emergency repairs on failed sections of the Onitsha–Iyiowa–Odekpe–Atani–Ogwuikpele–Ndoni Federal Highway linking Anambra and Rivers states.

The Senate also called on the Federal Ministry of Works to commence the immediate rehabilitation and reconstruction of the highway through a special intervention programme or other appropriate funding arrangements, citing its strategic importance as a link between the South-East and South-South geopolitical zones.

The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by Senator Tony Nwoye (NDC, Anambra North), titled, “Urgent Need for the Rehabilitation of the Onitsha–Iyiowa–Odekpe–Atani–Ogwuikpele–Ndoni Federal Highway, Ogbaru Local Government Area, Anambra State,” during Wednesday’s plenary.

The lawmakers also urged the Federal Government to prioritise the completion of abandoned and long-delayed road projects before embarking on new ones.

However, a proposal by Senator Adams Oshiomhole (APC, Edo North) seeking to prevent the Minister of Works, David Umahi, from starting new road projects until existing ones were completed was not adopted.

Instead, the Senate adopted a recommendation by former Senate President Ahmad Lawan (APC, Yobe North), urging the minister to give priority to older and abandoned projects.

Presenting the motion, Nwoye said the highway was a strategic federal road linking the South-East and South-South regions. He noted that parts of the road were constructed in the late 1980s but had suffered decades of neglect without major rehabilitation.

He said prolonged abandonment, ageing infrastructure, increasing traffic and inadequate routine maintenance had left the road in a deplorable condition, characterised by extensive pavement failures, deep potholes and severe erosion.

According to him, the condition of the highway poses serious risks to the lives and property of commuters and other road users.

Nwoye said the deterioration had significantly increased travel time, with a journey of about 70 kilometres from Onitsha through Ogbaru to Ndoni, which ordinarily takes approximately one hour, now taking nearly two hours.

He added that the delay had increased transportation costs, reduced productive working hours and disrupted commercial activities.

The senator further observed that failed sections of the road frequently caused vehicle breakdowns, leaving motorists stranded for extended periods and exposing commuters to accidents and security risks.

He said the highway served an important economic corridor, particularly because of oil and gas exploration and production activities in the Ogbaru oil belt, which contribute to the national economy.

Nwoye warned that continued neglect of the road could further undermine interstate commerce, agricultural value chains, regional integration and investment, while increasing the hardship faced by residents of Anambra and Rivers states.

As part of its resolutions, the Senate mandated its Committee on Works to conduct an on-the-spot assessment of the highway, engage relevant stakeholders and report back within four weeks with recommendations.

It also mandated the Senate Committees on Works and Appropriations to ensure adequate budgetary provision for the comprehensive rehabilitation and reconstruction of the highway.

The Senate further called for urgent intervention to address flooding and erosion threatening communities across the South-East, highlighting the need for relevant authorities, including the SEDC, to respond to the region’s infrastructure and environmental challenges.

World.title: Tension in Ibadan as suspected thugs attack Accord gov candidate supporters
World.content:
By Adeola Badru

Tension erupted in Ibadan on Wednesday as suspected street urchins allegedly attacked the political train of the Accord governorship candidate in Oyo State, Oriyomi Hamzat, during a procession in the Molete area, leaving some supporters injured and vehicles vandalised.

The attack reportedly disrupted the peaceful procession organised by hundreds of supporters to welcome Hamzat back to Nigeria from the United Kingdom, raising concerns over political intolerance and the safety of political activities in the state.

The procession, which took place in Molete, within Ibadan South-West Local Government Area, reportedly turned chaotic when the suspected attackers allegedly ambushed the supporters and pelted them with stones.

The development sparked anger among members of the political train, some of whom were reportedly injured in the attack, while several vehicles in the convoy were vandalised.

The situation threatened to degenerate into a confrontation as aggrieved supporters became increasingly agitated over the alleged assault.

The intervention of Hamzat and security operatives reportedly helped to calm frayed nerves and prevent the supporters from launching a reprisal attack.

Condemning the incident, the aggrieved supporters described the attack as an affront to democratic freedom, insisting that no individual or group should resort to violence to intimidate people because of their political affiliations.

“This is democracy. You have the right to support any candidate of your choice. We ought to have outgrown this kind of politics of bitterness and thuggery in Oyo State,” one of the supporters said.

They expressed dismay that a procession organised to welcome their candidate could be disrupted by violence, stressing that political differences should not be allowed to threaten the peace or undermine the right of citizens to associate with candidates of their choice.

“Some of our members were injured during these unprovoked attacks. Also, some of the vehicles in our convoy were vandalised,” the supporters said.

Despite the incident, the group insisted that the attack would not discourage them from supporting Hamzat’s governorship ambition, describing him as a peaceful politician.

“Hamzat is a man of peace. We have left the place,” they added.

The supporters said the procession would continue from the Ibadan Toll Gate end of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway and terminate at the headquarters of Agidigbo FM radio along the Iwo Road–Ojoo Expressway.

Meanwhile, the Police Public Relations Officer in Oyo State, DSP Olayinka Ayanlade, confirmed the incident during a telephone conversation with our correspondent.

“I am aware of the attacks,” he said.

World.title: El-Rufai: ICPC opposes Jimi Lawal’s bail as court fixes hearing for Oct. 16
World.content:
The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) prosecution has opposed the bail application filed by Jimi Lawal, second defendant in the alleged financial misconduct case involving former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai.

The Federal High Court in Kaduna on Wednesday adjourned the hearing of Lawal’s bail application until October 16, 2026, while fixing December 8, 2026, for the commencement of the substantive trial.

One of the prosecution counsel, Ibrahim Mukhtar, disclosed this to journalists after proceedings before the presiding Judge, Justice Hauwa’u Buhari.

Mukhtar said the prosecution had filed a counter-affidavit opposing Lawal’s bail application but had yet to present its arguments before the court.

“We have already filed a counter-affidavit to it. So, we are opposing the application,” he said.

He declined to disclose the grounds for opposing the application, explaining that the prosecution was yet to formally present its response before the court.

Mukhtar said the charges against the defendants bordered on alleged financial misconduct and involved about seven counts.

He, however, noted that the substantive trial had yet to commence and that no witnesses had been presented before the court.

At the court proceedings, Counsel to Lawal, Obong Okon, urged the court to grant his client bail on medical grounds, arguing that his health condition warranted his release.

Okon also argued that the prosecution could not reasonably oppose the application after granting Lawal administrative bail.

The counsel maintained that the medical grounds presented in the application were sufficient to justify bail, adding that only a living person could stand trial.

Counsel to El-Rufai, Mustapha Abubakar, SAN, told journalists that new counsel had announced an appearance for the prosecution and sought time to study the case.

Abubakar said the defence team representing El-Rufai was also appearing new in the matter and supported the request for adjournment to enable it to take over the brief from the former counsel.

He explained that the substantive case was consequently adjourned until December 8 for hearing.

On Lawal’s bail application, Abubakar said the relevant court processes, including the motion, the prosecution’s counter-affidavit and the further affidavit filed in response, were before the court.

According to him, the prosecution informed the court that it needed time to study the further affidavit, which was served on the same day (today).

He said Lawal’s counsel agreed to the adjournment in the interest of fair hearing, although the bail application had already been moved.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that both El-Rufai and Lawal were brought to the court under heavy security.

(NAN)

World.title: The Illusion of Comprehension, Productive Doubt and Nigeria’s 2027 Elections
World.content:
By Joshua Obasanya

One of the biggest risks we face is what psychologists call the illusion of comprehension. This tendency makes us think we understand issues far better than we really do. As Nigeria heads toward the 2027 elections, public discussion is growing louder, more divided, and more emotional. Social media is filled with posts showing tribalism, division, and strong party loyalty. Yet many conversations have shifted away from the high cost of living, insecurity, unemployment, inflation, and economic hardship into personal attacks, ethnic arguments, and political showmanship.

Too often, people attack each other instead of discussing ideas. Political discussions that should help us learn have become loyalty tests. Friendships suffer, families are split, and communities are divided over politics. The result is often more anger than understanding. Yet certainty is not the same as understanding. Many of us form opinions from short clips, viral videos, social media posts, and party-driven stories. We take in fragments of complex issues and wrongly believe we fully understand them. That is the illusion of comprehension.

Topics like government, economics, public finance, monetary policy, national security, constitutional change, and development are deeply complex. The more you study them, the more clearly you see how much remains unknown. This is where productive doubt is necessary. Productive doubt does not mean you are weak or unsure. It means you are humble enough to recognise the limits of what you know. It means you are willing to ask, “What am I missing?” and brave enough to say, “I may be wrong.”

Indeed, the wisest person is not the one who claims to know everything. The wisest person recognises how little he knows. The more we read, the more we discover how vast our ignorance is. Authentic learning produces humility; superficial knowledge often produces overconfidence. That is why productive doubt matters.

As citizens in a democracy, we have a civic responsibility not only to vote but also to choose responsibly. That means thinking critically, staying self-aware, and seeking truth rather than merely defending political camps. Citizens should resist the temptation to amplify political propaganda until it creates emotional and physical tension among siblings, friends, colleagues, and community members. No politician is worth destroying relationships built over years.

As Dele Farotimi wisely cautioned: “Don’t die in their war.” Political actors will come and go. Parties will rise and fall. Elections will be won and lost. Yet the social bonds that hold families, friendships, and communities together are too precious to sacrifice to partisan passion.

At the same time, the opposition has an important role. Beyond calling out the failures of those in power, it should offer constructive criticism, articulate credible alternatives, and present clear policy proposals that can move the nation forward. Democracy flourishes when the electorate sees competing ideas and solutions, not only competing accusations. As we approach 2027, Nigerians must demand more from both government and opposition. We must move beyond personality cults, ethnic considerations, religious sentiments, and political propaganda. We should assess leaders and parties by competence, character, vision, integrity, and capacity to improve citizens’ lives.

Before engaging in political debates online, perhaps we should ask ourselves:

Have I studied this issue deeply enough?

Am I evaluating evidence or merely defending a political tribe? Have I listened fairly to opposing views?

What facts would make me reconsider my position? Could I be mistaken?

A healthy democracy requires informed citizens, not merely loud ones.

Improving our self-awareness and critically assessing political and economic realities will help voters make wise choices in 2027. Nigeria’s future depends not on how fiercely we defend politicians, but on how thoughtfully we evaluate their ideas, policies, and performance.

As Socrates is famously credited with saying, “The only true wisdom is in knowing that you know nothing.”

As Nigeria moves toward another electoral season, let us choose productive doubt over false certainty, comprehension over noise, and wisdom over partisanship. Let us ask harder questions, resist easy answers, and demand better judgment from ourselves and others. Let us debate policies rather than personalities, ideas rather than identities, and solutions rather than sentiments. Let us choose facts over propaganda, reason over emotion, and national progress over political fanaticism. In 2027, let our judgment shape Nigeria’s future—not the loudest voices on social media.

*Dr Joshua Obasanya is a health security consultant and public policy expert. He lives in Abuja

World.title: Exclusion of Candidates From INEC List: CD Cautions Electoral Body Against Manipulation By Politicians
World.content:
. Demands untainted integrity ahead of 2027 elections

A leading pro-democracy group in Nigeria, the Campaign for Democracy (CD) has raised concerns over the omission of some political parties’ candidates from the list of candidates to contest in the 2027 general elections, particularly some governorship candidates.

The pro-democracy group warned the Independent National Electoral Commission against manipulation by desperate politicians, saying any threat to what it described as “political pluralism and participatory democracy” would be resisted.

In a strongly worded statement, signed by its President, Comrade Ifeanyi Odili, and released on Wednesday, CD wondered how the candidates’ names were excluded from the final list, without any immediate explanation, and when INEC, in its earlier list made available to the public on August 29, 2026, had cleared and published them.

The statement made particular reference to the Peoples Democratic Party’s governorship candidate in Gombe State, Isa Pantami; the party’s governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, and his deputy, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo.

The Campaign for Democracy said the development was particularly disturbing in Ogun State, where citizens had witnessed repeated boasts and triumphalism by members of the All Progressives Congress in the state that the PDP governorship candidate would be excluded from the final list.

According to CD, as if to validate that boast, INEC went ahead to publish a list that excluded both the PDP candidate, and his deputy, Hajia Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, without stating any reason for their omission.

CD said, “The timing of the omissions was even more disturbing, and this was where we became concerned and alarmed. A particular instance was that of Ogun State where the state’s citizens had witnessed repeated claims and apparent triumphalism by elements within the All Progressives Congress (APC) and their supporters that the PDP governorship candidate would be disqualified from participating in the forthcoming election.

“As if to validate that boast, INEC published a list that excluded both PDP candidates without stating the reason for their omission.”

“This troubling sequence of events raises legitimate questions about the independence and impartiality of the Commission that Nigerians cannot afford to ignore,” the pro-democracy group added.

It said, “Under your leadership, Mr. Chairman, INEC bears an enormous responsibility to demonstrate impartiality, transparency, and strict adherence to the law. Unfortunately, this development has raised serious doubts about the Commission’s preparedness to conduct a credible, transparent, and inclusive election in 2027.

“The clarification by the Commission published late yesterday, three days after the incident was belated.”

The group stated, “To the best of our knowledge, these are candidates that emerged through the primaries conducted by their various political Parties which were monitored by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Information in the public domain shows clearly that these candidates were on the earlier list published on the 29th of August, 2026.

“Even though the Commission has just published a belated clarification on the incident, we consider this development deeply troubling and a serious blow to public confidence in the electoral process, particularly because the published list provided no immediate explanation for the omissions of the governorship and other candidates.”

CD, which was formed in 1991 and was among the prominent civil society organisations that fought the military for restoration of civil rule in 1999, said it decided to intervene because the omission threatens Nigeria’s democratic credentials, warning INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, to avoid orchestrating anything that could set the nation on fire.

The organisation maintained that it was deeply troubling that candidates who emerged through primaries monitored by INEC itself could be so brazenly excluded without immediate explanation.

The group warned that an electoral umpire must not only be independent but must be seen to be independent.

CD said information from the affected states already showed heightened anxiety that could have exploded into intractable violence before the Commission’s belated clarification, describing the delay as inexcusable tardiness.

The pro-democracy body further demanded an immediate investigation into allegations circulating in the public that some candidates’ names were electronically removed after they were duly submitted.

It vowed that as a committed pro-democracy group, it would not hesitate to mobilise citizens and pro-democracy organisations across the nation for lawful mass civic action against any threat to political pluralism and participatory democracy.

“We remind INEC that elections belong to the Nigerian people, not to any political party, individual, or governing interest. No institution should take actions that create the impression that opposition participation can be determined by administrative discretion without transparent, constitutional justification and due process,” CD stated.

World.title: Senate Orders Nationwide Probe of Flood, Erosion Disasters, Demands Emergency Relief
World.content:
* Directs NEMA to provide food, shelter, medical supplies to victims

* Seeks reconstruction of washed-away roads, compensation for farmers

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Senate on Wednesday ordered a nationwide assessment of communities devastated by flooding and erosion, directing relevant federal agencies to provide emergency relief to displaced residents, rebuild damaged roads and assess destroyed farmlands and livestock for possible compensation.

The lawmakers also called for urgent federal intervention in erosion-prone communities in Anambra, Ebonyi and Imo States, warning that recurring environmental disasters had claimed lives, destroyed homes and livelihoods, and cut off communities from essential services.

As part of measures to address the worsening ecological crisis, the Senate mandated its Committees on Environment, Works, Ecology and Climate Change, in collaboration with other relevant committees, to conduct on-the-spot assessments of affected communities nationwide and submit their findings and recommendations within one month.

The resolutions followed three related motions presented during plenary by senators representing constituencies affected by flooding and erosion, who detailed the devastating consequences of the disasters on residents, businesses, agriculture and critical infrastructure.

The Senate specifically urged the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) to immediately provide food, potable water, temporary shelter, medical supplies and other essential relief materials to displaced persons and other victims of the disasters.

It also directed the Federal Ministry of Works and relevant agencies to assess and reconstruct damaged roads, restore access to communities cut off by flooding and erosion, and provide adequate drainage infrastructure to prevent further destruction.

The lawmakers called on the Federal Ministry of Environment to conduct comprehensive technical assessments of affected sites and implement sustainable flood and erosion control measures, including the construction, rehabilitation and expansion of drainage and stormwater management systems.

They further urged the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security to assess the destruction of farmlands, crops and livestock in affected communities in Ebonyi State and provide emergency grants to farmers who had suffered losses.

The Senate stressed the need for a coordinated, long-term rehabilitation and ecological restoration programme, backed by appropriate federal funding, to address the recurring disasters and prevent further loss of lives and property.

The resolutions were expanded to cover affected communities across the country, rather than restricting federal intervention to the South-east, following concerns raised by the lawmakers about the widespread nature of flooding and erosion disasters.

Leading the motion on the devastation caused by flooding and erosion in Anambra State, Senator Victor Umeh drew attention to the loss of lives, destruction of property and disruption of economic and social activities in several communities.

Umeh said at least four persons, including a pregnant woman and a six-year-old pupil of Nnamdi Azikiwe University Primary School, Awka, had died in the disasters, while several families had been displaced and numerous homes submerged.

He identified Ogidi, Obosi and Awka among the affected communities, noting that the destruction had extended to farmlands, economic trees, cash crops, streets and other critical infrastructure.

The senator expressed particular concern over the formation of deep and expanding erosion gullies, including one reportedly measuring more than 60 metres in depth.

He warned that the destruction of roads and other infrastructure had disrupted access to schools and important locations, while worsening insecurity as residents abandoned their homes and ancestral lands in search of safer places to live.

Umeh urged the Federal Government, through the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation and the Ecological Fund Office, to recognise the affected communities as requiring urgent national intervention.

He also called on the Federal Ministry of Works to urgently assess and reconstruct damaged roads, particularly the Onitsha-Ogidi-Awka federal road, where flooding had disrupted vehicular movement and other economic activities.

Seconding the motion, Senator Anthony Ani, who represents Ebonyi South, highlighted the devastating flash floods that ravaged communities across his senatorial district in late September 2026.

Ani said torrential rainfall had caused rivers to overflow their banks, submerging residential, commercial and agricultural areas across affected local government areas.

According to him, many residents had lost their homes and household valuables, while extensive agricultural lands, crops and livestock were destroyed, further worsening the economic difficulties confronting affected households.

“Most of the agricultural crops were destroyed. Many livestock in the households were equally destroyed. And so their lives are put into danger,” Ani said.

The senator called for urgent humanitarian assistance to the affected communities, stressing that the destruction of agricultural assets had compounded the hardship facing residents whose livelihoods depended on farming and livestock production.

He urged the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security to assess the extent of the damage to farmlands and livestock and provide emergency grants to farmers who had lost their sources of livelihood.

Ani also called for effective legislative oversight to ensure that NEMA complied with the Senate’s directive to provide relief materials to victims of the disasters.

Similarly, Senator Osita Izunaso raised the alarm over persistent flooding and erosion in communities across Imo West Senatorial District, warning that the situation had continued to deteriorate despite an earlier motion he presented on the problem in 2023.

Izunaso listed several of the affected communities, including Urualla, Obodoukwu, Osina, Abolo, Imo Chima, Imo Eshi, Ise Kenesi, Oso Obodo, Oguta Amishi, Nnefuku and Nkosi autonomous communities across Ideato North, Ideato South and Oguta Local Government Areas.

He said flooding and erosion had continued to destroy homes, businesses, farmlands and roads, exposing motorists and pedestrians to dangerous conditions and contributing to repeated accidents and loss of lives.

“The resulting erosion has washed away roads and also created dangerous conditions for motorists and pedestrians, with accidents and loss of life repeatedly occurring in some affected areas,” Izunaso said.

He called for emergency intervention by NEMA, the Federal Emergency Management Agency, the Federal Ministry of Works and other relevant agencies to provide relief materials, rehabilitate damaged roads, improve drainage and implement effective erosion control measures.

The senator also advocated a coordinated, long-term rehabilitation and ecological restoration programme, supported by adequate federal funding, to address the recurring environmental disasters and protect vulnerable communities from further destruction.

The Senate’s resolutions reflect growing concerns over the humanitarian and economic consequences of flooding and erosion, particularly in communities where damaged roads, destroyed agricultural assets and displaced households have compounded existing livelihood challenges.

By directing its committees to inspect affected locations nationwide and report within one month, the Senate sought to establish the scale of the destruction and identify the interventions required from relevant federal agencies.

The lawmakers also called for greater coordination among emergency management agencies, environmental authorities and infrastructure ministries to ensure that relief efforts were accompanied by lasting solutions to the underlying ecological problems.

The Senate observed a minute’s silence in honour of those who lost their lives in the flooding disasters.

World.title: MSF Carries Out 1,645 Surgeries on Noma Patients in Sokoto, 95 in 2026 Alone
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) has disclosed that it carried out 1,645 reconstructive surgeries for 1,078 noma patients at the Noma Hospital in Sokoto between 2014 and 2025.

Speaking at a media briefing in Sokoto, the Nursing Activity Manager of the hospital, Mr. Ajamah Samuel Afemike, said in 2026 alone, 95 patients benefited from its free surgical interventions.

Afemike said 55 surgeries were performed during the first phase of the intervention held between April 17 and May 1, while 40 more patients are expected to undergo surgery in the ongoing final phase for the year.

He explained that MSF, which has supported the Ministry of Health’s Noma Hospital since 2014, provides early case detection, medical treatment, nutritional care, physiotherapy and psychosocial support to patients.

According to him, noma is a non-contagious disease that rapidly destroys facial tissues and bones, progressing within days and causing severe facial damage and life-threatening complications if left untreated.

He said if left untreated, approximately 70 to 90 per cent of affected people die, while survivors often suffer difficulties in eating, speaking, breathing and carrying out daily activities.

Afemike added that many survivors also face stigma, social exclusion, psychological distress, barriers to education and livelihoods, and financial hardship.

He noted that noma primarily affects children under seven years old and is closely associated with extreme poverty, malnutrition, inadequate oral hygiene, low immunisation coverage, recurrent infections and limited access to healthcare.

He described noma as both a medical condition and an indicator of broader gaps in primary healthcare systems, lamenting that awareness remains extremely limited among communities and frontline healthcare workers.

He observed that many patients visit multiple health facilities before receiving correct diagnosis, thereby losing opportunity for life-saving early treatment with antibiotics, wound care and nutritional support.

Despite being recognised by the World Health Organization (WHO) as a Neglected Tropical Disease (NTD) in 2023, Afemike said noma remains largely absent from routine healthcare and child health programmes in Nigeria, calling for stronger action to integrate its prevention, detection, treatment, referral and surveillance into primary healthcare.

World.title: Tinubu Seeks Senate Approval to Establish National School of Government
World.content:
* Proposed institution to replace ASCON, strengthen leadership development, policy delivery

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has asked the Senate to approve a bill seeking to repeal the Administrative Staff College of Nigeria (ASCON) Act and establish the National School of Government, Nigeria, as a national institution for leadership development, policy delivery and executive capacity building.

Senate President Godswill Akpabio read the president’s letter transmitting the National School of Government Bill 2026 to the upper chamber during plenary on Wednesday.

In the letter, Tinubu urged the Senate to give the proposed legislation expeditious consideration, stressing the need to establish a dedicated institution to strengthen leadership development and improve the capacity of public officials to deliver government policies.

The president invoked Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, to formally transmit the bill to the Senate for legislative consideration.

“Pursuant to Section 58 (2) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended, I forward herewith the National School of Government Bill 2026 for the kind consideration of the Senate,” Tinubu stated in the letter.

He expressed the hope that the lawmakers would give the bill the necessary attention and facilitate its consideration.

The proposed legislation seeks to repeal the Administrative Staff College of Nigeria Act, A-4, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004, and replace the existing legal framework with one establishing the National School of Government, Nigeria.

According to the president, the proposed institution would serve as a national centre for leadership development, policy delivery and executive capacity building.

The initiative, as outlined in the presidential communication, would place the proposed school at the centre of efforts to develop leadership capacity and strengthen the ability of government officials to translate public policies into practical outcomes.

The bill’s transmission marks the beginning of the legislative process required to determine its provisions, institutional framework and other matters necessary for the establishment of the proposed school.

After reading the president’s letter, Akpabio informed senators that the clauses and provisions of the bill had been attached to the communication for their consideration.

He subsequently referred the bill to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative action.

The committee is expected to take the next procedural steps towards the bill’s consideration in accordance with the Senate’s legislative processes.

The proposed repeal of the ASCON Act would bring the existing statutory framework governing the institution under review as the Federal Government seeks legislative backing for the National School of Government.

However, the presidential letter, as read on the floor of the Senate, did not provide further details on the proposed institution’s governance structure, funding arrangements, location or the specific relationship it would have with existing public service training institutions.

These and other provisions will depend on the contents of the bill and the subsequent legislative process.

The bill will now proceed through the Senate’s established procedures for further consideration.

World.title: Dangote Group, Botswana Exchange Laud NGX Group for Driving Cross-Border Collaboration
World.content:
Dangote Industries Limited and the Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE) have commended Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX Group) for bringing African exchanges together to expand cross-border investment opportunities through the ongoing roadshow for the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE offer.

The commendation came on Wednesday at an investor engagement in Gaborone, following an earlier engagement in Nairobi, Kenya.

The roadshow forms part of NGX Group’s wider initiative to deepen collaboration among African exchanges and widen access to investment opportunities across the continent.

The Group Chief Financial Officer of Dangote Industries Limited, Murat Erden, praised NGX Group, under the leadership of Group Chairman, Alhaji Umaru Kwairanga, and Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Temi Popoola, for galvanising African exchanges around the initiative, which began with an engagement convened by NGX Group in Lagos in April 2026.

He also highlighted the role of digital innovation in broadening access to the offer, citing the addition of WhatsApp to NGX Invest, and acknowledged the partnership between NGX Group and participating exchanges in reaching investors across their respective markets.

The Chief Executive Officer of the BSE, Aobakwe Aupa Monyatsi, also welcomed the collaboration, highlighting the value of partnerships among African exchanges and the opportunity to widen participation by encouraging additional markets to join the initiative.

At the earlier engagement in Nairobi, President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, lauded Kwairanga and Popoola for their role in advancing collaboration among African capital-market institutions.

He highlighted how stronger ties between exchanges could enable companies to raise capital across multiple markets rather than being limited to their home markets. Citing the planned refinery in Mokowe-Lamu, Kenya, as an example, he pointed to the potential for businesses operating across Africa to list in more than one market.

NGX Group Chairman, Kwairanga, said: “Our vision is to build stronger connections among African capital markets, making it easier for businesses to access capital and for investors to participate in opportunities across the continent. The collaboration around the Dangote Refinery offer demonstrates what African exchanges can achieve when we work together towards a shared objective.”

Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Popoola, has similarly emphasised the importance of translating continental ambition into practical partnerships. He said: “When we began this engagement, our objective was continental: to bring African exchanges together and explore how we can create stronger connections between African capital markets.”

NGX Invest, NGX Group’s electronic public-offering platform, supports subscriptions through more than 180 distribution channels, including stockbrokers, banks and fintech companies. The addition of WhatsApp as an access channel further expands the ways investors can access the offer.

The roadshow continues with engagements at the Egyptian Exchange (EGX) and the Ethiopian Securities Exchange (ESX), extending the initiative’s reach and creating further opportunities for African exchanges to collaborate on cross-border investment.

World.title: EFCC Reopens Atiku Probe, Adopts Agbonayinma’s Petition
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has reopened an investigation into allegations involving former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar following a petition by a former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Ehiozuwa Johnson Agbonayinma.

The commission acknowledged receipt of the petition, dated August 27, 2026, and received on September 1, 2026, confirming that investigation has commenced.

The former lawmaker through his lawyer, Chief Hannibal Uwaifo (SAN), is seeking a review of the allegations arising from an earlier investigation involving the former vice-president.

As part of the process, the EFCC invited Agbonayinma to its headquarters in Jabi, Abuja, on October 12, where he adopted his petition and responded to questions from investigators.

He arrived at about 9:58 a.m. and left at approximately 4:07 p.m. after the interview.

The commission’s acknowledgement letter, referenced CR:3000/EFCC/HQ/SDC-2/VOL.3/398, forms part of the ongoing investigative process.

He told newsmen that his petition sought to revisit an investigation conducted by the former EFCC chairman, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, involving Atiku.

He argued that the matter deserved renewed attention in the interest of accountability and the rule of law.

“I want to thank Nigerians, the EFCC and those praying for me in this struggle. The laws are meant for both the rich and the poor. After the EFCC has done a fantastic job, it should not be kept under the table,” he said.

Agbonayinma added that he considered reporting alleged wrongdoing a constitutional responsibility, insisting that nobody was above the law.

He also disclosed that he had written a petition on the matter to United States President Donald Trump, calling for attention to the allegations.

World.title: PINL Deepens Community Ties as Stakeholders Renew Pledge To Protect Pipelines
World.content:
*Stakeholders call for replacement of 60-year-old oil, gas pipelines

The Pipeline Infrastructure Nigeria Limited (PINL), under the leadership of its Managing Director, Osahon Okunbo, has deepened its community relations drive across the Niger Delta, as stakeholders in Rivers and Bayelsa States renewed their commitment to peaceful relations and the protection of critical pipeline infrastructure at the company’s October 2026 Stakeholders’ Engagement Forum.

The two-day forum, held on October 9 and 10, 2026, in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, brought together traditional rulers, youth leaders, environmental advocates, community representatives and other regional leaders. It is part of a sustained engagement programme driven by Okunbo, who has made direct, regular contact with host communities the foundation of PINL’s pipeline surveillance operations in the communities that host the pipelines the company safeguards”, a statement issued by the company said.

While speaking at the event, the General Manager, Community and Stakeholders Relations (PINL), Dr. Akpos Mezeh said PINL had recorded two consecutive months without any pipeline vandalisation within its operational areas in the Niger Delta, which he attributed to good collaboration among stakeholders, which include host communities, security agencies, surveillance personnel, and industry operators.

Mezeh, who also called for sustained cooperation among stakeholders to protect critical national infrastructure, maintain peace, and promote development in the Niger Delta, added that infrastructure could deliver value only when adequately protected.

“Sustainable production and development depend on peaceful communities and trust among industry operators, government and host communities,” he said.

He said host communities and stakeholders along the Trans Niger Pipeline (TNP) and the Eastern Gas Network (EGN) will play a pivotal role in ensuring that Nigeria meets its oil and gas production targets for 2027 and 2030.

According to Mezeh, NNPCL Ltd’s recently released audited results for 2025, which reported a Profit after Tax of ₦7.2 trillion, up 33 percent from ₦5.4 trillion in 2024.

“More importantly for our discussion today, crude oil and condensate production averaged 1.77 million barrels per day in 2025, the company’s highest production level in five years, and natural gas production averaged 7.2 billion standard cubic feet per day, the highest in three years,” he said.

He further stated that PINL’s surveillance operations had provided employment for more than 35,000 youths, while its scholarship programme had awarded over ₦2 billion to more than 1,500 undergraduate and postgraduate students.

The PINL official also urged stakeholders to disregard what the company described as a campaign of calumny against it by individuals whose motives were unclear.

“Allegations should not be presented as established facts, particularly when they concern public expenditure, contractual arrangements or the reputation of individuals and institutions,” he said.

Meanwhile, stakeholders at the meeting expressed satisfaction with PINL’s operations and urged the federal government to sustain and expand its contract.

Engr. Omojevwhe Akponime, Head, Field Operations, Eastern Corridor, at the NNPC Project Monitoring Office, said NNPC’s daily reviews show the lines in PINL’s area of coverage running green, as he related to a recent NNPC management session.

“There is no question for PINL. They said so because they are doing well. “He said.

In his remarks, Eze Eberi-Ugo IX of Omuma Kingdom, Onyekachi Amaonwu, said national output targets are only achievable if there are grassroots cooperation across host communities.

“For you to achieve these targets, there is no pipeline in Abuja; the pipelines are located right here in our communities,” Amaonwu said, as he urged other traditional rulers and community leaders to support PINL.

Also speaking, the Eze Ekpeye-Logbo, Kelvin Anugwo, hinted that communities across Ekpeye land in Rivers State had returned to farming and fishing activities due to a decrease in crude oil theft along the corridor.

“Before PINL came on board, we were unable to fish in our rivers because spilled crude oil had ruined the environment,” Anugwo stated.

On his part, the spokesperson for the Niger Delta Ethnic Youth Leaders Forum, Legborsi Yamaabana, commended the federal government for renewing PINL’s contract.

He said, “As Niger Delta people, we have adopted PINL as our own,” adding that dissenting voices would not alter the region’s endorsement of the company.

Also, at the forum in Bayelsa, stakeholders called on oil companies and relevant authorities to address the environmental risks posed by ageing pipelines, abandoned wellheads and continued gas flaring, as they warned that these dangers could threaten livelihoods and damage the environment.

King Bubaraye Dakolo Agada IV, King of Ekpetiama Kingdom who made the call said efforts to prevent pipeline vandalism must go hand in hand with measures to address risks associated with oil and gas infrastructure.

The monarch noted that increased oil production could generate more revenue for Nigeria, but warned that oil spills could leave host communities struggling with environmental damage and loss of livelihoods for years.

He urged residents to discourage pipeline vandalism and other activities that could cause spills in their creeks and communities and also stressed that oil companies and relevant authorities must also take responsibility for preventing spills linked to ageing infrastructure.

According to him, PINL should draw the attention of relevant authorities and oil industry operators to the dangers posed by old pipelines, abandoned wellheads and gas flaring, urging them to take preventive action before incidents occur.

He said pipeline protection should not be limited to stopping sabotage but should also cover infrastructure-related risks that could harm the environment and the people living in host communities.

In his remarks, the President of the Ijaw Youth Council (IYC) Worldwide, Doubra Okotete, commended the leadership of pipeline surveillance contractors, saying there had been no reports of fatalities since the company took over the contract.

He described the development as a departure from the past, when such operations were, in his words, “plagued by fatalism”.

Okotete said the surveillance operations had helped secure oil and gas infrastructure while ensuring that host communities benefited from the resources flowing through the facilities they protected.

“Our appeal today is for the Federal Government, the NNPCL and the President of our great country to ensure that oil and gas pipelines that have lasted for over 60 years are replaced,” he said.

World.title: ‘Government must create jobs’: Taxpayer concerns spark fresh SASSA grant debate
World.content:
A group of male construction workers on site wearing safety gear during the daytime. Image: Pexels

South Africans are once again debating the future of SASSA social grants, with many raising concerns about who ultimately pays for them.

Comments on The South African’s Facebook page show a growing frustration with the country’s dependence on grants and the pressure these places on a limited pool of taxpayers.

Jobs over grants

Donovan Kay believes the answer to poverty lies in employment rather than handouts.



“Government must create jobs; that’s the only way to counteract poverty. SASSA grants come from taxpayers, and taxpayers are becoming fewer and fewer in this country,” Kay wrote.

His comment reflects a concern many economists share. South Africa has one of the highest unemployment rates in the world, which means fewer people earn enough to pay income tax while more people rely on state support. Every grant payment, from the Older Persons Grant to the Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant, draws from the national budget funded largely by individual and corporate taxpayers.

A shrinking tax base under pressure

Kay’s point touches on a long-running fiscal debate. When businesses close, skilled workers emigrate or jobs disappear, the tax base narrows. At the same time, demand for social assistance continues to rise as households struggle with the cost of living.

This imbalance places Treasury in a difficult position. Cutting grants would push millions of vulnerable people deeper into poverty, while expanding them without economic growth increases the burden on those who already pay.

Julian Humphries shared a similar view, writing that “Everybody that works regardless of what they do must contribute in order for this to be possible.”

Where the conversation goes next

The debate highlights a broader question about South Africa’s economic direction. Grants remain a lifeline for pensioners, caregivers and unemployed adults, and for many households they are the only reliable income.



However, commenters such as Kay argue that long-term relief will only come once more South Africans find stable work. Job creation would not only reduce reliance on grants but also widen the pool of taxpayers who fund them.

Until then, the tension between protecting the vulnerable and protecting the public purse is likely to remain at the centre of conversations about SASSA and the country’s social safety net.
