World.title: The old Surf Riders spot on Durban’s South Beach has a new tenant
World.content:
An artist's impression of the planned development at 17 Erskine Terrace on Durban's South Beach. Image: Surf Riders Cafe

Durban’s South Beach is getting a new hospitality destination.

It’s taking over a much-loved spot on the Golden Mile.

And it comes from a homegrown Durban brand that started out as a township car wash.



Here’s what we know: Durban-born hospitality brand Mojo’s has secured a lease for the municipal property at 17 Erskine Terrace, South Beach.

The property was previously home to Surf Riders Cafe.

The eThekwini Municipality announced the news on Tuesday, 13 October.



WHAT THE SOUTH BEACH LEASE INCLUDES

According to the municipality, Mojo’s Investment CC won the lease after a competitive bidding process.

The lease runs for nine years and 11 months.

The bidding process began in November 2023.

The award was delayed after an unsuccessful bidder appealed the outcome.



An independent appeal authority dismissed the appeal and upheld the original decision.

The unsuccessful bidder then launched a court challenge.

But on 1 October 2026, it filed a notice to withdraw the case at the KwaZulu-Natal High Court in Pietermaritzburg, clearing the way for the lease to go ahead.



WHO IS MOJO’S?

Mojo’s has been operating for about 20 years.

It started as a modest car wash in Chesterville, a township in Durban, before growing into Mojo’s Carwash & Shisanyama.

It has since expanded to Mojo’s on Davenport in Glenwood.



The municipality described the move to South Beach as an important milestone for a homegrown Durban hospitality and lifestyle brand.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR DURBAN SOUTH BEACH

The municipality says the new venue will bring more variety to the beachfront.

“The move will add to the diversity of food, hospitality, entertainment, and leisure experiences available along the Golden Mile and introduce the Mojo’s concept to a broader market of residents and visitors,” the municipality said.



It says the lease is part of its strategy to attract private investment and revitalise underutilised municipal properties along Durban’s beachfront.

Municipal spokesperson Senzelwe Mzila said the deal forms part of a growing pipeline of property transactions bringing new businesses and economic activity to the beachfront.

He said these investments are part of the municipality’s “broader approach to optimising the economic and development potential of strategically located properties.”



MORE INVESTMENT ON THE GOLDEN MILE

It’s not the first beachfront deal.

In 2024, the municipality named Southern Sun as the preferred bidder for a 50-year lease to redevelop the Elangeni and Maharani hotels.

Including refurbishments at two of its other beachfront hotels, Southern Sun’s investment was estimated at R1 billion.



Another R70 million private development is also planned at 137 Lower Marine Parade.

According to the municipality, construction is set to begin in January 2027, with the aim of opening during the 2027/28 festive season.

WHAT ABOUT SURF RIDERS?

Surf Riders Cafe was a familiar stop for locals, surfers and visitors on South Beach.



Its South Beach chapter has now ended. But fans can still find Surf Riders at Umhlanga Cabanas and Gateway Boulevard.

WHEN WILL IT OPEN?

There’s no opening date yet.

The municipality says it will work with Mojo’s to get the business up and running as soon as possible.



Details about the menu, layout and offering at the new South Beach venue haven’t been released yet.

World.title: Transfer report: Under-20 star captain to Sundowns
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns are expected to acquire the services of Lazola Maku, fresh from lifting the COSAFA Under-20 championship with South Africa.

The 19-year-old from Cape Town has been a free agent since parting ways with Siwelele FC last season.

LAZOLA MAKU TO MAMELODI SUNDOWNS

While Maku enjoyed a successful trial in Austria in September, it appears Ka Bo Yellow are set to sign the dumitive mifielder.



“Following an apparently successful trial in Austria, South Africa U20 captain Lazola Maku is closing in on a move to Mamelodi Sundowns, with the newly crowned MTN8 champions expected to sign the midfielder on a free transfer,” SABC Sports’ Mazola Molefe reported.

LONG CAREER AHEAD?

Hailing from the humble parts of Hout Bay’s Masiphumelele township, Maku took his first career steps at the renowned Ubuntu Football Academy. He later caught the eye of SuperSport United.

After several seasons in the DStv Diski Challenge, Maku earned his senior debut with Siwelele FC. Despite his young age, Maku featured in several important league matches, demonstrating his passing ability and versatility as both a defensive midfielder and a deep-lying playmaker.

At international level, the Sundowns-bound star has established himself as a leader, captaining South Africa’s Under-20 national team, Amajita. He captained the national Under-16 side. He later played a key role in South Africa’s historic triumph at the Under-20 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) in Egypt.

Maku played every minute of the tournament, helping anchor the midfield as South Africa secured the title. His performances earned him a place in the competition’s Best XI.

His international experience also includes representing South Africa at the COSAFA Under-20 Championship. It also includes competing at the FIFA Under-20 World Cup.

World.title: Biltong, braais and ‘now now’: 8 things South Africans living abroad miss most
World.content:
South Africans living abroad say they miss family, friends and food from home the most. Image: ChatGPT

South Africans living abroad have a reputation for being a little homesick.

It turns out the data backs that up.

According to a 2026 study, South Africans are among the most homesick people in the world.



So what exactly are they missing? We looked at the latest research to find out.

More than 1 million South Africans live overseas, according to estimates from the United Nations and Statistics South Africa.

Australia, UK and the US are home to more than half of them.



And many of them still feel the pull of home.

A 2026 study by financial services company Remitly ranked South Africa as the second most homesick nation in the world, with 96.1% of South Africans abroad saying they feel homesick.

Only the Philippines ranked higher.

Here’s what they miss the most.

1. FAMILY

This one tops every list.

According to the study, 80% of South Africans abroad miss their family.

The TEFL Academy found something similar, with more than 77% of South Africans who had lived abroad saying they missed time with family and lifelong friends.

2. FRIENDS

Close behind family are the friends who knew you before you left.



Remitly found that 62% of South Africans abroad miss their friends.

3. FOOD AND DRINK

You can take a South African out of Mzansi, but you can’t take Mzansi out of their stomach.

More than half of South Africans abroad (54%) miss food and drink from home, according to Remitly.



That includes the obvious favourites, like biltong, boerewors and a proper braai.

4. LOCAL BRANDS

Some cravings are very specific.

The University of Cape Town’s Liberty Institute of Strategic Marketing surveyed more than 1,500 South Africans living in 73 countries for its South African Diaspora Report 2026.



The brands they missed most included Woolworths, Spur and Nik Naks.

5. THE HUMOUR AND WARMTH

South Africans have a way of making strangers feel like friends.

According to The TEFL Academy’s research, 66.9% of South Africans who had lived abroad said they missed South Africa’s humour, warmth and social culture.



6. THE OUTDOOR LIFESTYLE AND WEATHER

Long sunny days. Braais under the stars. Beach weekends.

The TEFL Academy found that more than 55% missed South Africa’s outdoor lifestyle.

Remitly’s study found that 34% missed the climate.



7. HEARING THEIR OWN LANGUAGES

There’s nothing like hearing “eish“, “lekker” or “now now” in the wild.

According to Remitly, around 36% of South Africans abroad miss hearing their native language regularly.

8. KNOWING HOW THINGS WORK

This one surprises people.



Moving abroad means relearning everything, from how to open a bank account to how the local healthcare system works.

According to Remitly, 30% of South Africans abroad miss understanding how everyday systems work at home.

And 27% simply miss sleeping in their own bed.



WILL SOUTH AFRICANS LIVING ABROAD COME HOME?

Missing home doesn’t always mean moving back.

The University of Cape Town’s survey found that only 17% of South Africans abroad plan to return to South Africa.

I grew up in different countries, so I know that feeling well.



You can love where you live and still miss the small things: the slang, the food, the way people talk to strangers.

To every South African reading this from abroad: Mzansi misses you too.

WHAT DO YOU MISS MOST ABOUT SOUTH AFRICA?

Let us know in the comments below…

World.title: Heatwave: How to cope in hot weather
World.content:
High temperatures can pose health risks, making it important to take precautions during a heatwave. Image: Pexels

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued a heatwave advisory for north-western parts of the province.

Persistently high temperatures could increase the risk of heat-related illness.

According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), prolonged exposure to extreme heat can put pressure on the body, particularly when it struggles to maintain a normal temperature.



The heat can affect anyone, but older people, young children, outdoor workers and people with existing health conditions face greater risks.

Tips for keeping cool during a heatwave

Keep your home cool

Close curtains, blinds and windows during the hottest parts of the day if the air outside is warmer than inside.

Open windows in the evening or at night when outdoor temperatures drop below indoor temperatures.



Switch off electrical appliances that generate unnecessary heat and spend time in the coolest room available.

If possible, spend a few hours in a cooler public space or an air-conditioned building.

Drink water regularly

Make it a trend to drink water throughout the day, even before you feel thirsty.



If you work outdoors, make sure to carry a water bottle and take regular water breaks.

Avoid excessive alcohol as it increase the risk of dehydration.

Wear lightweight, loose-fitting clothing and a wide-brimmed hat to protect yourself from direct sunlight.



Also apply sunscreen when spending time outdoors.

Look out for children and older people

Never leave children or pets inside parked vehicles, even for a short time.

Check regularly on older relatives, neighbours and anyone who lives alone, particularly those with existing health conditions.



Keep babies and young children in cool, shaded places.

Know the signs of heat illness

Extreme heat can cause heat exhaustion or heatstroke.

Watch for symptoms such as dizziness, headaches, nausea, weakness and heavy sweating.



One should follow the latest SAWS advisories and take extra precautions while high temperatures persist.

World.title: Halloween 2026: Where to celebrate spooky season in South Africa
World.content:
Here’s where to celebrate Halloween in South Africa in 2026. Image: canva

Halloween falls on Saturday, 31 October this year, and South Africans have plenty of options for where to celebrate.

From haunted forests and ghost tours to family-friendly trick-or-treating, themed markets, and late-night raves, Halloween events are happening across the country!

Here are some of the events to put on your calendar for Halloween 2026.



Johannesburg

Johannesburg has one of the biggest selections of Halloween events this year, with something for families, horror fans and partygoers.

The Haunted Forest 10th anniversary

The Haunted Forest is marking its 10th anniversary with a Halloween event at Prison Break Market in Glenferness on Saturday, 31 October.

The experience includes a fog-filled forest with life-size scenes and scare actors, while younger visitors can take part in trick-or-treating. There will also be films, food and entertainment.



The event runs from 15:00 to 23:00, with adult tickets starting at R150.

Halloween at Johannesburg Zoo

Johannesburg Zoo is also bringing back its Halloween experience on 31 October from 17:00.

Visitors can expect themed zones, trick-or-treating, costume competitions and live entertainment. Tickets range from R81 to R135.



Halloween Rave 2026

For something considerably less family-friendly, Halloween Rave takes over AND Night Club and CARFAX in Newtown.

The event brings together Teknotribe, Science Frikshun, Psyology and The Temple for an electronic music night running from 21:00.

Tickets are priced from R200 to R300.

Edenvale Halloween Night Market

Families can also head to the Edenvale German Club on Friday, 30 October for a Halloween night market.



The event runs from 18:00 to 23:00, with spooky stalls, food, drinks, trick-or-treating, live music and a best-dressed competition. Entry is R30 per person.

Cape Town

Cape Town has also embraced the spooky season, with events ranging from large music parties to ghost tours and community celebrations. The city was even ranked among the world’s top 50 Halloween destinations for 2026.

Halloween 2026 at 20 Harrington Street

One of the bigger Halloween parties in Cape Town takes place at 20 Harrington Street from Friday, 30 October into Saturday morning.



The line-up includes Silverstein, Fokofpolisiekar, Jack Parow, Sunken State and Doomtrigger, among others.

The event is strictly for over-18s, with general admission tickets starting at R349.

Halloween at the Royal Cape Yacht Club

For something a little more sophisticated, the Royal Cape Yacht Club is hosting a Halloween party on 31 October.



The evening includes themed food, cocktails, music and a costume competition. Non-members pay a R100 cover charge, while members can attend with their membership cards.

Bookings are essential.

Soul Society Halloween Edition

The Grand Daddy Boutique Hotel is hosting a rooftop Halloween celebration from 12:00 to 21:30 on 31 October.



The event focuses on soulful house and R&B, with DJs including Ready D, Will ST and DJ Arch, along with food, drinks and city views.

Tickets start at R100, and the event is aimed at adults.

Halloween in the Hof

Families looking for something more relaxed can head to Kirstenhof on Halloween evening.



Halloween in the Hof runs from 18:00 to 21:00 and includes a community trick-or-treat walk, ghost tunnel, fire dancers and food. Tickets start at R25.

Cape Town Halloween Ghost Tour

For a more genuinely spooky experience, Mystery Ghost Productions is running Halloween ghost tours through Cape Town on both 30 and 31 October.

The tours run from 19:00 to 23:00, starting at Prestwich Memorial, and combine historic locations with local ghost stories and legends. Tickets cost R449 per person.



Durban and KwaZulu-Natal

Durban and surrounding KZN also have a surprisingly busy Halloween calendar this year too.

Ballito Halloween Horrors

Ballito Halloween Horrors returns to La Montagne Resort on 30 and 31 October.

The full horror experience takes visitors through four themed areas, including the Twisted Woods, Maze of Horrors, Dark Hollow and Realm of the Unknown.



There is also a family-friendly option featuring face painting, carnival games and Halloween activities.

Tickets start at R150 for the family-friendly experience and R250 for the full horror experience.

Halloween After Dark at Gibaland

Gibaland in Shongweni is going with a jungle theme this year.



The daytime JumanGi Family Adventure is aimed at families, while JumanGi After Dark offers a darker version of the experience for those looking for more of a scare.

The After Dark experience runs from 18:30 to 21:30 on 31 October and includes entry to a Halloween after-party. Tickets start at R200.

Riverside Massacre

Adults can head to Riverside Hops at The Riverside Hotel in Durban North on Halloween night for Riverside Massacre.



The event starts at 18:00 and includes DJs, Halloween-themed food and drink specials, live entertainment and a best-dressed competition.

Tickets start at R150, and the event is strictly for over-21s.

Barket by Night

Halloween isn’t just for humans. Barket by Night takes place at Ridley Park in Malvern on 24 October, bringing together dogs, families and local vendors for a Halloween-themed evening.



There will be trick-or-treating, best-dressed competitions, live music, games, a photo booth and other activities. The event also raises funds for KZN Doghouse.

Halloween at the KZN Museum

Pietermaritzburg’s KwaZulu-Natal Museum is hosting a family Halloween evening on 31 October.

The event includes a reptile show, magic show, Halloween scare area and a best-dressed competition. It runs from 17:00 to 20:00, with tickets priced between R65 and R80.



Pretoria

Pretoria has its own large-scale Halloween music event at Heartfelt Gardens on 31 October.

The Halloween 2026 festival runs from 13:00 until midnight and features acts including Silverstein, Ruff Majik, PHFAT, The Tazers, Fuzigish and Human Nebula.

The event is strictly over-18s. General admission starts at R349, while VIP tickets are R899.



For something more atmospheric, a Halloween Mystery Ghost Tour is also taking place in Pretoria on 31 October.

The tour runs from 19:00 to 23:00 and starts at Huckleberry’s Restaurant, with participants travelling in their own cars as part of a convoy. Tickets start at R329.

Gqeberha

Halloween celebrations aren’t limited to the country’s biggest cities.



The Music Kitchen in Gqeberha is hosting Halloweekend Part II on 31 October, with local acts including Rejects, Twiza, Boiling Point and Mezzanine Floor.

Doors open at 19:00, with tickets costing R100 online or R150 at the door.

For something less frightening, The Beach Hotel in Summerstrand is hosting a Halloween-themed afternoon tea on 31 October. It starts at 14:30 and costs R185 per person.



Bloemfontein

Bloemfontein is also getting in on the Halloween action with Common Ground: The Orange Experience at Du Monye Art Gallery in Bayswater.

Running from 14:00 on 31 October into midnight, the event combines art, music, creative activities and an after-dark experience with spooky vibes. Tickets start at R100, and the event is family-friendly.

The biggest events are likely to draw crowds, so it’s worth checking ticket availability and age restrictions before heading out, particularly for the larger Halloween parties on 30 and 31 October.

World.title: Both Sides | Why Is South Africa So Violent? Prof Garth Stevens On The Psychology Behind It | 14 October 2026
World.content:
Why South Africa's Violence Problem Is Bigger Than The People Who Commit It

When violence shocks a society, one of the first questions is usually about the person responsible. What kind of person could do this? Were there warning signs? Was there something psychologically different about them? These are understandable questions, particularly when crimes are brutal or appear to repeat. But focusing too narrowly on the offender can obscure a harder possibility: violence is also shaped by the society in which it occurs.

South Africa's history makes that distinction especially important. Clinical psychologist Professor Garth Stevens describes violence as having functioned for generations as a social instrument, used both to subjugate and to resist. That does not mean history mechanically produces today's violent offender. It means violence has occupied an unusually familiar place in the country's political and social imagination. Stevens describes this legacy as a kind of "wound of history".

History, however, is only one layer. Extreme inequality, unemployment, weakened institutions and failures of governance can alter the environment in which violence occurs. Institutions matter partly because they impose boundaries: the police, courts, schools, social services, families and community structures all help determine what behaviour is restrained, punished, tolerated or normalised. When those systems become inconsistent or lose legitimacy, the consequences extend beyond service delivery. They change what people believe will happen after rules are broken.

That is why South Africa's response to violence cannot be reduced to policing alone. The criminal justice system remains essential, particularly when lives are at risk, but prevention starts much earlier and extends much further. It includes whether children learn that aggression is strength, whether men are socialised into entitlement, whether abusive behaviour is challenged before it escalates, whether rehabilitation works, and whether somebody leaving prison has a realistic route back into ordinary life.

This wider lens is particularly important when examining violence against women. Stevens argues that misogyny can become more dangerous when it is combined with entitlement and objectification. Once another person is regarded less as an autonomous human being and more as an object over which power can be exercised, the psychological distance to violence can shrink. His argument is not that misogynistic thinking automatically produces physical violence; it is that attitudes, power and socialisation are part of the environment in which violence becomes possible.

That systemic argument is increasingly reflected in South Africa's institutional response to gender-based violence and femicide. Government's October 2026 recovery plan places policing alongside investigation, forensic processing, prosecution, community safety and challenges to harmful social attitudes. A separate national inquiry is examining how the criminal justice system handles reporting, victim support, investigation and pre-trial processes in GBV cases. In other words, even the formal response increasingly recognises that violence cannot be isolated to the moment of the offence. South African Government

Psychology adds another necessary caution. Risk factors are not destiny. Stevens rejects the idea of an inevitable line between a difficult childhood, particular personality traits and future violence. Some indicators can increase risk, but prediction is not certainty. The same principle applies to criminal profiling: patterns

can assist investigators, but the moment a profile becomes a stereotype, investigators risk seeing only evidence that confirms what they already expect.

The uncomfortable conclusion is that reducing violence requires two kinds of work at once. South Africa needs institutions capable of finding, prosecuting and managing dangerous offenders. But it also needs to confront the historical, economic, institutional and gendered conditions in which violence is repeatedly reproduced. Catching the person who commits an act of violence is justice. Building a society in which fewer people reach that point is prevention.

References

· Professor Garth Stevens, conversation with Randall Abrahams, Both Sides, October 2026. · South African Government, Government on Gender-Based Violence and Femicide, 1 October 2026. South African Government

· Commission for Gender Equality, SAHRC and CRL Rights Commission, Joint National Inquiry into the

· criminal justice system response to GBVF, August 2026.

Catch up on all Both Sides episodes here: https://www.enca.com/both-sides-podcast

World.title: Rosemary Ndlovu, co-accused slapped with 10 years' imprisonment
World.content:
KEMPTON PARK - Former police officers Rosemary Ndlovu and Nomsa Mudau have each been sentenced to 10 years in prison for plotting the murder of Mudau’s husband, Justice Mudau

The Kempton Park Magistrates’ Court found them guilty of incitement to commit murder in 2018.

Gauteng National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) spokesperson Magaboke Mohlatlole said the court heard that Ndlovu approached a man and asked him to help Mudau arrange her husband’s killing.

READ | Rosemary Ndlovu, co-accused sentencing postponed

According to Mohlatlole, the man had previously been involved in the murders of Ndlovu’s family members.

“Several telephone conversations and meetings subsequently took place between Mudau and the man in Tembisa. During these engagements, Mudau requested that they kill her husband, claiming that he was abusive and involved in extramarital affairs,” he said.

Mohlatlole said the court further heard that Mudau intended to pay the man after claiming insurance benefits following her husband’s death.

READ | Rosemary Ndlovu, co-accused found guilty of inciting murder

“The man later alerted Justice Mudau (the husband) to the plot. He subsequently reported the matter to the South African Police Service (SAPS), leading to the arrest of Ndlovu and Mudau.”

Ndlovu is already serving six life sentences following her conviction and sentencing in November 2021 for the murders of five family members and her partner for financial gains through life insurance and funeral policy payouts.

According to Mohlatlole the10-year sentence imposed on Ndlovu will run concurrently with the current sentences she is serving.

World.title: Saudi league postpones three matches after Houthi attacks
World.content:
RIYADH - The Saudi Arabian football league (SPL) has postponed three fixtures, including one involving Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr, following the dramatic escalation in the country's war with the Houthis.

The matchweek nine fixtures have been pushed back in the calendar for "logistical considerations, taking into account the mandatory minimum rest period between matches", according to a statement published on Tuesday on the SPL's website.

The meeting between league leaders Al Hilal and Al Riyadh and the match between Al Ittihad and Al Shabab have been postponed to December 19, while the clash between Al Ahli and Ronaldo's Al Nassr has been rescheduled for March 6, 2027.

The SPL added, however, that the other matchweek nine fixtures "will be played according to the previously announced schedule with no changes".

On Monday, Al Nassr's AFC Champions League match against Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana in Riyadh was delayed by an hour after the coalition announced it had intercepted a missile fired by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital.

A violent battle between a Saudi-led coalition and Yemen's Houthis has erupted in recent days, with missile strikes on airports and energy facilities across the kingdom.

The latest round of fighting was triggered by Houthi strikes on Riyadh's international airport at the weekend that left 13 people dead and operations suspended in the worst attack since 2015.

World.title: Eastern Cape man slapped with life sentence for relative's mob killing
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Aphelele Tshangela, a 33-year-old man from Eastern Cape, has been sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of his relative, Sandi Tshangela.

Sandi was killed in a mob attack on 14 September 2021; among those parts of the incident was Tshangela and five other participants.

According to Eastern Cape National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) regional spokesperson Luxolo Tyali, the court heard how Sandi had set a man's house alight following an altercation between the two at a local tavern.

READ | UPDATE: Zolani Tete murder case postponed

Tshangela and others searched for him throughout the night before finding him the following morning.

“They found [Sandi] at approximately 6am the following morning and subjected him to a prolonged assault, beating him with sticks and dragging him along the ground with a rope. The assault continued for several hours, and the deceased died at approximately 11am,” Tyali detailed.

Tyali said five of the participants pleaded guilty and were sentenced to 25 years in prison each.

READ | State alleges funeral policy claim at heart of four-month-old baby's murder plot

However, Tshangela pleaded not guilty, resulting in his trial being separated from that of his co-accused, Tyali added.

“Among the compelling evidence presented by the state was the testimony of his accomplices, who placed him at the scene and implicated him in the attack. Tshangela also made admissions during the trial and conceded that he had played a leading role in the incident. He was subsequently convicted of murder.”

Tyali said the NPA reiterates that vigilantism is not justice and that it remains committed to “prosecuting perpetrators of violent crime and ensuring that justice is delivered for victims, their families and affected communities”.

World.title: Laycock makes history with record-breaking five-wicket over
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Kaneez Tuskers’ Chad Laycock etched his name into the history books with a remarkable six-wicket haul against Momentum Multiply Titans in the YesPlay Pro20 Cup on Tuesday, recording figures of 6/26 in a record-breaking bowling performance.



Laycock became the first bowler to claim four wickets in four consecutive deliveries and the first to take five wickets in a single over in South African T20 cricket.



His figures also set a new competition record, surpassing the previous best of 6/29 recorded by Beuran Hendricks in 2014.



After electing to bowl first in Pietermaritzburg, Tuskers initially struggled to contain the Titans, who raced to a 112-run opening partnership through Lhuan-dre Pretorius and Sinethemba Qeshile.



Laycock provided the breakthrough, dismissing Pretorius for a blistering 81 off 36 balls.



Qeshile followed three overs later for 46, while Dewald Brevis added 33 before falling to Bamanye Xenxe.



However, it was the 19th over that belonged to Laycock. He dismissed Leus du Plooy before removing Dayyaan Galiem, Aphiwe Mnyanda, Janco Smit and Esosa Aihevba in four consecutive deliveries, bringing the Titans' innings to a dramatic close at 204.

Issued by: Cricket South Africa

World.title: Cosatu elects new leaders as Losi and Shingange take top posts
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Cosatu has elected new leadership at its 15th National Congress taking place in Kempton Park.

The trade union federation's outgoing president, Zingiswa Losi, has been elected as the new general secretary. She defeated the incumbent Solly Phetoe by 996 to 809 votes.

Losi will be deputised by Gerald Twala, who was elected unopposed.

Losi is the first woman to be elected to the powerful general-secretary post of Cosatu.

Mike Shingange was elected president, beating Mabutho Cele with 973 votes to 836.

Susan Khumalo was elected as first deputy president. She defeated Duncan Luvuno by 915 votes to 882.

Mbali Blose was elected unopposed as second deputy.

Kgomotso Makhupola will hold the trade union federation's purse. Her 966 votes were enough to secure the treasurer position over Mike Manganye with 832.

World.title: LIVESTREAM | Shadrack Sibiya continues bid for bail
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Disgraced former Deputy Police Commissioner Shadrack Sibiya is expected back in court on Wednesday as his bail hearing continues.

The proceedings took a dramatic turn on Tuesday when a voice recording introduced serious new allegations into the case.

In the recording, businessman Serge Cabonge allegedly claims that Sibiya received money from alleged crime boss Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala.

Cabonge also allegedly claims that a judge advised him to leave the country after his name surfaced at the Madlanga Commission.

The inquiry has indicated that it plans to obtain Cabonge’s statement as the allegations come under further scrutiny.

World.title: South Africa's water crisis: Is poor municipal management to blame?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Poor municipal management, weak governance, and inadequate infrastructure investment are exacerbating South Africa's water crisis.

Futuregrowth investment analyst Taariq Mohamed says the problem is not necessarily a lack of funding, but how available funds are spent and managed.

Municipalities currently owe water boards more than R25-billion.

Mohamed says poor financial management and insufficient infrastructure investment are hampering municipalities’ ability to maintain and repair water systems, worsening shortages.

He says South Africa’s water availability has also come under pressure from lower average rainfall and population growth, which has increased by about 37% over the past two decades.

While South Africa is naturally water-scarce, Mohamed argues that poor municipal management is compounding the problem.

World.title: Kenya confirms second Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health workers in personal protective equipments against Ebola. [Courtesy]

Kenya has confirmed a second case of Ebola, raising the country’s total to two confirmed infections and one death as health authorities intensifies contact tracing, quarantine and surveillance to prevent further transmission.

In a press release issued on October 14, 2026, Director General for Health Dr Patrick Amoth said the latest patient is a 39-year-old man who is a close family member of the first confirmed case.

The man had already been placed under quarantine and was receiving daily monitoring when he developed fever, fatigue and joint pains on October 13.

Health teams immediately isolated him and collected samples for testing. The National Virology Reference Laboratory and the KEMRI-CDC laboratory independently returned positive results for Ebola, specifically Bundibugyo Virus Disease.

The patient has since been admitted to a designated treatment centre, where trained medical personnel are providing supportive care.

The Ministry said the early detection demonstrated the effectiveness of the containment measures, noting that the patient’s existing quarantine status had helped prevent further exposure.

“This is the response working as designed,” the Ministry stated, adding that updates on the patient’s condition would be provided as appropriate.

Authorities have stressed that the two confirmed cases are linked and that there is currently no evidence of transmission within the wider community.

However, the emergence of a second case underscores the importance of sustained vigilance, particularly as investigations continue to establish whether other people may have been exposed.

According to the Ministry, 128 contacts associated with the first case have been identified. By October 13, health teams had traced 113, including 108 who are quarantined in Kenya and undergoing daily clinical assessments and temperature checks for 21 days following their last potential exposure.

Five other contacts are outside the country, and the relevant health authorities have been notified under the International Health Regulations of 2005. Efforts to trace the remaining 15 contacts are ongoing.

Investigators are also assessing people who may have interacted with the second patient after he developed symptoms, including quarantine personnel and healthcare workers.

The Ministry said anyone among the identified contacts who develops symptoms will be isolated and tested immediately.

Infection prevention and control measures have also been strengthened at quarantine and treatment facilities, with protective equipment provided to medical personnel.

The response is being coordinated under national public health regulations, while the World Health Organization has been notified. Kenya has not imposed restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings.

Amoth urged Kenyans to remain calm, avoid speculation and seek medical attention promptly if symptoms develop.

“Ebola is not spread through the air; it spreads through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of a person who is sick with, or has died from, the disease,” he said.

He advised anyone experiencing fever, unusual tiredness, muscle or joint pains, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding to seek care at the nearest health facility.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
