World.title: Liberia: As Hypertension and Obesity Rise, Government Urges Citizens to Get Moving
World.content:
Participants exercise outside the Ministry of Health in Congo Town during Liberia’s first National Exercise and Wellness Day

Summary

The health ministry has launched a monthly National Exercise and Wellness Day as the country confronts rising risks from hypertension, diabetes, obesity and other chronic or “noncommunicable” diseases.

A national health survey found nearly one in four adults had raised blood pressure, while six in ten were overweight obese, putting them at heightened risk. Few of those with raised blood pressure are taking medication.

Health officials are urging Liberians to make physical activity, healthier eating and regular health checks part of their everyday lives.

By Tetee Gebro, gender and health correspondent with New Narratives

CATHOLIC JUNCTION, Monrovia – Rain was falling Saturday morning when Nadia S. Jolo joined a group of people walking from through Monrovia’s streets as part of the country’s first National Exercise and Wellness Day.



For the 51-year-old, getting wet was not enough to turn her back. Just days earlier, Jolo had watched a colleague at work collapse from a stroke. Jolo has hypertension herself. The incident frightened her. So when Jolo, who works with the Ministry of Health’s Malaria Division, heard about Saturday’s walk, she decided to join.

“I need to exercise. I need to reduce my diet,” Jolo said.

Jolo is among a growing number of Liberians confronting noncommunicable diseases such as hypertension, stroke and diabetes – illnesses that can develop without obvious symptoms and lead to strokes, heart disease and other illnesses, and premature death. Liberians’ vulnerability was documented in a FrontPage Africa/New Narratives series last year . They are called chronic or “lifestyle” diseases because they are mostly caused by lifestyle decisions – a diet heavy in sugar, processed foods and fat – lack of exercise and sleep, smoking and too much stress. NCDs are now the second most common cause of death in Sub Saharan Africa.

Liberia’s 2022 STEPS survey , — a nationwide World Health Organization-supported survey that measures NCDs and their risk factors among adults — found nearly one in four adults aged 18 to 69 had raised blood pressure and almost six in ten were overweight or obese, putting them in the danger zone. More than eight in ten people found with raised blood pressure were not taking medication for it meaning they were at great risk of developing a chronic disease.

The growing burden has prompted President Joseph Boakai to declare the last Saturday of every month National Exercise and Wellness Day, part of a government effort to encourage physical activity and prevent noncommunicable diseases. Six to eight a.m. on the last Saturday of every month will be reserved for the nationwide observance. It calls on government institutions, businesses, schools and communities to participate in activities including walking, jogging, cycling, stretching, health education and screenings.

“This helps the Ministry of Health to be able to reinforce the issue of physical activity because it helps to minimize those risks,” said Jamesetta Smith, director of the Ministry’s Noncommunicable Diseases and Injury Unit.

Saturday’s inaugural event was a 4.7 kilometer walk from Catholic Junction on Tubman Boulevard to the Ministry of Health off SKD Boulevard in Congo Town.

Rosetta Stubblefield, 70, right, participates in Liberia’s first National Exercise and Wellness Day.

Regular physical activity can help prevent and manage NCDs including heart disease and diabetes and can lower the risk of developing hypertension. Health experts also recommend healthier diets, avoiding tobacco and harmful alcohol use, and regular screening for conditions such as high blood pressure and diabetes.

“Most people think you have to go to the supermarket and buy something expensive, but we have potato greens, cassava leaves, we have our palava sauce, our okra,” Smith said.

The Ministry is also urging Liberians to regularly check their blood pressure and blood sugar so that people with abnormal readings can be identified early and referred to health facilities for treatment. And they’re also urging them to make exercise a daily thing.

“We want to enforce it beyond just that one day,” Smith said. “We want to make it as part of our lifestyle and culture in our country.”

The Ministry plans to work with other government agencies and institutions to develop their own exercise routines rather than create a separate government-run exercise program. Institutions can choose their own days for regular physical activity. The initiative is also intended to extend across all 15 counties.

For some participants at Saturday’s event, fitting exercise in has been challenging. Jolo had not exercised regularly in two years. When she was diagnosed with hypertension, her doctor told her to exercise regularly, eat healthier and stop drinking alcohol. She stopped drinking, but her busy work schedule got in the way of her exercising. She says this walk gave her the encouragement she needed to reset.

Ansumana Morris, a 61-year-old retired employee of the Liberia Petroleum Refining Company, said a doctor previously told him that his cholesterol was high and advised him to watch his diet and exercise. But Morris admits that he has struggled to exercise. Morris blamed his own “laziness”. “I’ve not been regular,” he said. “Sometimes I do and sometimes I don’t.”

He said the new national exercise day could give people like him another reason to get moving. He plans to return for the next event.

Dr. Olushayo Olu, the World Health Organization representative to Liberia, said noncommunicable diseases are increasing in Liberia, as they are in other African countries. One of the dangers, he said, is that people can live with hypertension without realizing it.

“If you have high blood pressure, you don’t know,” Olu said in an interview with New Narratives after participating in Saturday’s walk. “You are fine, you are okay, until you get a problem.”

“Liberians should not only make it a monthly thing,” Olu said. “They can put their exercise regime into their daily life.”

Nadia S. Jolo, 51, joins the National Exercise and Wellness Day walk in the rain in Monrovia.

Smith acknowledged that public awareness of noncommunicable diseases remains limited and that funding to address them is inadequate. She said health donors – which have funded more than 50 percent of Liberia’s health care until last year’s cuts – have traditionally directed support toward communicable diseases that need heavy medical intervention including malaria, HIV and tuberculosis. Those donors expect government to take on more of the burden of their own healthcare starting with education.

“It’s now time for our donor community, our government to shift our attention and support to NCDs,” Smith said.

Smith said about 63 health facilities supported by the World Diabetes Foundation are providing free diabetes services and treatment. Government health facilities also provide services for hypertension and diabetes, she said. Some services charge minimal fees intended to help facilities maintain supplies.

The Ministry is also encouraging communities and businesses to organize their own exercise events to serve as an opportunity for early detection. People found with abnormal blood pressure or blood sugar readings can be referred to health facilities.

For Rosetta Stubblefield, 70, the message about exercise was familiar.

Stubblefield travelled from ELWA Junction to join Saturday’s walk despite the rain. She also has hypertension. She used to exercise but had stopped. After hearing about the government’s exercise day on the radio Friday, she decided to come out.

“You don’t have to have symptoms or be diagnosed,” Stubblefield said. “Your body needs to move.”

For Jolo, however, the warning was more immediate. This time, she said, she knows exercise must be a priority.

“I will join the march every last Saturday,” Jolo said. “And even at my house, I will be doing it in my yard.”

This story was a collaboration with New Narratives .

World.title: Liberia: Tappita Student Leader Urges UL to Resume Classes Amid Shutdown, Proposes Online Learning
World.content:
Monrovia — The President of the Tappita District University and College Students Association (TADUCSA), Effort N. Karr, has called on the University of Liberia administration to urgently resume academic activities, proposing online classes and the use of the Fendall campus to prevent further disruption to students’ education.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

In a press statement issued Tuesday, October 13, Karr appealed to University of Liberia President Dr. Layli Maparyan and her administration to introduce alternative learning arrangements while renovation work continues at the university’s main campus.



The appeal comes amid the suspension of academic activities at the University of Liberia following strike actions by the University of Liberia Faculty and Staff Association over staff and faculty benefits and concerns about the institution’s deplorable conditions.

It is not yet clear whether the demands for faculty and staff benefits that prompted the strike have been addressed. Meanwhile, renovation work has commenced at the university’s Capitol Hill campus, leaving students awaiting clarity on when academic activities will resume.

The disruption has left students waiting for classes to resume, raising concerns about potential delays to academic calendars, graduation plans and future opportunities.

Karr, who represents students from Tappita Statutory District in Nimba County attending tertiary institutions across Liberia, said the university’s infrastructure improvements were necessary but should not bring academic activities to a complete standstill when alternative arrangements could be made.

“Our position is clear: Renovation should improve the university, not unnecessarily suspend the education of its students,” Karr said.

He noted that while several other universities across Liberia had commenced academic activities, University of Liberia students remained uncertain about when regular classes would resume.

According to him, the administration should consider practical measures that would allow students to continue their education without waiting for renovation work to be completed.

Proposes Online Classes, Fendall Campus

Karr outlined three recommendations he believes could help minimize the disruption.

First, he called on the administration to introduce online classes for students assigned to the main campus, where renovation work is ongoing. He argued that virtual learning would allow students to continue their academic programs while physical improvements proceed.

Second, he urged the university to consider resuming regular in-person classes at its Fendall campus, provided the necessary facilities and learning conditions are available.

The proposal, he said, would allow students who can be accommodated at Fendall to return to classrooms rather than remain idle during the interruption.

Third, Karr called for the administration to communicate a clear reopening plan, including a timeline for the resumption of academic activities and arrangements to ensure equitable access to learning opportunities for students at both campuses.

He said clear communication would help students plan their academic and personal lives while reducing uncertainty surrounding the university’s operations.

Warns of Consequences for Students

The TADUCSA president said prolonged delays in the resumption of classes could have significant consequences for students who have invested time, money and personal sacrifices in pursuing higher education.

He emphasized that students’ educational aspirations should remain central to decisions concerning the university’s operations, particularly when disruptions threaten to extend their time in school.

“Students invest their time, financial resources, and aspirations in their education,” Karr said, warning that prolonged delays could affect academic calendars, graduation plans and future opportunities.

He acknowledged the importance of infrastructural development, noting that improved facilities are essential to creating a better learning environment. However, he argued that renovation and academic activities should be coordinated to avoid unnecessary interruptions.

For students, the concern extends beyond the temporary closure of classrooms to the uncertainty surrounding when they will be able to return and how the interruption might affect their academic progress.

Karr said the administration could address these concerns through responsible planning, constructive dialogue and practical arrangements that allow learning to continue while renovation work is underway.

Calls for Constructive Engagement

Karr stressed that his appeal was not intended to criticize the university administration but to draw attention to the difficulties students are facing.

He urged Maparyan and the relevant authorities to give the proposals serious consideration and take appropriate steps toward reopening academic activities.

“As a student leader, I believe that constructive dialogue, responsible leadership, and practical planning can help address this challenge in the best interest of the student population,” he said.

The Tappita District University and College Students Association brings together students from Tappita Statutory District who are pursuing tertiary education at institutions across Liberia. A significant number of its members attend the University of Liberia, making the disruption particularly consequential for the association’s constituency.

Karr said the association remained committed to advocating for quality education and student welfare, expressing hope that the administration would respond positively to the appeal.

His proposed measures offer possible alternatives to a prolonged suspension of academic activities, although their implementation would depend on the university’s capacity to support online instruction, the readiness of the Fendall campus and decisions by the administration.

The immediate challenge for the university is to address the concerns that prompted the faculty and staff strike while determining how best to restore academic activities and minimize further disruption to students.

For Karr and the students he represents, the central message is that infrastructure improvements and uninterrupted learning should not be treated as competing priorities.

“Education must continue, even while development is taking place,” he said.

World.title: Liberia: ADWANGA Opens Justice Conference, Puts Survivors at Center
World.content:
MONROVIA — The Aiding Disadvantaged Women and Girls Association (ADWANGA) has opened a three-day conference in Monrovia examining how Liberia can address the lasting effects of gender-based violence, strengthen public accountability, and ensure that survivors of the country’s civil conflicts have meaningful access to justice and reparations.

The conference, held under the theme “Constitutional Futures of Justice: Gendered Violence, Decolonizing Reparations, and the Making of Public Accountability in Liberia,” brings together government officials, international partners, researchers, legal practitioners, civil society organizations, and survivor advocates to discuss how emerging justice institutions can respond to the harms caused by Liberia’s conflicts.

The October 12–14 gathering comes as Liberia advances efforts to establish the War and Economic Crimes Court (WECC), renewing debate over how accountability mechanisms should recognize conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, address economic harm, and restore survivors’ dignity.



Opening the conference, ADWANGA Founder and Executive Director Amelia M. Cooper said the discussions were intended to move beyond legal accountability alone and examine what justice should mean for survivors seeking to rebuild their lives.

“For many survivors, justice goes beyond seeing perpetrators held accountable,” Cooper said, explaining that it can also mean recognition of the harm suffered, access to support and services, restoration of dignity, opportunities to rebuild lives, and guarantees that such violence will not happen again.

She urged participants to use the three-day gathering to identify practical approaches to reparations and survivor-centered justice in Liberia and beyond.

Government, UN Officials Call for Survivor-Centered Justice

Deputy Gender Minister Curtis Dorley, speaking on behalf of the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, acknowledged the disproportionate burden of conflict-related violence borne by Liberian women and girls.

He said sexual violence during the civil conflicts left physical, emotional, social, and economic scars that continue to affect survivors, families, and communities.

Dorley stressed that lasting recovery requires more than the absence of conflict, emphasizing the need for recognition of harm, access to justice, restoration of dignity, and concrete measures to help survivors rebuild their lives.

He also underscored the importance of placing survivors at the center of policies and institutions intended to address past abuses.

“Justice must not only be legal and procedural,” Dorley said. “It must also be responsive, inclusive and compassionate.”

He added that the effects of sexual and gender-based violence often extend beyond the immediate incident, affecting survivors’ health, education, livelihoods, family relationships, economic opportunities, and participation in society.

At the opening, Marion Deniaud of the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) welcomed the conference as an opportunity to build on renewed momentum for implementing recommendations of Liberia’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

Deniaud said the legacy of the conflicts includes not only conflict-related sexual violence but also lost livelihoods, psychological trauma, economic vulnerability, and intergenerational harm, including trauma affecting children born as a result of sexual violence.

She emphasized that the proposed War and Economic Crimes Court and the complementary National Anti-Corruption Court must be designed to earn public trust and respond meaningfully to victims and survivors.

According to Deniaud, survivor participation must go beyond information-sharing and help shape the institutions themselves. She called for gender-sensitive court mandates, specialized expertise in gender-based violence, and safeguards that allow victims and witnesses to participate safely.

Three-Day Monrovia Gathering Examines Gender-Based Violence, Reparations, and Accountability as Liberia Advances War Crimes Court Efforts

She also highlighted the importance of mental health and psychosocial support for those engaging with justice processes.

Deniaud cautioned that criminal accountability alone would not be sufficient, urging participants to examine reparations and other forms of redress for physical, psychological, and financial harm.

She called for the conference’s recommendations to be specific, time-bound, and accompanied by follow-up and implementation plans.

Research Highlights Links Between Violence and Economic Harm

The conference also builds on research undertaken by ADWANGA and its partners on sexual and gender-based violence, reparations, and Liberia’s emerging accountability framework.

Anna M. Agathangelou of York University said she and ADWANGA had been working together for years on questions surrounding sexual and gender-based reparations. She recalled a previous gathering in Liberia in June 2024 that examined the relationship between reparations and the proposed War and Economic Crimes Court.

She said the subsequent research was intended to deepen discussion about how reparations could be considered alongside the creation of the court.

Caroline Bowah of the National Investment Commission also highlighted the importance of evidence and the challenges survivors can face when presenting their experiences within formal legal systems.

She questioned whether trauma, fragmented recollections, or difficulties recounting events chronologically could affect how survivors’ testimony is assessed as evidence.

Her remarks reflected a central concern of the conference: how legal institutions can recognize survivors’ experiences without excluding or distorting the realities of trauma.

The program features sessions on gendered violence and economic extraction, the role of evidence in producing legal truth, the proposed WECC as an emerging constitutional institution, and the long-term effects of war on bodies, livelihoods, and communities.

Other discussions will examine institutional legitimacy, trauma and legal recognition, decolonizing reparations, and how justice systems should be funded and structured to remain credible and sustainable.

Building Public Trust in Liberia’s Justice Process

A major focus of the gathering is how Liberia can design accountability institutions that are trusted by the people they are intended to serve.

Deniaud said the proposed court framework must consider whether its mandate adequately covers gender-related crimes, whether it has the necessary expertise, and whether its procedures protect victims and witnesses.

She also encouraged participants to develop recommendations that can inform policymaking and contribute to the implementation of Liberia’s transitional justice commitments.

The conference brings together representatives of government institutions, including the Ministry of Gender and the Office of the War and Economic Crimes Court, alongside international partners and civil society actors.

ADWANGA is convening the gathering with support and collaboration from York University, Medica Mondiale, and Canada’s Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council, according to the conference materials.

Cooper thanked the partners, visiting speakers, researchers, and advocates for participating, while paying tribute to survivors whose experiences underscore the importance of continued efforts toward justice.

As the discussions continue through Wednesday, October 14, the organizers hope to identify practical ways to strengthen reparations, improve institutional accountability, and ensure that survivors’ voices influence the future of justice in Liberia.

The central challenge, participants emphasized, is to ensure that the pursuit of justice addresses not only past violations but also the continuing social, economic, and psychological consequences of violence.

World.title: Liberia: Unrealistic and Blanket Statement: Saar Insurance Describes Call From Aggrieved Teachers For Cancellation Of Health Services Contract With NTAL
World.content:
The Management of Saar Insurance Company has raised serious concerns over what it described “unjustified” call from aggrieved members of the National Teachers Association of Liberia (NTAL) to cancel its provision of health insurance services contract signed with the institution and approved by the Ministry of Education.

By Obediah Johnson

It can be recalled that the aggrieved teachers recently staged a peaceful protest at the headquarters of the NTAL against their leadership headed by Madam Mary Nyumah.



In a 17-count petition, the aggrieved teachers demanded a comprehensive audit of the institution’s account and the reinstatement of their National Security General Samuel Johnson in keeping with a ruling from the labour court.

They also called for the cancellation of the insurance contract signed with SAAR Insurance.

However, they failed to state reasons why the contract should be cancelled.

But addressing a news conference in Monrovia on Tuesday, October 13, the Deputy Managing Director of Saar Insurance, Philip Tamba Cooper, said the company is taken aback by the “blanket statement” made by the aggrieved teachers for the termination of its contract with the NTAL.

He observed that no realistic and justifiable reasons were given by the aggrieved teachers for the cancellation of the contract.

He pointed out that since its establishment in Liberia several years ago, Saar Insurance has been committed to fulfilling all terms and conditions enshrined in contracts signed with its clients, including the Ministry of Education, NTAL and other clients across the country.

Cooper disclosed that the company pays between US$400,000 to US$500, 000 monthly as medical claims to hospitals, clinics and other medical facilities which treated their clients and their respective beneficiaries.

He stressed that though the company remains willing to listen to the concerns of the aggrieved teachers, their call for the cancellation of the contract without any cogent reasons is unacceptable.

“Contract issue is administrative and those who are in authority that supposed to do contract and award it know that we are performing and living up to the terms and conditions of the contract. Our medical service forms and ID cards are financial instruments that our clients can take anywhere, and they cannot be denied. We have hospitals and clinics in almost all of the 15 counties.”

Cooper, however, encouraged the aggrieved teachers to channel their grievances in a peaceful manner instead of using its contract signed with the NTAL as a scapegoat to settle scores with their leadership.

He said the company is not troubled by any call for the cancellation of its contract because, it continues to act in line with the terms and conditions in the respective contracts signed with its clients.

Speaking further, Cooper pointed out that the company has put in adequate systems and modified its policy to protect and guarantee the welfare of clients.

He added that principle insured can now access medical centers and hospitals with only their Identification or medical insurance cards, instead of the medical health insurance forms that are regularly used for their beneficiaries.

Meanwhile, the company raised concerns over the abuse of its insurance policy by others.

Individuals who are not insured normally visit hospitals, medical and other health facilities to seek medical treatment with the insurance ID cards of others.

Cooper said the company has confiscated scores of fraudulent ID cards that were attempted to be used by them.

He, however, used the occasion to call on Liberian journalists to always cross-check their stories before publication.

Cooper further cautioned against the fabrication of new stories and the practice of yellow journalism in Liberia.

He assured clients that the company would continue to improve and add value to its insurance schemes and services being rendered.

He stressed that Saar Insurance would also pay its claims on time.

World.title: COMMENT: Copper Queens showed the hunger Zambia needs
World.content:
The Copper Queens have done it again.

Down 2-1 from the first leg in Kampala, many had written them off. But on Tuesday evening at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium, Barbra Banda and her charges showed what it means to wear the Zambian colours with pride – fighting back to thrash Uganda 4-1 and advance 5-3 on aggregate to the next Olympic qualifying round.

This victory is more than just about football. It is about resilience, belief and home advantage.

As Rachael Kundananji rightly put it, “We know well our stadium Levy Mwanawasa.” That statement speaks volumes about the power of home support. The Ndola crowd turned up, braved the heat, and lifted the Queens when it mattered most.

Captain Barbra Banda’s brace, coupled with goals from Natasha Nanyangwe and Eneless Phiri, shows the depth of talent in this squad under Coach Charles Haalubono.

But the journey gets tougher. Ghana awaits in February, after thrashing Mauritius 10-nil on aggregate. Ghana will not be Uganda.

Going forward, FAZ, Government and the corporate world to invest more in the Copper Queens.

Early preparations, competitive friendlies and adequate support are not a favour, but a necessity.

With adequate preparations, a place at the 2028 Olympic Games is within reach.

Ghana is beatable.

For now, congratulations Copper Queens. You have made Zambia proud.

World.title: Kopala Inter-Company Relay rescheduled
World.content:
Zambia Athletics (ZA) has announced the rescheduling of the much-anticipated KCM Kopala Inter-Company Relay – ICR – 2026 scheduled for Chingola.

The event, which was scheduled for 17th October 2026, will now take place on Saturday, 28th November 2026, at Nchanga Stadium in Chingola.

Zambia Athletics General Secretary Teddy Shimishi says all confirmed participants, partners and sponsors have been informed.

Shimishi says going forward, the Kopala ICR will be held annually on the last Saturday of November, as was the case last year.

He has advised all registered participants not to travel to Chingola this weekend, and regrets any inconvenience caused.

“All confirmed participants, partners and sponsors have been informed of the date change.All Registered Participants are hereby informed not to travel to Chingola this weekend. Zambia Athletics regrets the inconvenience this may have caused but remains committed to hosting a successful event,” Shimishi said.

According to ZA, after Kitwe last year, Chingola is hosting in 2026, with ambitions to take it to Choma, Kaputa and every province.

The 2026 edition is expected to attract more than 50 companies, over 1,000 participants and thousands of spectators with a budget of approximately K850,000.

World.title: UPND Will Not Defend Members Who Attacked Mwila, Says Mwiimbu
World.content:
The United Party for National Development (UPND) has condemned the attack on former Patriotic Front (PF) secretary-general Mr Davies Mwila at the Supreme Court in the strongest terms. The party has warned that any of its members involved will face the law alone, with no protection and no legal representation.

In the same briefing, the ruling party rejected claims attributed to Mr Mwila that it was responsible for the death of former minister Honourable Mutotwe Kafwaya and of a youth killed in a township while playing music. It described the claims as preposterous and highly mischievous, and challenged him to produce evidence.

Former Home Affairs Minister Mr Jack Mwiimbu, who chairs the UPND Legal and Constitutional Affairs Committee, delivered the party’s position at a media briefing in Lusaka. He said the incident at the country’s highest court was unfortunate and that the party did not condone any act of lawlessness.

“We, as UPND, would like to state categorically that we condemn in the strongest terms possible the action of individuals who harassed and assaulted the former Secretary-General of the Patriotic Front at the Supreme Court grounds,” Mr Mwiimbu said.

He said the attack should be condemned by every right-thinking Zambian, regardless of political affiliation.

Mr Mwiimbu reminded party members of a warning President Hakainde Hichilema has repeated on several occasions. The UPND, the Head of State has said, will not support lawlessness of any kind, and members who break the law will not be shielded by the party.

“If any of our members are involved in lawlessness, they are on their own,” Mr Mwiimbu said.

He called on the security wings of the State to identify everyone involved and bring them to book, insisting that political connections would count for nothing.

“There are no sacred cows,” Mr Mwiimbu said. “We have stated on several occasions, through ourselves as officers of the UPND and the President of the Republic of Zambia, that there is no one who is above the law, and we have endeavoured to ensure that the rule of law is observed. There is no exception to ensuring that the law is implemented.”

The former minister said the party expected the police to act quickly and without fear or favour.

“We hope and believe that the law enforcement agencies will rise above board and ensure that those who are responsible for that act are brought to book immediately,” he said.

He also appealed to the public, including UPND members, to respect the laws of the country and the rights of individuals at all times. That, he said, was the party’s plea to all Zambians, its own supporters included.

Mr Mwiimbu said the location of the attack made it particularly grave, since the Supreme Court and the other courts of Zambia are institutions every citizen is expected to respect.

“The courts of law are supposed to be held in highest esteem and be accorded the decorum and respect that they deserve,” he said.

The attack, he said, exposed a dangerous belief among some people that they could act without consequence.

“What happened shows that other members have impunity, thinking that they can do anything and get away with it. We will not allow, as a party, for such things to happen in this country,” Mr Mwiimbu said.

Having condemned the assault, the UPND turned its attention to Mr Mwila himself. Mr Mwiimbu said the party took great exception to statements attributed to the former PF secretary-general in a newspaper published on the same day, in which he allegedly blamed the UPND for deaths in the country.

The first was the death of Honourable Mutotwe Kafwaya. Mr Mwiimbu said Zambians were aware that the circumstances surrounding the former minister’s death were under investigation. Government had made various statements on the matter, he said, and the facts would be brought to light very soon.

“It is therefore irresponsible for Mr Mwila to allege that the UPND is responsible,” Mr Mwiimbu said.

The second claim related to a youth who was killed in a township while playing music. Mr Mwiimbu said Mr Mwila had attributed that death to the ruling party, a claim he called preposterous and highly mischievous.

“In the same light, it is irresponsible for Honourable Mwila to state that the UPND killed a youth who was playing music in the township,” he said.

The former minister challenged Mr Mwila to back both claims with proof.

“Let him lay evidence on the table to show that it is the UPND who are responsible. The UPND as a party has never killed anybody. We are on record condemning violence in this country,” Mr Mwiimbu said.

To make his case, he pointed to the UPND’s own dead. The party was a victim of political violence before the 2021 general election, he said. During the most recent polls, it lost one of its members in Kaputa.

Even then, Mr Mwiimbu said, the UPND did not attribute the Kaputa death to any specific political party. It left the matter to law enforcement agencies to investigate and bring the culprits to court, and he said Mr Mwila should have shown the same restraint over the deaths of Honourable Kafwaya and the township youth.

“It is therefore unacceptable for a senior citizen to make such allegations against the UPND,” he said.

Mr Mwiimbu closed the briefing by returning to the party’s own members. He said the UPND had at all times instructed its members not to take part in such activities, and he repeated the President’s warning.

“I would like to repeat the words of the President, that if any one of our members is involved in criminal activities, they are on their own. We will not be there to defend them,” Mr Mwiimbu said.

As chairperson of the legal committee, he made clear that the party’s lawyers would not step in. The committee would not offer legal services to anyone involved in such activity.

The briefing marks a sharper position than the earlier statement from the UPND Media Team. That statement condemned the attack but devoted much of its attention to PF-Pamodzi Alliance National Youth IPS Mr Given Gift Chibale, who had linked the incident to suspected UPND cadres. It challenged him to take any evidence to the police and said the party would report the matter under the cybercrime laws.

The attack happened shortly after the Lima Constituency election petition was adjourned. In that case, UPND candidate Mr Lee Mukupa is challenging the election of National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) candidate Mr Kelvin Kaunda, who won the seat with 22,760 votes against Mr Mukupa’s 8,041. Mr Mwila had attended the hearing in solidarity with Mr Kaunda.

UPND members were at the scene. Former PF Kabwata parliamentary aspirant Mr Clement Tembo, who joined the ruling party earlier this year, said Mr Mwila had insulted him and other UPND members by calling them poverty-stricken. He also said Mr Mwila boasted that he had enough wealth to benefit even Mr Tembo’s next generation. Mr Mwila is also alleged to have mocked the “salt sana” slogan.

“He is misbehaving and insulting as if he is not an elderly person,” Mr Tembo said.

Mr Tembo and a group of supporters followed Mr Mwila into the building, where the former minister ended up on the floor of the reception area. Court officials, onlookers, security personnel and police officers intervened as one man tried to keep beating him.

Chief Justice Mumba Malila condemned the incident as flagrant lawlessness and an assault on the administration of justice. He said law enforcement agencies were investigating and that those responsible would face the full force of the law.

“Unruly conduct and violence will not be tolerated under any circumstances,” Dr Malila said.

Security has since been tightened at the courts, and the Lima hearing resumed later that day before High Court Judge Derrick Mulenga with police reinforcement.

The ruling party has now said publicly that it will neither defend nor represent anyone involved, and the matter rests with the police. No arrests have been announced.

World.title: Mark is off the Mark
World.content:
Some statements condemn violence, and some only use the language of condemnation to cover something else. The statement issued by the UPND Media Team after former Patriotic Front (PF) secretary-general and former Cabinet minister Mr Davies Mwila was beaten at the Supreme Court belongs to the second kind. Mr Mark Simuuwe, you missed the mark.

Here are the facts. On 13 October 2026, Mr Mwila attended the Lima Constituency election petition hearing at the Supreme Court in Lusaka. After the hearing was adjourned, a group followed him into the building, and he ended up on the floor of the reception area. One man tried to keep beating him while he struggled to get up. It took court officials, security personnel and police to pull him away.

Chief Justice Mumba Malila did not hesitate. He called the incident flagrant lawlessness and an assault on the administration of justice, and he said those responsible would face the full force of the law. That is what a clean condemnation sounds like: short, direct and without a political agenda.

The ruling party’s statement started in the same place. It called the attack unfortunate and unacceptable, and it asked the police to investigate without political interference. Then it changed direction.

Most of the statement goes after PF-Pamodzi Alliance youth leader Mr Given Gift Chibale for linking the attack to United Party for National Development (UPND) cadres. It lectures the public about “dragging political institutions into disrepute” and reminds everyone that legal remedies are available against damaging claims. It even turns the beating of an opposition figure into a sermon about “the opposition’s political discipline”, followed by a reminder that Zambians were right to renew the UPND’s mandate.

Read it twice and ask yourself who the statement is really protecting.

The man who says he led the group that followed Mr Mwila into the building is not a stranger to the UPND. Mr Clement Tembo, a former PF Kabwata aspirant who joined the ruling party this year, said openly that he confronted Mr Mwila because Mr Mwila had insulted UPND members. By Mr Tembo’s own account, he and his supporters went after the former minister inside the court building.

So when the party’s media team tells Mr Chibale to separate “evidence from political speculation”, the evidence is not hard to find. Some of it is coming from the party’s own people.

Let me be fair. Mr Mwila is alleged to have provoked the group by mocking the “salt sana” slogan and boasting that his wealth would outlive their poverty. If he said those things, they were careless words from a senior citizen who should know better. But the UPND statement itself says no political disagreement, personal grievance or ideological difference can justify physical attacks or humiliation. On that point the statement is right, and it should have stopped there and acted on it.

What would a genuine response have looked like? It would have named the problem without hedging. It would have said the party has seen the footage, knows some of those involved claim to be its members, and is handing every name to the police. It would have suspended anyone found to have taken part. And it would have apologised to Mr Mwila, an elderly former Cabinet minister who was knocked to the floor of the highest court in the land.

That is what the rule of law means when it is your own people in the frame. The rule of law is easy to defend when it is applied to opponents. The real test is applying it to your own side.

Instead, the public got a statement that condemned violence in one paragraph and spent the rest defending the party’s image and attacking the victim’s camp. The tone is divisive at a time when the country needs calm. It speaks of peace while pointing fingers, and it is the kind of message that tells young cadres the party will cover for them if they go too far.

The courts are supposed to be the last line of defence for justice. They are where the powerful are held to account and the ordinary citizen is protected. When a court building becomes another battlefield in the political war, every Zambian should be worried, whatever their party.

Today it is an opposition figure on the floor. Tomorrow it could be anyone. When justice becomes selective, nobody is safe.

Mark, here is a reminder offered in good faith. Politics was here before all of us and will be here when we are gone. Governments change, and parties that rule today will sit in opposition tomorrow. What follows the loss of power is often the bill for what was covered up while power was held.

You still have time to get this right. Withdraw the lecture, name the problem and apologise to Mr Mwila. Let the police do their work without a party statement standing in front of them.

The Almighty sees everything. The question for those who think they can do whatever they like, whenever they like, and get away with it is a simple one: for how long?

By Choolwe Haatembo

World.title: Chilengi sends 123 officers out of Ndeke House, orders qualifications audit of headquarters staff
World.content:
Health Minister Professor Roma Chilengi has ordered 123 officers out of the Ministry of Health headquarters in Lusaka and back to their original stations. Every remaining post at Ndeke House now faces a qualifications audit, in a clean-up aimed at pushing more staff to the front line of the health service.

An internal assessment found that the 123 officers had been working at headquarters under temporary administrative arrangements. Their positions supported central operations, but they fell outside the ministry’s approved 2021 establishment, which caps headquarters staffing at 403 positions. The ministry described the move as part of a comprehensive institutional clean-up and operational optimisation exercise, aimed at enforcing strict structural compliance and restoring administrative integrity across the healthcare sector.

In a ministerial statement dated 13 October 2026, Prof Chilengi said all the affected officers would be redirected immediately to their substantive stations, where their official pay points and original postings are based. The ministry said the move would eliminate structural redundancies and address critical operational personnel needs across the country.

“This step will immediately bolster healthcare delivery at front-line health facilities and decentralised administrative centres,” Prof Chilengi said.

The return of the 123 officers is only the first phase. Once they have been moved, the ministry will carry out a full qualification and competency assessment of everyone holding a post within the approved 403-member headquarters establishment.

Each position will be measured against established professional standards and job descriptions, to determine whether the officers holding them have the required academic, professional and technical qualifications. Staff who fall short for their headquarters roles will be reassigned to operational stations that match their verified credentials.

“This exercise establishes a vital operational baseline as the ministry of health continues to strengthen governance frameworks, streamline administrative efficiency and deliver high-quality public healthcare across the nation,” Prof Chilengi said.

The ministry said the exercise will strengthen administrative accountability and ensure that staff are deployed in line with approved structures and operational needs. It also expects staffing levels to rise at service delivery points, where patients are seen.

The shake-up comes with the health system under pressure from a cholera outbreak. The Zambia National Public Health Institute (ZNPHI) has recorded 55 new cases and one death in 24 hours, bringing the cumulative number of cases to 874 since the outbreak began.

The cumulative death toll has risen to 23. As of Tuesday, 777 patients had recovered and been discharged, while 74 remained in hospital.

Thirteen districts have been affected. Lusaka has recorded the highest number of cases at 429, followed by Chibombo with 217. Chilanga has 46 cases, Mpulungu 42, Chongwe 36 and Chiengi 33.

Mwansabombwe and Nsama have recorded 20 cases each, Mwense 15 and Nchelenge 11. Chikankata and Monze have two each, and Kalomo has one.

The institute has urged the public to wash their hands with soap and clean water, drink boiled or treated water, cook food thoroughly and use clean toilets. It also stressed proper hygiene when handling food and keeping sanitation facilities clean.

Districts without cases are also preparing. In Lumezi, which has recorded no suspected cases, director of health services Evans Phiri said rapid response teams had been activated at facility and district levels, and health workers had been trained to pick up symptoms early.

Dr Phiri said two facilities had been identified for isolating and managing cases. Rapid diagnostic test kits, medicines and intravenous fluids had been set aside.

“A cholera patient may die just from dehydration, just the loss of fluids in the body. So we have kept fluids just for this cause,” Dr Phiri said.

At Ndeke House, the qualifications review of the 403 approved posts is next. The 123 officers are being returned to their substantive stations, where the ministry says they are most needed.

World.title: Chief Justice condemns Supreme Court attack on Davies Mwila as security is tightened at courts
World.content:
Chief Justice Mumba Malila has condemned the attack on former Patriotic Front (PF) secretary-general and former home affairs minister Davies Mwila at the Supreme Court in Lusaka. He called it flagrant lawlessness and an assault on the administration of justice, and security has since been tightened at the courts to protect judicial officers and the public.

Law enforcement agencies are investigating the incident, the Chief Justice said, and those responsible will face the full force of the law.

“Unruly conduct and violence will not be tolerated under any circumstances,” Dr Malila said in a statement issued on Tuesday.

The confrontation broke out shortly after the court adjourned the Lima Constituency election petition. In that case, United Party for National Development (UPND) candidate Lee Mukupa is challenging the election of National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) candidate Kelvin Kaunda, who won the seat with 22,760 votes against Mr Mukupa’s 8,041.

Mr Mwila had attended the hearing in solidarity with Mr Kaunda. Tension rose when former PF Kabwata parliamentary aspirant Clement Tembo, who joined the UPND earlier this year, complained that Mr Mwila had insulted him and other UPND members who had come to follow the proceedings.

Mr Tembo said the former PF secretary-general had called them poverty-stricken and boasted that he had enough wealth to benefit even Mr Tembo’s next generation. Mr Mwila is also alleged to have mocked the “salt sana” slogan.

“He is misbehaving and insulting as if he is not an elderly person,” Mr Tembo said.

Mr Tembo and a group of supporters, who had been standing at the main entrance, then followed Mr Mwila into the building. Mr Mwila retreated into the reception area and ended up on the floor. Accounts differ on how he fell: some say he slipped while trying to get away, while others say one of the group knocked him down.

Court officials and onlookers restrained one man who tried to keep beating Mr Mwila as he struggled to get back on his feet. Judiciary staff, security personnel and police officers intervened and stopped the situation from escalating further.

Police officers at the scene said security would need to be reinforced when the hearing resumed later in the day before High Court judge Derrick Mulenga. Security has since been stepped up across the courts.

In his statement, Dr Malila urged everyone visiting court premises to conduct themselves with decorum, respect and dignity.

The UPND has also condemned the attack. Its Media Team described the assault as unfortunate and unacceptable in a democratic society governed by the rule of law, and called for a professional, impartial investigation free from political interference.

“No political disagreement, personal grievance or ideological difference can justify physical attacks, intimidation or the humiliation of another person,” the party said.

The UPND also rejected statements attributed to PF-Pamodzi Alliance National Youth IPS Given Gift Chibale, who linked the incident to suspected UPND cadres. It challenged him to hand any evidence to the police and said it would report the matter under the cybercrime laws. The party’s statement did not refer to Mr Tembo.

The Lima petition continues under the tighter security arrangements. Police investigations into the attack are ongoing, and no arrests have been announced.

World.title: ZCTU joins calls for Archbishop Banda to step aside
World.content:
The Zambia Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) has joined calls for Lusaka Archbishop Alick Banda to step away from his position until the criminal case he is defending is concluded. The union says church leaders facing court proceedings must act to protect public confidence in their institutions.

The labour movement adds its weight to a widening list of voices on the matter. Catholic-aligned Members of Parliament, among them Nominated MP Noel Nkoma, Kazungula North MP Clement Andeleki and Rufunsa MP Sheal Mulyata, have already called on the Archbishop to step aside. House of Clergy Zambia and the Anti-Voter Apathy Project (AVAP) have since taken similar positions.

Archbishop Banda faces a charge of possession of property reasonably suspected to have been unlawfully obtained, contrary to Section 319 of the Penal Code, Chapter 87 of the Laws of Zambia. The Drug Enforcement Commission arrested him on 28 September 2026.

ZCTU president Blake Mulala said leaders of religious institutions should be seen to uphold high moral standards. In his view, they should consider stepping aside whenever they face investigations or court proceedings.

“In many churches, leaders facing investigations or court cases are expected to step aside on moral grounds until the matter is concluded. As an overseer of the church, it is important to maintain public confidence and integrity,” Mr Mulala said in Lusaka.

The union leader said the Catholic Church should be guided by its own doctrines and disciplinary procedures in deciding how to handle the matter. Church leaders, he added, should remain above reproach while carrying out their pastoral responsibilities.

House of Clergy Zambia took a similar line, grounding its position in the rule of law. National executive director Reverend Jimmy Ng’ambi said accountability applied to all citizens, regardless of position, profession or religious office.

“As a matter of integrity, wisdom and institutional responsibility, it may be appropriate for a member of the clergy facing serious legal proceedings to voluntarily step aside while the legal process takes its course,” Rev Ng’ambi said.

The cleric drew a firm line between the individual and the institution, saying holding religious office does not exempt anyone from personal responsibility.

“No one is above the law, accountability is not persecution, and a legal case involving an individual cleric is not a battle against the Church,” he said.

Rev Ng’ambi described the Church as an important partner in national development, peacebuilding and moral guidance. He said legal proceedings involving a cleric should not be misread as an attack on Christianity or an attempt to undermine the Church’s role in society.

He was careful to stress that a step-aside would not amount to an admission of guilt. The call, he said, was neither a declaration of guilt nor a legal requirement, but a position based on integrity and the need to safeguard the Church’s standing.

A temporary withdrawal, the House of Clergy leader said, would also stop the case from being portrayed as a confrontation between Government and the Church. He urged citizens to exercise restraint, avoid premature conclusions and respect the presumption of innocence throughout the process.

AVAP national director Richwell Mulwani said his organisation supported calls for the Archbishop to temporarily relinquish his duties until investigations were concluded. He acknowledged, however, that the final decision did not rest with outside groups.

“As AVAP, we feel it would be acceptable for Archbishop Banda to step aside while the matter is being addressed. However, the Catholic Church has its own rules and procedures and it is up to the institution to determine the appropriate course of action,” Mr Mulwani said.

He said the Church should reach its decision in line with its doctrines, while respecting the legal principle that a person is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Not every voice has joined the call. The Southern Africa Centre for the Constructive Resolution of Disputes (SACCORD) urged caution, saying the matter should be handled fairly and without prejudice. Executive director Boniface Muyunda said any call for the Archbishop to step aside should respect both the rule of law and the autonomy of the Catholic Church.

University of Zambia lecturer Professor Bizeck Phiri described the situation as complex. He pointed out that the Catholic Church had not publicly indicated that Archbishop Banda should step aside. The Church, he said, has established doctrines and procedures for matters involving members of the clergy and should be allowed to decide the way forward.

Government has set out its own position. Ministry of Information and Media Permanent Secretary Thabo Kawana has distinguished between the Church as an institution and individual members of the clergy, with Government reaffirming that no person is above the law, whatever their position or religious office.

The case remains before the courts, where the Archbishop is entitled to the presumption of innocence and a full defence. Most of those calling for a step-aside have stopped short of demanding one. Several have left the final word to the Catholic Church, which has not publicly announced any change to the Archbishop’s duties.

World.title: Political parties hail parley speech
World.content:
The ruling United Party for National Development (UPND) says President Hakainde Hichilema’s speech during the official opening of the first session of the 14th National Assembly spelled out clear intent by Government to reduce the cost of living.

UPND Media Director, Mark Simuuwe says the President laid out a blueprint for citizens to be involved in the development agenda of the country.

Mr Simuuwe said there are numerous opportunities that give citizens a platform to improve their livelihood while contributing to the Grow Zambia Agenda, describing the Head of State’s plan as inclusive.

Meanwhile, New Nation Party Acting President, Reuben Samboh says the targets set out by President Hichilema present an opportunity for the private sector to contribute effectively.

And Rev Samboh says the 7 percent economic growth target that Zambia is aiming to attain in three years’ time is realistic.

The opposition leader however called on the Government to instead set a target of 10 percent.

Meanwhile, Rev Samboh urged the private sector to take advantage of the Grow Zambia Agenda, describing President Hichilema’s targets as inclusive.

On Friday, President Hichilema officially opened the first session of the 14th National Assembly, making different pronouncements in various sectors.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 14, 2026
World.content:
Former DR Congo President Joseph Kabila to Lead New Rebel Coalition

Former Democratic Republic of Congo President Joseph Kabila has been named leader of the newly formed Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), a rebel coalition seeking to remove President Félix Tshisekedi's government. Launched in Goma, the movement brings together former leaders of the AFC/M23 alliance, including M23 military leader Sultani Makenga, who was appointed one of Kabila's deputies. The coalition accuses Tshisekedi's administration of corruption, economic mismanagement, insecurity, and weakening democratic institutions. It is vowing to pursue change by all means, including force. Kabila, who ruled from 2001 to 2019, was sentenced to death in absentia for treason last year. The announcement comes amid continued fighting in eastern DR Congo and stalled peace negotiations.



Nigeria Plane Crash Raises Fears of Water Contamination

Residents of Igbokoda in Nigeria's Ondo State are raising concerns about possible water contamination after a Nigerian Air Force plane crash that killed all 25 people on board on October 5. The aircraft crashed into a swamp connected to a river that supplies the community's drinking water. Difficult terrain has hampered efforts to recover the wreckage and victims' remains. Community leaders fear that decaying human remains, possible oil spills and reports of dying fish could threaten public health and local livelihoods. Traditional ruler Afolabi Odidiomo has called for an urgent environmental clean-up and the provision of alternative safe drinking water. Recovery teams are continuing their search, with locating the aircraft's black box among their priorities.

Caine Prize Investigates Zimbabwean Writer Over AI Allegations

The Caine Prize for African Writing is investigating Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Steyn Kundizeza after allegations that he used artificial intelligence to produce his award-winning short story, The Blue Fighter. The controversy followed an article published by The Atlantic that criticised the story and raised questions about its authorship. The prize organisers confirmed they had begun an investigation, saying they have a responsibility to uphold trust within Africa's literary and publishing community. The story centres on Tinashe and his family, whose circumstances deteriorate after his father leaves his profession to pursue his ambition of building fish tanks. Kundizeza previously described winning the 2026 prize as an important recognition of years of writing. He could be stripped of the award if the allegations are proven.

Somalia Sanctions 10 Individuals Over Alleged Al-Shabaab Links

Somalia has added 10 individuals to its national financial sanctions list over alleged involvement in financing or supporting Al-Shabaab, the Al-Qaeda-linked militant group. The National Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Committee said the move aims to disrupt the group's funding networks and strengthen enforcement of counter-terrorism measures. Under the directive, financial institutions, businesses and individuals operating in Somalia are prohibited from conducting transactions with those listed. They must also freeze any assets belonging to the designated individuals and report related transactions to the Financial Reporting Center. The committee did not disclose detailed evidence supporting the designations but warned that violations could result in legal action. Al-Shabaab has waged an insurgency against Somalia's federal government for more than 15 years.

Two Suspected Ebola Cases Test Negative in Kenya's Laikipia County

Health authorities in Kenya's Laikipia County have confirmed that two suspected Ebola cases in Nanyuki tested negative, urging residents to remain calm and avoid spreading unverified information. Concern arose after a patient presented with symptoms resembling Ebola and was admitted to Nanyuki Teaching and Referral Hospital. Laboratory results ruled out the virus. The patient died while receiving treatment. A second suspected case reported by a private hospital also tested negative after samples were analysed at the National Public Health Laboratory. County Health Executive Albert Taiti said precautionary measures had been activated and healthcare workers had been sensitised on identifying and managing suspected infections. Authorities have urged residents to rely on official updates, report suspected cases promptly and continue observing recommended health precautions.

Close 

Malawi High Court Blocks Extradition of Prophet Bushiri to South Africa

Malawi's High Court in Lilongwe has issued a 175-page judgment explaining why it overturned the extradition order against Shepherd Bushiri and his wife, Mary. The court found serious procedural and legal flaws, including that the couple was not allowed to be heard before the order was granted in March 2025. Their lawyer, Wapona Kita, said they can no longer be extradited to South Africa under the quashed order. Kita said that the State would have to appeal the ruling to pursue the matter further. The decision deals a major setback to South Africa's efforts to bring the couple back to face legal proceedings after they returned to Malawi in 2020.

World.title: South Africa: Two Killed in Katlehong Drive-By Shooting - South African News Briefs - October 14, 2026
World.content:
press review

Two Killed in Katlehong Drive-By Shooting

Two people were killed and five others, including a 12-year-old child, were injured in a drive-by shooting in Katlehong on the East Rand, reports EWN. The victims were allegedly returning from a political party member’s memorial service when a gunman opened fire. Gauteng police confirmed that a suspect had handed himself over to authorities. The case, involving charges of murder and attempted murder, has been assigned to the Gauteng Political Killings Task Team for further investigation.

Bail Hearing Continues for Ex-Police Chief



The bail application of former Deputy National Police Commissioner Shadrack Sibiya is expected to continue at the Randburg Magistrate's Court, reports SABC News. Proceedings heard allegations linking the 59-year-old to unlawful activities and the criminal underworld. Sibiya, who was arrested in September, faces charges including the alleged sexual grooming of a 16-year-old girl, rape, human trafficking and contravention of the Firearms Control Act. An investigating officer presented an audio recording involving the complainant’s father and businessman Serge Cabonge, which allegedly supports an affidavit submitted by Sibiya’s wife.

Johannesburg CBD Hit by Fourth Substation Fire

Parts of Johannesburg’s inner city have been left without electricity following another fire at City Power’s central substation, reports EWN. The incident marks the fourth fire at the facility in just over two months, affecting areas including Marshalltown, Wemmer, Selby and sections of Albert, Eloff, Commissioner and Anderson streets. Emergency teams attended the scene, while investigations into the damage and cause of the fire are underway. City Power said previous fires had been linked to suspected vandalism and electricity infrastructure theft, but the cause of the latest incident has not yet been established.
