He further argued that financial considerations alone would not determine the government's decision on Starlink, writing: âIf our policy were driven by money, we would have rolled out the red carpet welcome for you despite opposition from the security agencies.â

Musk, meanwhile, has argued that Starlink's entry would increase competition and expand consumer choice. Responding to arguments against the service, he wrote that competition would benefit ordinary Indians, adding that Ambani's profits might decline but that his business would not cease to exist.

World.title: Evening news wrap: Woman, lover get death sentence in Blue Drum murder case; US ends automatic work permit extensions & more
World.content:

Here are top news stories of the day:

Meerut court sentences Muskan Rastogi, Sahil Shukla to death for Saurabh Rajput murder

A Meerut court sentenced Muskan Rastogi and her lover Sahil Shukla to death for murdering her husband, merchant navy officer Saurabh Rajput, and concealing his dismembered remains in a cement-filled drum in March 2025.

The verdict came 15 days after their conviction, following a trial involving 22 prosecution witnesses.

US ends automatic work permit extensions, raising concerns for Indian H-4 spouses

The Trump administration has finalised a rule ending automatic work permit extensions for eligible foreign nationals awaiting renewals, potentially affecting over one lakh Indian spouses of H-1B visa holders. Applicants covered by the change may have to stop working after their permits expire while renewals are processed.

Air India Frankfurt-Delhi flight diverted to Jaipur after false hijack alert

An Air India Boeing 787-9 carrying around 300 people was diverted to Jaipur after Mumbai air traffic control detected the aircraft transmitting hijack code 7500. The pilots reportedly said all operations were normal, but security protocols required a diversion and checks.

World.title: Delhi protests: Pakistan-linked handles under probe for fake claims of police firing
World.content:
Clash between security personnel and protesters during Delhi protests

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police is investigating social media handles allegedly spreading rumours and inflammatory content during protests demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumarâs resignation in the national capital. The probe has traced the IP address of at least one suspicious handle to Pakistan, police said on Wednesday.Sanjay Bhatia, Additional Commissioner of Police in the Delhi Policeâs Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit said that false claims about police action against demonstrators were circulated online to create panic and provoke unrest.The Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit has a dedicated cyber patrolling team to monitor such content and verify its authenticity, Bhatia told ANI, outlining the police's response to misleading posts."Delhi Policeâs IFSO unit has a dedicated cyber patrolling team that monitors such posts to verify their authenticity and compliance with legal provisions. If we find a post to be factually incorrect, false, a rumor, a threat to public order, defamatory, or likely to incite anarchy, we take action in accordance with the law," he said.Bhatia said the investigation into the Pakistan-linked account was ongoing, along with other cases registered over social media content."When we sought registration details for one such specific handle, the IP address traced back to Pakistan; we are currently investigating that case. The process is ongoing, and we have registered other cases as well; investigations are underway, and we will share further details and evidence with you as they emerge," he said.Giving details of a post that allegedly claimed police were firing at demonstrators, Bhatia said the claim was false and could have heightened tensions."We found a post intended to incite chaos; the handle registered in Pakistan."He further claimed that the handle alleged that the police were opening fire on the demonstrators. "It was a deliberate attempt to whip up a volatile atmosphere based on falsehoods. Since the claim was untrue, we immediately requested the post's removal and registered a case; further action is underway," he said.The Delhi Police had also recently debunked a viral social media video claiming that Rahul Gandhi's residence had come under attack and that gunfire had been reported.According to the police, the footage was from December 2019 and was unrelated to current events. The police said legal action was being initiated against accounts sharing the misleading content and urged users not to circulate unverified videos.The investigation comes amid police action against three Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists over alleged attempts to disturb public peace and instigate others through social media. Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were remanded to five days of judicial custody, while Ajinkya Shinde was bound down for six months to maintain peace and good behaviour.According to a Delhi Police statement, the action followed an incident on October 13 in which the three activists and 11 other CJP members allegedly entered the denotified Jantar Mantar protest site through private premises and obstructed police personnel. CJP has maintained that it will continue to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and challenge the denotification of Jantar Mantar.

World.title: Delhi protest: Journalists slapped with SC/ST Act for casteist slur against ACP on duty
World.content:
NEW DELHI: An Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) in Delhi has accused a woman journalist and two others of making casteist remarks against him, publicly humiliating him and obstructing his official duties during a protest in the national capital on October 3.

The FIR was registered on October 13 at Parliament Street Police Station on the complaint of ACP Vivek Bhagat, who is posted in the Connaught Place subdivision. Journalist Rosy, Gajendra Singh, who is associated with a news portal, and an unidentified person have been named as accused.

The case has been registered under Sections 221, 356(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

Bhagat has been at the centre of allegations of harassment of women protesters during the recent agitation against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Those allegations are being investigated by the Crime Branch.

What the ACP alleged

According to Bhagat's complaint, the incident took place at Buta Singh Roundabout on October 3, when police personnel were deployed to manage a protest called by Neha Bora and others against the Election Commission of India (ECI).





The ACP said the protesters gathered around 2.30 pm and tried to march towards Jantar Mantar. Police personnel announced that restrictions under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were in force and asked the protesters to disperse. When they allegedly refused to leave, the police began detaining them.

He claimed the remarks were made in the presence of her colleague Gajendra Singh and others.

World.title: ‘Advancing our Strategic Partnership’: EAM Jaishankar meets Canadian counterpart Anita Anand as India, Canada push to reset ties
World.content:
NEW DELHI: External affairs minister

met his Canadian counterpart Anita Anand in New Delhi on Wednesday to review bilateral relations, with discussions covering trade, investment, education, energy, defence and people-to-people exchanges.

The two ministers also exchanged views on key regional and global developments and discussed ways to advance the Strategic Partnership between the two countries.

âDelighted to meet FM @AnitaAnandMP of Canada in New Delhi today. Reviewed progress in our ties across trade & investment, education, energy, defence and people-to-people exchanges. Also exchanged views on key regional and global developments. Guided by our leadership and sustained engagement across government and industry, we are advancing our Strategic Partnership,â Jaishankar said in a post on X.

The meeting follows Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's telephone conversation with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday, during which the two leaders agreed to build on the positive momentum in bilateral ties and pursue concrete outcomes across key areas of cooperation.

PM Modi, Carney discuss trade, security and CEPA

PM Modi said the two leaders had a âwarm and productive conversationâ and agreed to work towards tangible results in trade, energy, technology, security and people-to-people ties.





âTogether, India and Canada are contributing towards a more stable and prosperous world,â PM Modi added in his post on X.

When asked about the conversation between both leaders, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal on Wednesday said, "Prime Minister Carney had visited India recently, I mean some months back, and there is a positive momentum in this particular relationship on various aspects of our bilateral cooperation, strategic partnership and its progress in the areas of trade, investment, energy, technology, security, all these aspects that came up for discussion when the two Prime Ministers had their conversation on the bilateral relationship.

So that is where we are."

According to a statement from the Canadian Prime Minister's Office, the leaders welcomed increased engagement over the past year and reaffirmed their commitment to conclude negotiations on the India-Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) at the earliest opportunity.

The agreement is intended to support efforts to double bilateral trade by 2030. The two leaders also welcomed the ongoing Team Canada Trade Mission to India and discussed the impact of geopolitical instability on the Indo-Pacific region, as well as the importance of trusted partners in energy and agriculture.

They also welcomed a bilateral security dialogue held in India the previous week as part of ongoing security and law enforcement engagement at the national security adviser level. Carney thanked PM Modi for his leadership in seeking a peaceful resolution to Russia's war on Ukraine.

The two prime ministers agreed to remain in close contact ahead of Modi's planned visit to Canada in December.

Trade negotiations and corporate delegation

The diplomatic engagement comes as commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal and Canada's minister of international trade, Maninder Sidhu, discuss progress on CEPA negotiations.

Goyal said the discussions focused on a balanced and mutually beneficial agreement that would improve market access and create fresh opportunities for trade and investment.

âDiscussed advancing the India-Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) negotiations, with a focus on a balanced, mutually beneficial agreement that enhances market access and unlocks new trade and investment opportunities.

Confident that the CEPA will provide fresh momentum to bilateral trade and strengthen our economic partnership for shared prosperity,â Goyal said in a post on X.

Sidhu is leading a Canadian corporate delegation of around 300 members on a visit to India, Canada's largest such delegation to the country in three decades.

The delegation is exploring potential joint ventures across sectors including aerospace, clean energy, technology, life sciences, agri-food and forestry.

Sidhu said Canada was also advancing CEPA negotiations to create more opportunities for Canadian businesses and workers.

Anand's third visit to India since June 2025

Anand arrived in India on Tuesday. The MEA described the visit as reflecting sustained high-level engagement and positive momentum in bilateral relations.

World.title: 'Four Indians still in ICU': MEA condemns attack on Saudi airport, oil facilities
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Four Indians injured in an October 10 attack in Saudi Arabia remain hospitalised, including four in intensive care, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Wednesday.

The ministry condemned the recent attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure, including an assault on Aramco headquarters, and called for an immediate halt to such strikes.

MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said 12 people were injured in the October 10 incident. One of them later died. His last rites were performed in Riyadh, as wished by his family, with assistance from the Indian embassy. Of the 11 surviving injured people, three have been discharged, while eight remain in hospital, including four in the ICU.

"Embassy officials are regularly visiting them and staying in touch with their families," Jaiswal said, adding that India remained committed to ensuring the welfare of its nationals abroad.

MEA condemns attacks, stands with Saudi Arabia

Condemning the latest attacks on Saudi Arabia, Jaiswal said India stood in solidarity with the country's people and government.

"There has been a string of attacks in Saudi Arabia, including yesterdayâs attack on Aramco headquarters.





We condemn all such attacks on civilian infrastructure and call for them to cease immediately. They are totally unacceptable. We stand in solidarity with the people and government of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty and hope for a return to peace and normalcy in the region," he said.

Flights disrupted, embassy issues advisories

The attacks have also disrupted flight schedules, affecting Indian carriers and passengers travelling to and from Saudi Arabia.

"Flight schedules have been disrupted following attacks on airports, impacting Indian carriers, particularly flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam, Medina and Jeddah," Jaiswal said.

The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia is in regular contact with the Indian community. It has issued advisories and is providing updated information to travellers and passengers stranded by the disruptions.

The embassy is providing updated information to travellers and those stranded," Jaiswal said.

The latest developments come amid a series of attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, including airports and oil infrastructure. Yemen's Houthi rebels sent out missles and drones striking Saudi locations and emergency facilities.

The attacks have raised concerns over the security of critical infrastructure and the impact on civilian travel. India has urged an immediate halt to attacks on civilian facilities while its embassy continues to assist affected Indian nationals.

World.title: 'Your Didi is with you - today and forever!' Mamata Banerjee to detained CJP activists
World.content:
NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister

has rallied behind the arrested Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders, accusing the BJP-led Centre of trying to suppress democratic rights and silence young people.

In a message posted on X on Wednesday, Banerjee condemned the arrests of Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, who were sent to judicial custody, and assured young people of her support. âYour Didi is with you - today and forever!â she wrote.

The arrests came amid opposition protests in Delhi over alleged electoral irregularities and demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Why the CJP leaders were arrested

Delhi Police detained CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Ajinkya Shinde on Tuesday.

They were accused of allegedly entering the Jantar Mantar area without authorisation and violating peace bonds signed earlier by Ranka and Das.

The area was recently denotified as a designated venue for demonstrations. Police alleged that the three leaders breached barricades, entered the restricted area, raised slogans demanding Kumar's resignation and displayed the National Flag.

Shinde was granted bail, while Das and Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody after being produced before an executive magistrate on Wednesday morning.





They were subsequently lodged in Tihar Jail.

Mamata calls arrests an attempt to silence youth

Condemning the police action, Banerjee said the fight for democratic rights had continued across generations and called on people to stand together to protect them.

âWe, and many generations before us, have fought strongly for our democratic rights. We must continue to do so. I strongly condemn the arrest of Ashutosh and Saurav of the CJP. These moments are about us all, pledging and standing up to fight unitedly to protect our great democracy,â she wrote on X.

Banerjee described the arrests as an âattempt to intimidate and silence an entire generationâ and said people must not give up their constitutional rights.

âThis is unacceptable. We must never surrender our constitutional rights. This murdering of democracy is happening in many parts of the country. At this moment, 14,000 of our people in Bengal are facing the brunt of police and political atrocities,â she claimed.

The Trinamool Congress leader had also joined opposition protests in Delhi demanding Kumar's resignation. She backed the agitation initiated by the CJP and supported by the INDIA bloc, which has raised allegations of âvote choriâ (vote theft) and electoral roll manipulation linked to the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

âA government that has forgotten that 'it is of the people, by the people, for the people' is nearing its end.

To the millions of young people I say: Your Didi is with you - today and forever! Let us stand together and save our Mother India. Jai Hind! Vande Mataram! Joy Bangla!â Banerjee wrote.

Opposition leaders join criticism of Delhi Police

Abhishek Banerjee, the Diamond Harbour MP from the Mamata-led TMC faction, also criticised the arrests, accusing the BJP of targeting people for displaying the national flag.

âThe so-called biggest nationalists are now arresting Indians for unfurling and waving the Tricolour in their own country, an act which, according to the Union Government, constitutes a breach of peace.

Welcome to the @ BJP4India's new Pakistanified Bharat,â he wrote on X.

Other leaders from the faction, including Derek O'Brien and Mahua Moitra, also criticised the police action.

Several opposition figures have voiced concern over the arrests, including Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, former Tamil Nadu chief minister and DMK leader MK Stalin, AAP leader and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal, CPI general secretary D Raja, NCP MP Supriya Sule and Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Aditya Thackeray.

World.title: Siddaramaiah video row: CCB detains two for questioning
World.content:
The Central Crime Branch (CCB) cybercrime police have detained two persons for questioning in connection with allegedly defamatory videos targeting former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah that were circulated on social media.

The two suspects were picked up as part of the investigation into the alleged creation and circulation of the videos and are being questioned to ascertain their source.

Mr. Siddaramaiah had lodged a complaint with Bengaluru City Police Commissioner Seemanth Kumar Singh, alleging that fake and malicious videos were being circulated on social media to tarnish his reputation. He had also submitted details, including the IDs of social media accounts allegedly involved in spreading the content.

The Police Commissioner referred the complaint to the CCB Cyber Crime Police Station, where a case was registered. Investigators are now attempting to identify those who created the videos, trace the accounts that circulated them, and ascertain whether others were involved in a coordinated effort.

The police are examining the digital trail, including the IP addresses linked to prominent social media accounts that shared the videos, to identify those operating them and determine the origin of the content.

On Tuesday, Mr. Siddaramaiah secured an injunction restraining media organisations, including social media platforms, from circulating the allegedly defamatory videos. He had also sought police action against those responsible for what he described as false propaganda.

Govt. targeting JD(S) members: HDK

Meanwhile, Union Minister and JD (S) State President H.D. Kumaraswamy alleged that those detained by police were JD(S) social media team members. “Shankar, who works with our social media team, was taken away by the police today without any case being registered against him. I have also received reports that another team member, Mohan, and his family are being harassed. Why are these young people being targeted, and under what authority?”, he wondered in a social media post. “The person alleged to have carried out the sting operation and recorded footage intended to malign former CM Siddaramaiah has not faced the same scrutiny, while those questioning the episode are being pursued. This raises serious questions about the government’s priorities,” he said.

“I will not be intimidated for questioning a suspected honey-trap conspiracy involving senior Congress leaders. Instead of answering serious questions, the government appears to be targeting the young members of our JD(S) social media team,” he remarked.

World.title: History-sheeter ends life in hospital
World.content:
A remand prisoner ended his life even as he was undergoing treatment in Tirunelveli Medical College Hospital on Wednesday.

Police said Sankaralingam, 28, of Munneerpallam near Palayamkottai, who was facing more than 20 criminal cases, including murder and attempt-to-murder cases, had been lodged in Palayamkottai Central Prison after being arrested for allegedly in possession of ganja.

Since he had suffered injuries in the leg when he was arrested, Sankaralingam, who had been categorised by the police as ‘A+ history-sheeter’, was admitted to the Tirunelveli Medical College Hospital for treatment. When he went to the toilet on Wednesday afternoon, he ended his life.

World.title: Supreme Court makes protection from arrest ‘absolute’ for journalist who reported on Ayodhya Temple theft allegations
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) made absolute the interim protection granted to independent journalist Abhishek Upadhyay from coercive action in a road rage case, as well as any subsequent First Information Reports.

Mr. Upadhyay had authored investigative online stories of the alleged misappropriation and theft of donations at the Ayodhya Ram Temple.

A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi also quashed an Uttar Pradesh Police notice issued to social media platform X to provide Mr. Upadhyay’s digital data, generated around three months prior to the road rage incident.

The court found the police version that the data was sought to trace/arrest the petitioner “somewhat in contradiction” with the contents of its notice to the platform.

The court termed the notice an “overkill”, and said any information received by the police pursuant to the notice would not be used against the journalist.

The “arrest of the petitioner (Mr. Upadhyay) shall remain stayed till further notice,” the court said. It made absolute its interim orders of August 25 and September 7, which had protected him from arrest and directed him to cooperate with the investigation, respectively.

The copy of the road rage FIR had been supplied to the petitioner, the court noted.

The Bench ordered that Mr. Upadhyay could challenge the road rage FIR on any grounds. The apex court has not commented on the merits of the case.

The court allowed Mr. Upadhyay, who said the road rage case was “staged”, to counter his online reports about the temple, and the liberty to file a separate petition seeking guidelines to protect digital privacy and journalistic freedoms.

The apex court further directed the police to release the journalist’s vehicle in the next two days.

World.title: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra condole the death of Cheruvayal Raman
World.content:
Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have condoled the death of Cheruvayal Raman, renowned conservationist of traditional paddy seeds, who passed away at the age of 74 on Wednesday (October 14, 2026). He was undergoing treatment at Kozhikode Medical College Hospital for age-related ailments.

In a Facebook post, Mr. Gandhi, also a former Wayanad MP, said on Wednesday, “Deeply saddened by the passing of Padma Shri Cheruvayal Raman, our beloved Ramettan. He devoted his life to preserving Wayanad’s indigenous paddy seeds, keeping generations of Adivasi knowledge alive. I join the people of Wayanad in mourning him. My heartfelt condolences to his family and all who loved him.”

In a post on X, Ms. Vadra said Mr. Raman had touched her heart by calling her his daughter whey they first met. “From then on, I teased him and called him my Malayali Achan. When we last spoke to each other a month back, he wanted me to go and meet him. I promised that I would, but I had to cut short my trip to Wayanad because of events in Delhi so I missed meeting him thinking that I would return soon. When I heard about his passing today, my heart sank,” she said.

“My Malayali Achan was wise, dignified, and bold in thought and action. He wanted more for his people, he refused to accept less. His mind could not tolerate discrimination and injustice. He showed me his awards and honours with sadness in his eyes - he said they would mean nothing to him until his people could live better lives. He was a genius in his knowledge of paddy and agriculture and he understood the great value of his own culture and tradition. He was proud of his heritage and lived it with every breath. I will miss my wise friend and keep his teachings in my heart for always. India has lost a noble son,” Ms. Vadra’s post said.

World.title: Pro-tem Speaker administers oath to newly-elected MLA in Puducherry
World.content:
More than five months after the National Democratic Alliance government headed by Chief Minister and AINRC founder N. Rangasamy came to power in Puducherry, the Speaker’s post remains vacant leading to a situation where the Pro-tem Speaker, a temporary arrangement made during government formation for administering oath to newly-elected legislators, continued to officiate legislative procedures in the Union Territory.

The delay in conducting the Speaker election was because of the claims made by both the All India NR Congress (AINRC) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) for the post within the NDA fold. After Mr. Rangasamy was sworn-in along with two other Ministers on May 13, Lieutenant Governor K. Kailashnathan had appointed AIADMK MLA A. Anbalagan as Pro-tem Speaker for administering the oath of office to the newly-elected legislators.

However, in the absence of election to the Speaker’s post, he chaired the entire Budget session of the Legislative Assembly held in August. Again on Wednesday, he administered the oath of office to the newly-elected AINRC MLA Ashok Anand following his election from Thattanchavady Assembly constituency in the recent bypoll held after Mr. Rangasamy vacated the seat by retaining the second seat of Mangalam he won in the April polls.

Political parties and social organisations have been critical of the AINRC-BJP government for the delay in fulfilling the Constitutional requirement. Article 178 of the Constitution explicitly mandates the appointment of a Speaker to the Legislative Assembly.

“Every Legislative Assembly of a State shall, as soon as may be, choose two members of the Assembly to be respectively Speaker and Deputy Speaker thereof and, so often as the office of Speaker or Deputy Speaker becomes vacant, the Assembly shall choose another member to be Speaker or Deputy Speaker, as the case may be,” the article states.

The chapter-III of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of the Business of the Puducherry Legislative Assembly also prescribes election of Speaker and Deputy Speaker. The rules clearly put the onus on the government for the appointment of a Speaker and Deputy Speaker for the conduct of the Assembly proceedings.

Legal experts argue that though the Constitution has not prescribed any timeline for appointing the Speaker, the term “as soon as may be” mentioned in the Article 178 does not mean an endless wait for fulfilling a legally binding requirement on the part of an elected government.

“The Supreme Court in a different context has held that the words as soon as possible have significant constitutional content which is a constitutional imperative of expedition. Just because the Constitution has not set a deadline, it does not mean that the appointment could be made any time during the tenure of a government. The onus is on the elected government to fill the post at the earliest,” the expert told The Hindu.

Former Member of Parliament and president of Puducherry Maanila Makkal Munntera Kazhagam M. Ramadass said the people of Puducherry deserve a government and a legislature that function according to the law, constitutional principles and established parliamentary conventions.

The appointment of Pro-tem Speaker is a temporary arrangement made at the commencement of a new Assembly. The arrangement cannot be treated as an indefinite substitute for the statutory offices of Speaker and Deputy Speaker, the economist-turned-politician said.

AINRC-BJP tussle

Though the ruling AINRC and BJP have not openly spelt out the exact reason for the delay in electing a Speaker, sources within the parties confirm that the leadership of both the parties are not ready to budge after making a claim for the post.

While BJP leaders say, there was a pre-poll agreement to allocate the Speaker’s post and two Ministers for the BJP in the coalition government, the AINRC leadership said the election results were highly in favour for them because of the better performance of the party in the alliance.

“During the first NDA government, the Speaker post and two Minister posts were given because the seat difference between both the parties was only around four. In the present Assembly, we have more than double the number of their seats and hence the previous tenure’s formula cannot be adopted. We are hopeful of finding a solution to the stalemate at the earliest,” said an AINRC leader.

World.title: Israeli PM Netanyahu says he is not seeking to attack Iran again before Israel election
World.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ​said on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) that he was not in favour of a preemptive strike ‌against Iran before Israel’s October 27 election but also warned ​Tehran and its proxies against striking Israel.

“It is not ⁠convenient for us, it’s no good,” Mr. Netanyahu said in an interview on Israel’s Army Radio, when asked about the possibility of a preemptive strike and allegations by ‌his political rivals that he was seeking a military confrontation ahead of the election.

“Even if Iran fires missiles at us ‌they will blame me,” Mr. Netanyahu said, though he also repeated ‌his ⁠previous warnings to Iran, saying Israel would respond forcefully if ⁠attacked.

He would not elaborate on the possibility of a preemptive strike after the election or about his recent discussions with Washington about Iran.

The United States and Iran have ​been at war since February 28 ‌when the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran and Tehran responded with its own strikes on Israel and Gulf states.

Israel and Iran have not traded fire since June.

“Asked whether Israel was assisting ‌Saudi Arabia against attacks by the Iran-aligned Yemeni Houthis,” Mr. Netanyahu said: “I ​don’t get into those matters. I can only tell you that many countries in the Middle East are ⁠turning to us following our massive success and tremendous achievements.”

Saudi Arabia has faced widening Houthi strikes over the past week, including an attack on ‌Riyadh airport on Saturday (October 12) that killed 13 people.

Mr. Netanyahu said that Iran’s proxies were also looking to launch attacks on Israel before the election.

Defence Minister Israel Katz, speaking from the self-declared security zone Israeli forces are occupying in southern Lebanon, warned Iran-backed Lebanese group Hezbollah against attacking Israel.

“Hezbollah will suffer a severe blow and lose additional territories in southern Lebanon ‌within the Nabatieh and Litani regions, which will become part of Israel’s permanent ​security zone. The IDF (Israel Defence Forces) is prepared to carry out the manoeuvre,” Mr. Katz said.

Mr. Katz said that a million Shi’ites ⁠would be displaced and that Hezbollah’s stronghold in Beirut would not be spared.

Israel ⁠launched air strikes and a ground invasion in southern Lebanon this year in parallel with the war in Iran, after ‌Hezbollah fired into Israel in revenge for the attacks against Tehran.

Hundreds of thousands of people from Lebanon’s Shi’ite Muslim community, from which ​Hezbollah draws its support, were uprooted by the fighting.

World.title: Plea to provide free battery operated vehicle services at Madurai and Tiruchi Railway Junctions
World.content:
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Wednesday directed the Central government and the Southern Railway to file a report to a public interest litigation petition that sought a direction to the authorities to provide battery operated vehicle services at Madurai and Tiruchi railway junctions free of cost.

A Division Bench of Justices P. Velmurugan and K.K. Ramakrishnan was hearing the petition filed by Swamimalai Sundara Vimalanathan of Kumbakonam in Thanjavur district.

The petitioner said battery operated vehicles were provided at railway stations as a mobility-assistance facility for senior citizens, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, and other needy passengers.

Battery operated vehicle services were introduced in Tiruchi railway junction in 2017 and were initially provided free of cost. However, from 2018 onwards the service was converted into a paid facility and ₹30 was collected per passenger for the service, he said.

Battery-operated vehicles at Tiruchi railway junction were procured through the Corporate Social Responsibility contributions and government welfare schemes. Charging the beneficiaries defeats the purpose of such welfare funding, he said.

He said in Madurai railway junction the services were initially provided free of cost before a nominal charge was introduced. As per the consolidated accessibility data, out of the 252 railway stations under Madurai and Tiruchi divisions, battery operated vehicle services were available only in 11 stations. The data provides widespread non-availability of battery operated services for passengers requiring assistance, he said.

He sought a direction to the authorities to provide the battery operated vehicle services at Madurai and Tiruchi railway junctions free of cost. The court posted the matter for hearing to November 10.

World.title: No consensus yet on seat-sharing between NDA partners in local body elections
World.content:
The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) partners were yet to reach a consensus on seat-sharing for the local body elections, even as the notification was issued on Wednesday.

The Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and the Jana Sena Party (JSP) remained firm on their respective positions on the number of seats and posts to be contested.

It would take another “two days” to sort out the issue, though the parties announced that they would fight the elections as NDA.

Mayor posts have emerged as a major stumbling block in the negotiations. The posts in prominent municipal corporations, including Visakhapatnam, Tirupati, Anantapur, Nellore and Vijayawada, are reportedly drawing the attention of the JSP and BJP, both of which are keen on securing a larger share of civic bodies and key positions under the alliance arrangement.

The BJP is seeking three Mayor posts. But TDP national president and Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has offered it one Mayor post and five municipal chairman posts, leading to a stalemate between the TDP and BJP.

Sources said that Mr. Naidu also turned down the BJP’s request for Nellore, citing its Muslim-dominated population and the party’s limited chances of winning there.

The TDP and JSP leaders held a meeting on Wednesday, but no tangible outcome was announced. The BJP leaders, too, gave no positive indication of a breakthrough following their meeting with Mr. Naidu.

“The seat-sharing arrangement will be finalised at another meeting, following which the alliance will announce its list of candidates,” said JSP MLA Bolisetti Srinivas, sharing details of the meeting.

The TDP and the JSP had reached a consensus to contest together during their discussions, he said, adding that care would be taken to ensure that the sentiments of both parties were not hurt in the seat-sharing process. Decisions on which party should contest particular seats would be based on local political conditions.

The alliance was yet to finalise the number of seats each party would contest. Details of the seats to be contested would be announced within two days, Mr. Srinivas said.

World.title: National Assembly, Senate pass resolutions endorsing Centre's imposition of emergency in KP
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Shortly after the National Assembly passed a resolution endorsing the federal government’s imposition of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Wednesday, the Senate also gave its approval for the measure.

The Centre had imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Sunday, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.

Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry tabled the motions regarding the proclamation of emergency before both Houses.

Senate proceedings

In the Senate, the resolution was passed amid the opposition’s outcry, with PTI senators staging a walkout.

The Senate’s approval followed a heated debate between treasury and opposition members, during which Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar defended the procedural propriety presenting the resolution in the House and getting it approved.

He argued that a “constitutional resolution” had been laid before the House in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Senate. “Under Article 232, a copy of [the proclamation of] emergency has been laid before the House. An attempt to bypass the constitutional procedure cannot succeed,” he said, adding that the requirement of a seven-day notice for tabling a resolution did not apply to one presented under a constitutional necessity.

“If its opponents have any objections, they should reject the resolution through their vote after the debate. We cannot deviate from the Constitution and rules of the House,” he said.

As opposition voiced opposition to the resolution, Senate Chairperson Yousuf Raza Gilani asked them to exercise patience. “This is not a classroom, do not make noise,” he remarked as senators from the opposition benches continued sloganeering.

Among them, PTI’s Humayun Mohmand said independent Senator Faisal Vawda had said months ago that governor’s rule would be imposed. He alleged that terrorism being cited as the reason for the measure was just an excuse and the actual “target is the PTI”.

“The decision to impose governor’s rule and emergency was taken months ago,” he alleged. Seemingly referring to the creation of Bangladesh, he said the federal government’s decision since 1970 had proved wrong.

PTI-backed Senator Hamid Khan also argued that there “seems to be some other objectives behind governor’s rule and emergency”. Referring to the talks between the Centre and the opposition ahead of governor’s rule and emergency in KP, he alleged that negotiations “were just a drama” and were held “only to deceive the people”.

“The real decision was taken elsewhere long ago,” he claimed. He further said that Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, who tried to mediate between the Centre and the opposition, had stated that while the negotiations were taking place, “a decision came”.

“Governments formed on the basis of Form-47 do not have the real mandate,” he added.

He further regretted that after the 26th Amendment, “there is neither any Constitution nor an independent judicial system”.

“The judiciary has been stripped of its independence, which closes the avenues to challenge unconstitutional steps,” he said.

Khan went on to say: “Article 232 has to be presented before the House for debate, not just for saying yes. Decision was taken by those whom Constitution does not allow to take the decision, but they have complete dominance over Constitution. At this time, neither is there any Constitution nor any court in the country.”

PTI Senator Mohsin Aziz railed against federal ministers, who have been accusing the PTI of facilitating terrorism.

“You talk about terrorism, what do you know about terrorism? People of KP sacrificed their children and picked up bodies. […] Did we support Pakistan or terrorists? Those calling people of KP terrorists should be ashamed. These are valiant people who saved this country,” he said.

Aziz said terrorism was a result of unemployment, hunger, non-availability of hospitals, water and education.

Senator Zeeshan Khanzada, also from the PTI, said he condemned the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP. He accused the federal government of “abducting” Sohail Afridi, who has been rendered non-functional as the KP chief minister following the imposition of governor’s rule, and other PTI MPAs.

JUI-F’s Kamran Murtaza said the opposition’s resolution against governor’s rule should have also been included in the agenda for the day, but it was returned with objections.

Murtaza argued that the relevant material required for endorsement of enforcement of Article 232 and 234 — constitutional provision related to imposition of emergency and governor’s rule — had not been presented in the House.

Despite letters and applications, the government had not provided documents and material related to the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule, he said, adding that senators had to obtain that material through social media.

Members could not be satisfied with a decision until complete information came forth, he said.

NA proceedings

The NA question hour session was suspended due to discussions on the emergency. The motion in the lower House of Parliament was adopted with a majority vote after a discussion opened by Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar.

“The National Assembly approves the Proclamation of Emergency issued by the President on the 11th October, 2026 in the Province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under second proviso of clause (1) of Article 232 of the Constitution,” read a post by NA’s official X account.

According to Article 232, if the “president acts on his own, the Proclamation of Emergency shall be placed” before both Houses of the Parliament for approval by each House within 10 days.

Meanwhile, a proclamation for governor’s rule issued under Article 234 “shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months”, unless a joint sitting approves its extension. However, such a measure shall not remain in force for more than six months.

Throughout Wednesday’s proceedings, opposition members participated calmly and did not stage any loud protest, unlike past instances when the PTI objects to the Centre.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also attended part of the session, with pictures released by the NA showing him shaking hands with Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif shakes hands with leader of the opposition in the National Assembly, Mehmood Khan Achakzai, on Wednesday. — Photo courtesy NA Facebook

Federal ministers defended the emergency imposition while assailing what they described as the PTI-led KP government’s lack of will to combat terrorism.

In tune with that, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari blamed the PTI for the circumstances that compelled the Centre to impose emergency in KP and termed it a “political suicide attack” for the party.

However, he also urged the treasury and the opposition to get back on the path of dialogue and make joint efforts against terrorism.

At one point during the proceedings, NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq noted that the Oct 3 dialogue was held in a cordial atmosphere.

Sadiq praised both sides for “attempting more than their capacity so that the matter is settled”.

However, he said some matters were beyond the parties’ control and voiced his support for forming the same committees for negotiations if ever needed in the future.

Addressing PTI lawmakers, the speaker said, “Everyone’s response was that this [process of dialogue] should continue, but you also understand that your hands were tied.”

He took note of the PTI’s complaints regarding the jail conditions of party founder Imran Khan, adding that he had even provided details of facilities provided to the jailed ex-premier.

The session was adjourned to meet again at 11am on Oct 16 (Friday).

‘Political suicide attack’

Bilawal began his speech by highlighting that emergency and governor’s rule in KP were measures taken under the Constitution. Reading the relevant provisions, he asserted that the Centre tried its best to “engage the opposition so this step did not have to be taken”.

“They will have to accept, even if not publicly, but the responsible leadership of the opposition knows that the PTI itself carried out a political suicide attack on its KP government,” he remarked.

The PPP chief maintained that the PTI could not deny that its “leadership, particularly in the province had a key role in the political, constitutional and legal circumstances” at present.

Bilawal emphasised that the PPP’s stance was that “before employing this constitutional atomic bomb, we must engage with PTI and the opposition and try to address the federal government’s reservations that they were not supporting them in the war against terrorism”.

He observed: “If political space is restricted for one political party, it is impossible that it remains restricted for that particular party; it is limited for every political party, political worker and Pakistani citizen.

“We are responsible for this, but you cannot deny that you are also responsible for it,” he said.

Terming the imposition of emergency a “difficult decision”, Bilawal recalled alleged remarks by Sohail Afridi — the KP chief minister whose role is now non-functional — that he would not combat terrorism the way the Centre wanted.

“If this was not a political suicide, then what else was it?”

The Bhutto scion wondered if the opposition and Afridi had left any reason for President Asif Ali Zardari, who he said prides himself on passing the 18th Amendment, to “refuse to sign” the emergency proclamation.

He argued that due to the PTI’s actions and statements, neither the president, the Centre, nor he had any legal or political reason left for not imposing emergency in KP.

“But even today, I would recommend to the federal government that we extend our hand forward once again for negotiations, political discussions and try to find a resolution and a middle path,” Bilawal added.

The PPP chairman noted that emergency was “always a stopgap measure”.

“We cannot sustain the emergency forever,” he added, emphasising that while the counterterrorism fight would be better than before, an “all-of-society and all-of-country response” was needed to eradicate it completely.

Regarding the Oct 3 talks of a joint delegation of the PPP and the government with the opposition, Bilawal said, “Late at night, I was informed that congratulations, negotiations are succeeding.”

He said the PTI was willing to declare the areas in KP with surging terrorism as “terrorist areas”, and the opposition was about to agree that the federal and KP governments would sign a pact on joint efforts against terrorism. However, the dialogue collapsed.

The former foreign minister pointed out that the security challenges Pakistan was facing were “way more complicated” than before, adding that India “could still not digest […] its embarrassment” from the May 2025 conflict.

Referring to remarks by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi that its ‘Operation Sindoor’ was still ongoing, Bilawal said: “It means that India is still sponsoring terrorist incidents in Pakistan, sometimes in the form of TTP (Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan) and sometimes in the form of separatist terrorist groups.”

He reiterated Pakistan’s stance that India was involved in terrorist activities being conducted from across the Afghan border.

The ex-foreign minister then highlighted Islamabad’s role as a mediator in the US-Iran war.

“But there is a state — which we do not recognise as a state — that will neither be happy nor ever forget that you took this step. And those Zionist forces will and are interfering in Pakistan’s internal politics and state.”

Concluding his speech, the PPP chairman emphasised the need for building consensus on “some fundamental issues” for an empowered lower house.

“Even today, we are saying, come and at least begin from this house,” he said while addressing the opposition benches.

Gohar demands implementation of NAP

Speaking in the NA, PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan said his party “rejected” the Centre’s move to impose emergency in KP.

He asked what “terrorism” Imran’s wife or sisters had allegedly been involved in that they had been put behind bars, or what the accusations were against the PTI MNAs and MPAs who he said were detained.

Gohar further said, “One person is not present in the house currently. When he comes during a joint session, then I will reveal the reality of the negotiations.”

He affirmed that the PTI had raised its voice against terrorism, adding that measures against the scourge must be taken according to the National Action Plan (NAP).

Gohar argued that the PML-N opposition during the PTI’s tenure carried out “14 long marches in two years, but you did not let us stage even one long march”.

Presenting his version of the Oct 3 talks with the government, the PTI leader said his party was being asked to immediately call off the long march. “I said where did [the topic] of terrorism arise from suddenly.”

Noting that the government had put forward “five reservations”, Gohar said PTI was willing to make the KP Police Act similar to that of Punjab and Sindh.

The PTI leader reiterated his party’s request for the production of certain MNAs it says were taken into custody.

Gohar also welcomed Bilawal’s proposal to continue dialogue.

Responding to Gohar’s remarks, the PPP chairman said the PTI was busy in its long march while the people of KP were being targeted by terrorists.

Bilawal reiterated that the opposition could keep arguing against the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, but no one could deny that the decision was grounded in the Constitution.

“I cannot insist on the government to continue talks with PTI despite being defrauded multiple times,” the PPP chairman said.

Pointing towards Gohar and Achakzai, Bilawal said: “I believe that none of them is allied with terrorists. I believe that they will definitely want to combat terrorism; however, they cannot deny the fact that their former chief minister contradicted this fact.”

Bilawal again requested all the stakeholders to unite and combat terrorism collectively. He also called for the provision of all facilities to the incarcerated PTI founder.

‘Threat to national security’

Addressing the house, the law minister explained that emergency was imposed in KP as the security situation there was becoming a threat to “national security”.

Tarar noted that after the Proclamation of Emergency was issued, the Constitution’s Article 232 required that both houses of the parliament approve the measure.

He recalled that the federal cabinet examined “material” regarding terrorism in the province during its Oct 11 meeting and then advised PM Shehbaz to recommend the imposition of emergency.

He noted that some people compared the measure to the emergency imposed by former dictator Gen Pervez Musharraf on Oct 12, 1999.

The minister particularly noted “internal disturbances” and cross-border infiltrations. He contended that the situation since Oct 15, 2025, when Sohail Afridi’s government came into power in KP, was “turning into a threat to national security to an alarming extent”.

He went on to highlight that there was a rise in terrorism in KP, especially after 2021, due to the approach of the provincial government.

“Perhaps there might be foreign, diplomatic and political reasons behind it, which got inflamed due to a political party’s point of view.”

Tarar stated that 2,911 incidents of terrorism took place between 2021 and 2024 in KP, but they surged to 3,787 incidents between Oct 15, 2025 and Oct 9, 2026.

He criticised the KP chief minister for ignoring martyred security and police personnel, and for instead preferring to promote his political designs and make visits across the country.

“Even this was announced that the federal capital will be conquered,” he said, referring to the party’s plan to hold a protest long march towards the federal capital.

The PML-N leader expressed his government’s gratitude to NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq for providing a platform for dialogue between the Centre and the opposition. He reiterated the government’s stance that the PTI had the agreement draft changed multiple times, but even then backed off from it.

Tarar observed that the PTI demanded the release of their party founder Imran Khan and his treatment in a private hospital despite knowing that only courts could provide such a relief.

He said two days would be “remembered in the country’s democratic history with regard to misfortune and a political party”.

On the emergency measure, the law minister noted that a special mechanism has been introduced for 12 districts of KP.

Speaking after Tarar, Achakzai criticised him for trying to prove that terrorism was not tackled in KP.

The opposition leader questioned the government’s mandate in the February 2024 general elections, quipping that the opposition would “surrender” if the minister could swear that the government won those polls fairly.

Achakzai alleged that the incumbent ruling coalition was formed “illegally”.

‘You do not have clean hands’

Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif went on to recall the tenure of the PTI government in the Centre and assailed the party’s past actions.

Referring to ex-prime minister Imran Khan’s plan to resettle members of the TTP, he said PTI tried to convince the then-opposition that “bringing these terrorists back would be better for Pakistan”.

The PML-N leader mentioned the 2019 episode of an Indian pilot’s capture in Pakistan: “They had threatened and we were surrendering. The then-prime minister was saying, ‘What should I do? Attack India?’”

Asif urged the opposition to reflect on its past actions, adding that Imran often used to praise former army chief retired General Qamar Javed Bajwa.

“As long as this contradiction remains in our words and actions and in our society, the circumstances of this country will not fix.”

He narrated his time behind bars during the PTI government, when Shehbaz “smuggled a blanket” to him to brace the low temperatures. “I used to eat the jail’s food,” he said, claiming that orders were given to remove the geyser when it was installed.

“But we did not hold rallies or mourn at D-Chowk or dig graves. We did not martyr police and law enforcement personnel,” Asif remarked.

“You demand equity when you have clean hands. You do not have clean hands, you cannot demand equity; this is a thousand-year-old principle,” he contended.

“You know very well what Gen Musharraf did to me. There was a 4x6 cell in Attock jail,” the PML-N politician said, emphasising that he stood with his party and ex-PM Nawaz Sharif.

Speaking on the current political situation, Asif alleged that Afridi used to “take directives […] from a person sitting in Afghanistan”.

He referred to a statement by the TTP condemning the imposition of emergency and deployment of troops in certain places. “Who is their ally and who is their rival?” he said.

The minister further countered the PTI’s stance that its leaders have not been able to meet Imran, who is imprisoned in the Adiala jail. “Meetings are held, [but] a lot of them are not publicised or brought on record,” he maintained.

Farooq Sattar urges PTI to ‘openly condemn terrorism’

In his remarks on the floor of the lower house, Farooq Sattar expressed Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan’s (MQM-P) confidence in the decision taken by the prime minister.

“This was an extremely difficult decision, but so unavoidable that you had no other option,” Sattar said about imposing emergency and governor’s rule.

“We trust your decision as we trust your experience, capabilities, political acumen, and that you made this decision in the interest of the nation,” he added.

The MQM-P lawmaker contended that the PTI was “on the wrong side and does not have concrete arguments” to declare that the decision was baseless or made with political motives.

“The main issue is of the mindset,” he declared, adding that Imran had “publicly said that the war on terror is not ours”. “This is their policy. This is their mindset.”

Sattar questioned whether the KP government had ever published reports to expose terrorist hideouts and extremist trends. He further raised questions about the government’s pursuit of cases against suspected terrorists.

“Openly condemn terrorism; else, the allegation of backing [it], if a commission is formed and God forbid, it is proven in the inquiry that there is political extremism and terrorism complicity, there is a nexus, then where will you go?”

Sattar recounted his past MQM experiences, saying, “I have also suffered such times. A lot of times, the narrative coming from the top was difficult to defend. Today, I feel that Barrister Gohar is also not in the position to defend his [party’s] position on KP.”

World.title: PTI Chairman Gohar moves PHC against emergency, governor's rule in KP
World.content:
PESHAWAR: PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Wednesday moved the Peshawar High Court (PHC) against the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, requesting the court to declare the move unconstitutional.

The emergency, declared on Sunday, follows heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the PTI-led KP government. The Centre and opposition have been at odds over various issues, particularly the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons cited by both parties behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks .

Governor Faisal Karim Kundi has assumed the role of running the province on behalf of the Centre, with an 11-member technocratic KP Advisory Council formed to assist him. The federal government has also authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in KP.

Advocate Shah Faisal Ilyas submitted the petition challenging the emergency proclamation on behalf of the PTI chairman. A copy is available with Dawn.

The petitioner requested the PHC to declare the Oct 11 emergency proclamation as “unconstitutional, ultra vires, coram non judice, tainted with malice in law and fact, devoid of objective material, and of no legal effect”; and urged it to set the proclamation aside.

Barrister Gohar is represented by a panel of lawyers, including Barrister Sameer Khosa, Salman Akram Raja, Ali Zaman, Sardar Haseeb Ahmad and Zainab Shahid.

Filed under Article 199 (jurisdiction of high court) of the Constitution of Pakistan, the petition named the Federation of Pakistan (through the secretaries of the Cabinet, law ministry, interior ministry and defence ministry); the province of KP; KP Governor Kundi; the KP Assembly speaker; and the secretary of the KP Home and Tribal Affairs Department as respondents.

Sohail Afridi, the now non-functional chief minister of the province following the imposition of governor’s rule, was also named as a pro forma respondent.

Gohar challenged the “constitutionality, legality and vires” of the Oct 11 Proclamation of Emergency in the province, the order deploying army troops to the province, and “all consequential and derivative executive orders, notifications, and bodies” constituted as a result, including the establishment of the KP Advisory Council and the “arbitrary” detention and unseating of Afridi as the chief minister.

Afridi and some of his cabinet members were taken into preventive custody shortly after the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule, as confirmed by officials on Monday.

The petitioner sought further declaration from the PHC that Paragraph (3) of the proclamation, which purported to direct that the KP CM and ministers cease to hold office, was “illegal, ultra vires the Constitution, and in violation of the fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 4, 9, 17(2), 25 and 130”.

He requested that the court order the immediate constitutional restoration of Afridi as the lawful chief minister of KP, along with his provincial cabinet, with full executive powers vested under Article 130 (the cabinet) of the Constitution.

The PHC was further requested to declare that Paragraph (2) of the proclamation — transferring the legislative powers of the KP Assembly to Parliament in the absence of a prior resolution passed by the assembly as required under Article 232(1) — was “void ab initio and an unconstitutional usurpation of provincial autonomy”.

The plea also urged PHC to restrain the federation from “tabling, entertaining, or enacting any provincial legislative business concerning Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in Parliament”.

The petitioner requested the court to declare as illegal and unconstitutional and to set aside, dissolve or permanently restrain all executive orders, notifications, actions, and bodies created “pursuant to or under the colour of” the proclamation.

These included the constitution of the 11-member KP Advisory Council headed by Governor Kundi; the establishment of the “Area Development Secretariat” (ADS) across 12 districts of the province; and the unseating of the advocate general of KP and purported appointment of any replacement officer.

The petitioner also challenged the Oct 11 order of army deployment under Article 245, requesting the court to declare it as unconstitutional on the basis that it could not “supplant or bypass the civilian executive and constitutional administration” of the province, and could not be invoked in the absence of a lawful requisition by the provincial government headed by Afridi.

Barrister Gohar sought directives for respondents, including the federal government and KP governor, to immediately disclose, produce, and place before the PHC “the entire record and so-called ‘objective material’”, including Governor Kundi’s report and the summary of the federal cabinet, upon which the emergency proclamation and subsequent orders were alleged to be founded.

He also sought directives for the immediate release of Afridi and members of the KP cabinet and assembly from “unlawful executive or preventive detention”.

Additionally, the petition requested the court to permanently restrain the respondents from “obstructing, barricading, or creating physical impediments” to the lawful functioning of the CM’s Secretariat, Civil Secretariat and KP Assembly.

It further requested that the PHC suspend the operation and implementation of the notification establishing the ADS, and restrain its administrator and additional chief secretary from exercising parallel administrative or law enforcement powers in the designated 12 districts; and additionally restrain the federal government from “tabling, considering, or passing” any legislative measures or bills pertaining to the Provincial Legislative List or affairs of KP in Parliament.

The petition also urged the court to direct respondents to immediately produce Afridi before the PHC and restrain the state from placing him or any cabinet members under preventive detention, or transferring them out of the jurisdiction of the court.

It also asked the court to direct the local administration and authorities to immediately remove all containers, barricades and blockades from around the KP Assembly Secretariat and CM’s Secretariat and to ensure unimpeded access to all elected representatives. Finally, it also requested the granting of “any other relief, order or direction” that the court deemed proper in the circumstances of the case.

The PTI chairman stated as grounds for the petition that the issuance of such a proclamation was subject to the “indispensable condition precedent of a prior resolution passed by the provincial assembly of that province”.

“No such resolution was ever moved, debated, or passed by the provincial assembly of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” he contended. “In the absence of this mandatory constitutional prerequisite, the federal government had no constitutional competence to advise or issue the impugned proclamation under Article 232(1), rendering the entire exercise coram non judice.”

The petition claimed that by unilaterally bypassing the elected provincial assembly on an alleged question of internal disturbance, the impugned proclamation violated “the federal structure guaranteed under Article 1, the principles of democracy and provincial autonomy enshrined in the Objectives Resolution (Article 2A), and the legislative domain of the province recognised by Article 142 of the Constitution”.

On these grounds, the proclamation was “ultra vires the proviso to Article 232(1) read with Article 1, 2A, and 142 of the Constitution” and liable to be set aside, it added.

Gohar further contended that the proclamation made no mention of any “grave emergency” arising from a war or other external aggression, as required by the text of Article 232(1) — nor would such an assertion be supported by facts. He maintained that neither the country nor KP faced a grave emergency from any ongoing war or external aggression, nor was there any known risk or threat of such.

The petition further contended that the reliance on “internal disturbances” in the province needed to be measured against a demonstrable and objective criterion which was “entirely absent” from the impugned proclamation.

“Despite an unfortunately high number of incidents of terrorist violence in the Balochistan province, no declaration of emergency has been declared or even contemplated,” it highlighted.

“This clearly demonstrates that the terrorism and security pretext in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is nothing but a colourable device, deployed in sheer violation of Article 25.”

The petition alleged that this pretext was deployed solely because the KP government was formed by the opposition and their demands with respect to PTI founder Imran Khan were not acceptable to the federal government.

It added that the federal government’s claim was also belied by the fact that even at the peak of the phase of terrorism between 2007-2015, “no emergency was ever imposed anywhere inside Pakistan”.

He also argued that the invocation of Article 234 was “without lawful authority, tainted with malice in law, and devoid of jurisdictional basis”.

World.title: Houthis vow more attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities after claiming they targeted Aramco
World.content:
Yemen’s Houthi rebels said on Wednesday they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco, after Saudi officials reported a strike on a building in an area in Riyadh housing the energy giant’s operations centre.

Powerful explosions meanwhile rattled the Saudi capital, as the coalition fighting the Houthis said it had intercepted a missile fired by the group towards Riyadh.

Saudi Arabia, the world’s top crude oil exporter, has in recent days come under sustained attack in a dramatic escalation in the war with the Houthis.

It has hit back with strikes against the group’s stronghold in the Yemeni capital Sanaa, which for years has been under their grip.

Yahya Saree, Houthi military spokesman, said their forces had conducted “a high-quality military operation targeting Aramco in Dhahran” as well as strikes targeting Riyadh airport and a refinery in the capital.

“This was carried out using a large number of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones,” he said, adding that “operations toward Saudi depths will continue in the coming days, targeting Saudi enemy airports and oil facilities”.

Earlier, a Saudi energy ministry official said a building belonging to Aramco in Dhahran was struck, resulting in a “limited fire” but “no casualties or fatalities”.

Dhahran is home to Aramco’s headquarters, a vast complex comprising numerous buildings and residential compounds.

‘We heard an explosion’

More blasts were heard on Wednesday, AFP journalists in Riyadh reported, as messages were received on phones warning of an “aerial threat” and urging people to take shelter.

The alert was lifted a few minutes later.

Most strikes on Saudi Arabia have targeted infrastructure on the outskirts of the capital, but the barrages appear to be getting closer to the city centre.

In the city’s downtown, residents have been seen parking their cars to stop and look up at the sky, an AFP journalist said.

On Tuesday night, the white plumes of air defence missiles could be seen streaking across the sky followed by explosions.

While walking down a major avenue, a witness told AFP he “saw a projectile cutting across the sky” above a mall, saying it left “a yellowish trail of light followed by a trail of smoke. Then, we heard an explosion”.

“People were calm; no one was speaking. We were scared and all looking up at the sky,” he added, requesting anonymity.

Strikes on Yemen

The Saudi-led coalition meanwhile struck oil sites across western Yemen, with spokesman Turki Al-Malki claiming that the attacks targeted facilities used to supply the Houthis’ effort to “threaten the kingdom, Yemen, the southern Red Sea and waterways”.

An AFP correspondent in Sanaa reported an explosion, while a breaking news alert on the Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV channel said “Saudi aggression” targeted an oil firm.

The coalition has supported Yemen’s government militarily against the Houthis since 2015 in a long-running civil war that has created a humanitarian crisis.

Many civilians in the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital, fearing shortages, have rushed to queue in front of fuel stations, an AFP journalist said.

Renewed threats

The latest escalation follows a strike on Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday that left 13 people dead in the worst attack on the kingdom since 2015.

The Saudi cabinet vowed in a meeting led by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman that it “will not allow its security or freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab strait to be threatened”.

Many countries have issued travel warnings to their citizens in Saudi Arabia, with France telling its nationals on Tuesday to avoid Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam airports.

Traffic in perennially gridlocked Riyadh was noticeably lighter this week as remote learning for all schools and work-from-home orders for some companies took effect, according to AFP journalists.

Saudi Arabia faces a major economic contraction this year, with GDP expected to shrink 3.3 per cent, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday, predicting a regional drop over Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

The kingdom was already facing headwinds from Iran’s chokehold on Hormuz since the start of the Middle East war in February, when the United States and Israel attacked Iran.

But the restart in July of Yemen’s frozen war has further roiled the kingdom and brought the fight to its own soil.

Houthi attacks have also targeted oil tankers in the Red Sea — Saudi Arabia’s alternative export route.

World.title: Russian interior minister highlights potential for expanding economic cooperation in meeting with PM Shehbaz
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev highlighted the potential for expanding trade and economic cooperation with Pakistan in a meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

Kolokoltsev arrived in Pakistan on Monday on a four-day visit at the invitation of Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, marking the first instance of a Russian interior minister visiting Pakistan.

According to a statement issued by the PMO, in a meeting with the premier on Wednesday, Kolokoltsev highlighted the “significant potential for expanding bilateral trade and economic cooperation” between the two countries.

He conveyed Russia’s desire to further strengthen bilateral ties and expand cooperation in areas of shared interest, while expressing his country’s readiness to further enhance bilateral engagement with Pakistan, the statement said.

The Russian minister also appreciated Pakistan’s support at various multilateral forums, particularly the United Nations.

Meanwhile, PM Shehbaz reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further deepening its friendly relations with Russia and making “effective use of existing bilateral mechanisms to advance mutually beneficial cooperation”, the PMO said.

“He underscored the need to expand cooperation across areas of mutual interest, particularly trade and investment, energy, and economic development,” it added.

The premier expressed satisfaction over the positive momentum in Pakistan-Russia relations and stressed the importance of building on this momentum to further strengthen bilateral cooperation.

Russian minister meets CDF, discusses defence cooperation

Kolokoltsev also called on Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi on Wednesday, where both sides stressed the importance of bolstering defence cooperation between Islamabad and Moscow.

According to a statement from Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), both sides discussed matters of mutual interest and the regional security landscape, with emphasis on strengthening bilateral security cooperation.

“They underscored the importance of closer institutional linkages and improved coordination between the security institutions of Pakistan and Russia,” the statement said.

It added that CDF Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s resolve to “deepen its longstanding relations with Russia and expand tangible cooperation in areas of shared interest, particularly in the security domain”.

Kolokoltsev also expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s contributions to regional peace and stability, acknowledging the professionalism and sacrifices of Pakistani forces in the fight against terrorism, the statement concluded.

Pakistan, Russia agree to finalise extradition treaty

Earlier in the day, Pakistan and Russia agreed to finalise an extradition treaty and pledged to sign a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on cooperation in preventing organised crime and exchanging information.

The understanding was reached during a meeting between Naqvi and Kolokolstev in Islamabad. The meeting was followed by delegation-level talks, the interior ministry said in a statement.

According to the PMO, the signing of the MoU was witnessed by the prime minister.

Naqvi, during the meeting, said the proposed MoU on prevention of organised crime would be an important milestone in cooperation between the two countries.

The two sides pledged to enhance mutual cooperation in areas of shared interests as they agreed to finalise an extradition treaty and an agreement on the exchange of criminals.

Both sides resolved to promote cooperation in areas of mutual interest and decided to ensure early implementation of a readmission agreement, according to the statement.

They also agreed to enhance cooperation between the Anti-Narcotics Force and relevant Russian institutions.

It was agreed in the meeting that working groups from the interior ministries of both countries would soon visit each other.

The two sides also discussed sending skilled manpower from Pakistan to Russia and facilitating visa acquisition for tourists and the business community, as per the statement.

They agreed to enhance cooperation for the prevention of cybercrime between the National Police Academy and the Russian Police Academy, the statement said.

Naqvi said easing the visa regime would increase people-to-people contact between the two countries. He also expressed desire to benefit from Russia’s experiences in curbing cybercrime.

He further noted that at present, 1,300 Pakistani students were studying in Russia and Pakistan wanted more students to study there.

Russian Interior Minister Kolokolstev, for his part, said joint measures were essential for the prevention of all organised crime, including terrorism, drug smuggling, and illegal migration.

He said Russia had brought a 33 per cent reduction in cybercrime through effective measures.

The meeting was attended by Minister of State Tallal Chaudhry, the Russian ambassador in Pakistan, special and additional secretaries to interior and other senior officials.

In recent years, Pakistan and Russia have significantly strengthened their economic ties, driven by mutual necessity.

In January, Russian President Vladimir Putin had said Moscow’s relations with Pakistan were “ genuinely mutually beneficial ” and that it maintained close ties with Islamabad.

Last July, Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister Alexei Overchuk called Pakistan and Russia “ natural allies ”, stressing that Putin viewed Islamabad as an important strategic partner in the areas of economy and energy.

Following Western sanctions related to the Ukraine conflict, Moscow turned toward new energy outlets, while Islamabad simultaneously sought more affordable fuel sources to reduce national import expenses.

World.title: Aurangzeb discusses targeted fuel subsidies in meeting with senior IMF official
World.content:
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb met International Monetary Fund (IMF) Deputy Managing Director Nigel Clarke in Bangkok on Wednesday, with their discussion covering targeted fuel subsidies among other matters.

Aurangzeb “outlined targeted fuel subsidies to protect vulnerable groups and preserve social cohesion” during the meeting, a statement issued by the finance ministry said.

The government has already rolled out a fuel subsidy scheme for the users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to amid rising global oil prices. Days after its announcement on Sept 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed that motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi rickshaws up to 20 years old should also be included in the scheme.

Pakistan also remains engaged with the IMF for a $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and $1.4bn Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF). The two reached a staff-level agreement after a fourth review under the EFF and a third review under the RSF earlier this month, which qualified Pakistan to draw about $1.2bn from the Fund’s resources.

On Tuesday, the IMF called on countries to offer narrow, targeted subsidies in the wake of the energy crunch caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran.

The finance ministry statement said Aurangzeb and Clarke met on the sidelines of the World Bank Group-IMF Annual Meetings 2026 to discuss Pakistan’s economic progress and reform priorities.
